entries.text: Ah, she's got her troubles, but she's got a good head on her shoulders, too.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "She'll do right in whatever she set..."
entries.text: She'll do right in whatever she sets her mind to, I'm sure of that.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Saoirse

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Murphy?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Murphy?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Awww Declan. My poor heart."
entries.text: Awww Declan. My poor heart.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Our society is broken in so many wa..."
entries.text: Our society is broken in so many ways, and it has failed this young woman in all of them.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If I could do something for the poo..."
entries.text: If I could do something for the poor thing, I would.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I like her. Genuine and down to ear..."
entries.text: I like her. Genuine and down to earth. Very few airs and graces for her background.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Nice to see a young woman in comfor..."
entries.text: Nice to see a young woman in comfortable shoes.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What's your opinion on Miss McLeod?"
entries.text: What's your opinion on Miss McLeod?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, let me tell you this. My dhá..."
entries.text: Well, let me tell you this. My dhá sheallach isn't being affected by being in this place.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And I saw nothing about her that wo..."
entries.text: And I saw nothing about her that would suggest the cause of her loss - all of which tells me it's not mystical in nature.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Whatever is happening to that girl,..."
entries.text: Whatever is happening to that girl, it's as un-magical as you or... well, you.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "..."

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Varley

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The man needs to loosen up a bit! I..."
entries.text: The man needs to loosen up a bit! I've never seen anyone so dour in all my life.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of Mister Varley?"
entries.text: What do you make of Mister Varley?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I do see him about Gauford, doing j..."
entries.text: I do see him about Gauford, doing jobs from time to time.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You'd almost get the feeling that h..."
entries.text: You'd almost get the feeling that he's more against this séance than myself.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Lan Fen

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Missus Lau?"
entries.text: Have you met Missus Lau?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "She's a sharp one, isn't she? Fierc..."
entries.text: She's a sharp one, isn't she? Fierce bad luck to be a widow at that age, but these things happen...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "At least she's got Miss McLeod to t..."
entries.text: At least she's got Miss McLeod to take her to all sorts of interesting places.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh Lord, have mercy on anyone curse..."
entries.text: Oh Lord, have mercy on anyone cursed enough to have to deal with this small-minded amadán.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Mister Skerritt?"
entries.text: Have you met Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "He has strong opinions for a man wh..."
entries.text: He has strong opinions for a man who's achieved so little in his life. Achieved so little with so much, I might add.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If you or I had been born with a sp..."
entries.text: If you or I had been born with a spoon so silver in our mouths, we might have changed the world.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Instead, he decided to shove it up..."
entries.text: Instead, he decided to shove it up his thóin and do nothing.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Corentine

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Miss Quinn? I wasn't expecting her..."
entries.text: Miss Quinn? I wasn't expecting her to have her feet on the ground like she does, I'll give her that.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What impression do you have of Miss..."
entries.text: What impression do you have of Miss Quinn?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Maybe it's that heaviness she's car..."
entries.text: Maybe it's that heaviness she's carrying; there's something on her shoulders much greater than any one person should have to bear.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Caitlin

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know Missus Joyce?"
entries.text: Do you happen to know Missus Joyce?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, Caitlin. I know her. She knows..."
entries.text: Ah, Caitlin. I know her. She knows everyone's business, but that's nothing new - she's been a nosy beggar since we were small.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Pious as anything, except for when..."
entries.text: Pious as anything, except for when she'd get caught - then she'd find somebody to sacrifice to save herself.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darragh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I made it my business to get to kno..."
entries.text: I made it my business to get to know all the staff. Best source of information in a place like this. Better company, too.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know Mister Hunter..."
entries.text: Do you happen to know Mister Hunter?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mister Hutner is a fine, strong gen..."
entries.text: Mister Hutner is a fine, strong gentleman - though I can't say I've noticed... ahem!

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Seamus

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Bit of a blank slate there, like he..."
entries.text: Bit of a blank slate there, like he's blocked something out. Poor dear could do with a hug.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of Mister Doyle?"
entries.text: What do you make of Mister Doyle?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Deane

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Deane?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Deane?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Pfft, I have."
entries.text: Pfft, I have.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You stay away from that one, Declan..."
entries.text: You stay away from that one, Declan.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Lest she try take what's of value t..."
entries.text: Lest she try take what's of value to you.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Walter Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know young Walter Blake?"
entries.text: Do you know young Walter Blake?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, I've heard of him. Everyone l..."
entries.text: Well, I've heard of him. Everyone local has. Had hoped I'd get a good look at him while I was here, but he really does stick to the shadows, doesn't he?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Unusual Hair Colour - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Might I ask how you came to have th..."
entries.text: Might I ask how you came to have the white streak in your hair? I don't think I've seen its like, before.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I've had it all my life. You should..."
entries.text: I've had it all my life. You should have seen me with it when I was a little girl!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Some people believe it's a sign of..."
entries.text: Some people believe it's a sign of wisdom to be born with such a thing, you know.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Now, I can't say for certain that t..."
entries.text: Now, I can't say for certain that that's true - but I do like the idea.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Celtic Cross Necklace - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That's a fine cross you have there."
entries.text: That's a fine cross you have there.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, this? This is just to keep the..."
entries.text: Ah, this? This is just to keep the priests off my back. Between you and me, Declan, I don't much care for these new gods. Up on high on golden thrones? Pah!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I prefer the old Gods, walking and..."
entries.text: I prefer the old Gods, walking and working the land, side by side with us.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Folk Jewellery - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I don't believe I've seen jewellery..."
entries.text: I don't believe I've seen jewellery of the sort you're wearing before.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, well, a lot of it is handmade...."
entries.text: Ah, well, a lot of it is handmade. Some of it brings me luck, and some of it protects me. They're old crafts, to be sure, but not soon forgotten.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/patches - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I see you are handy with a needle a..."
entries.text: I see you are handy with a needle and thread.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I can stitch up jumpers and wounds...."
entries.text: I can stitch up jumpers and wounds. All part of the work. No need throwing something out, when all it needs is a mend.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh gods, no. The séance is still go..."
entries.text: Oh gods, no. The séance is still going ahead - damage will still happen.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Satisfied?"
entries.text: Satisfied?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But we've protected the well."
entries.text: But we've protected the well.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And..."
entries.text: And...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...I think a rift between Ruairí an..."
entries.text: ...I think a rift between Ruairí and I is mended.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah Declan. I'm so proud of him."
entries.text: Ah Declan. I'm so proud of him.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "What a fool I was to be such a stic..."
entries.text: What a fool I was to be such a stick in the mud!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I should have trusted his new ways,..."
entries.text: I should have trusted his new ways, and in doing so had faith in myself as a teacher.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I guess one always worries they've..."
entries.text: I guess one always worries they've not done enough to prepare their young 'uns.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But you have to let them fly, I sup..."
entries.text: But you have to let them fly, I suppose. And Ruairí? He soared.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "..."

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Someday, Declan, by the grace of Go..."
entries.text: Someday, Declan, by the grace of God, you'll have kids of your own. Then you'll know.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's leaving letter - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It turns out Miss Deane left a lett..."
entries.text: It turns out Miss Deane left a letter excusing herself from the event.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Then Miss Deane sounds like a smart..."
entries.text: Then Miss Deane sounds like a smarter person than I first gave her credit for.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know about the second s..."
entries.text: What do you know about the second sight?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, Declan, some people are born..."
entries.text: Well, Declan, some people are born with an innate ability to sense beyond the mundane.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "There exists a certain interconnect..."
entries.text: There exists a certain interconnection and weaving of the interlacing patterns of life in its many forms.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I myself can sense in my bones wher..."
entries.text: I myself can sense in my bones where a person or event is aligned in this network.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "For others, they can see ahead in t..."
entries.text: For others, they can see ahead in the pattern, sometimes in the forms of visions, often in the form of dreams.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You mentioned an ability of yours,..."
entries.text: You mentioned an ability of yours, an dhá sheallach, is it the same thing?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I am very glad I am not one of thes..."
entries.text: I am very glad I am not one of these people. It can hold a great weight and a constant sense of unease.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It seems that my instinct is not qu..."
entries.text: It seems that my instinct is not quite as on point as I thought.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Explain yourself, Mister Ward."
entries.text: Explain yourself, Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "[ CONFIDE IN HER ]"
entries.text: [ CONFIDE IN HER ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "[ LIE ]"

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'll come clean with you. I am here..."
entries.text: I'll come clean with you. I am here investigating the disappearance of Evelyn Deane.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found this key in the hallway, I..."
entries.text: I found this key in the hallway, I was just looking for the porter to return it.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I... "borrowed" this key to help wi..."
entries.text: I... "borrowed" this key to help with my investigations.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You did, did you? Then you might be..."
entries.text: You did, did you? Then you might be hurrying along to get it back to its rightful owner, hadn't you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Thank you, Declan, for not being an..."
entries.text: Thank you, Declan, for not being another of the liars. I'll be keeping a close eye and I'm happy to know you will be too.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Statement, Mister Doyle - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister Doyle said he overheard Miss..."
entries.text: Mister Doyle said he overheard Miss Deane arguing with someone on Tuesday.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's a new moon, Declan, on the eve..."
entries.text: It's a new moon, Declan, on the eve of Samhain. The veil is thinning, emotions are high... and something, I think, is afoot.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I took the trouble of seeing about..."
entries.text: I took the trouble of seeing about where Miss Deane went when she left, and I've found that her trail seems to stop in the middle of the hedge maze.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "As the veil thins, more gateways wi..."
entries.text: As the veil thins, more gateways will open that'll be hard to see if you don't know how to look.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "How would I look? It's as if she va..."
entries.text: How would I look? It's as if she vanished into thin air.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "One does not simply vanish into thi..."
entries.text: One does not simply vanish into thin air, Declan, but there are realms beyond the one we stand in.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And more occupiers of the land than..."
entries.text: And more occupiers of the land than ourselves.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I would start by looking beyond wha..."
entries.text: I would start by looking beyond what your eyes want you to see. Eyes cannot always be trusted.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Silks - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "Oh, how kind of you. I'll put it wi..."
entries.text: Oh, how kind of you. I'll put it with my others.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ OFFER SILKS ]"
entries.text: [ OFFER SILKS ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ KEEP SILKS ]"
entries.text: [ KEEP SILKS ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'll hold onto this for now."
entries.text: I'll hold onto this for now.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, I do think it's quite likely..."
entries.text: Well, I do think it's quite likely I'll be out in the maze for most of it.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It seems I'll be in the maze most o..."
entries.text: It seems I'll be in the maze most of the day again, Declan! I've offered a few scrying sessions at the old well.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "This old well may not show it, but..."
entries.text: This old well may not show it, but it needs a great deal more care than it likes to let on.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I'm tending to the old well, you se..."
entries.text: I'm tending to the old well, you see. It needs a great deal more care than it likes to let on.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Between all that, my dear nephew an..."
entries.text: Between all that, my dear nephew and I have lunch plans at one.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I want to run through my talk with..."
entries.text: I want to run through my talk with him which, incidentally, is in the drawing room at three.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "After that, it's dinner at seven, a..."
entries.text: After that, it's dinner at seven, and then feet up for the night!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Otherwise, I still have lunch at on..."
entries.text: Otherwise, I still have lunch at one. And I'm seeing the drawing room talks at three and five.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Then, of course, it's time to face..."
entries.text: Then, of course, it's time to face that damnable séance and see what's to come of it.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you have any plans for the weeke..."
entries.text: Do you have any plans for the weekend?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you have any plans for today?"
entries.text: Do you have any plans for today?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Though my Ruairí does like to gab,..."
entries.text: Though my Ruairí does like to gab, so I'm sure we'll be in the dining room right up until my talk!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It would be lovely to see you there..."
entries.text: It would be lovely to see you there, Declan. We're doing it in the drawing room at three.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "As for tomorrow..."
entries.text: As for tomorrow...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "After all that, I think this evenin..."
entries.text: After all that, I think this evening calls for a few quiet hours in the library!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "At least... now I feel watched over..."
entries.text: At least... now I feel watched over - safe. Ready for whatever is to come.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you at the bridge game on Tues..."
entries.text: Were you at the bridge game on Tuesday?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I was, dear, and a fine thrashing w..."
entries.text: I was, dear, and a fine thrashing we gave the posh beggers too, ha!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, well, it was myself and little..."
entries.text: Oh, well, it was myself and little Ruairí against Marquess Blake and Mister Coventry - much to their dismay.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Who was playing?"
entries.text: Who was playing?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The other table was Miss Quinn and..."
entries.text: The other table was Miss Quinn and Missus Lau against Missus D'Arcy and poor Miss Barbosa, who thought it would be fun to play, but was soon set right in those thoughts.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Newspaper clipping - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It seems like Missus Joyce has an i..."
entries.text: It seems like Missus Joyce has an interest in the goings on in Dublin.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, Declan... It seems, does it n..."
entries.text: Well, Declan... It seems, does it not, that the proverbial cat may be out of the bag?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But look, I'll never judge a man fo..."
entries.text: But look, I'll never judge a man for doing his job.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Drafted telegram - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It appears Missus Joyce sent for he..."
entries.text: It appears Missus Joyce sent for help - that she was worried about Miss Deane.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well if anyone would know, it would..."
entries.text: Well if anyone would know, it would be Caitlin.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And if she is concerned enough to t..."
entries.text: And if she is concerned enough to telegram... then that in itself is concerning enough to me.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Entertainment schedule - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A caught a glimpse of the entertain..."
entries.text: A caught a glimpse of the entertainment schedule for the week... they are packing quite a lot in!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Orchestrated to divert, Declan. Don..."
entries.text: Orchestrated to divert, Declan. Don't be fooled.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Even the magpie knows when to be ca..."
entries.text: Even the magpie knows when to be cautious of novel, flashy distractions.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Though I confess even I fell a litt..."
entries.text: Though I confess even I fell a little. A few games of bridge on Tuesday night but I forgive myself. Guilt is for the  Catholics.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/cigar burns - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mister Skerritt, conveniently for h..."
entries.text: Mister Skerritt, conveniently for him, fell asleep in one with a lit cigar - just as we were supposed to play a game of bridge. But then, that did give me cause to send for my Ruairí.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "We played a lot when he was little...."
entries.text: We played a lot when he was little. He doesn't like to let on, but he's quite good - and a better partner than that old man would have been.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Who'd be smoking in the library arm..."
entries.text: Who'd be smoking in the library armchairs?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/talks - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I can't say I was expecting there t..."
entries.text: I can't say I was expecting there to be talks at this event.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's for the better, I say. These p..."
entries.text: It's for the better, I say. These people ought to learn something about what they're doing while they're here.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Maybe they might even think better..."
entries.text: Maybe they might even think better of it.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Memento Mori - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know anything abou..."
entries.text: Do you happen to know anything about the Quinn family having an unusual number of deaths?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah. Quite a story, that one. And no..."
entries.text: Ah. Quite a story, that one. And not a happy one. Now, it was before my time that the Quinns were still in Ireland...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But as I hear it, they moved to Eng..."
entries.text: But as I hear it, they moved to England to try and escape a curse put upon them. I hear it didn't work.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "... And so the Quinns are still cur..."
entries.text: ... And so the Quinns are still cursed to reach untimely ends, every one of them. There can't be many left, now. Miss Quinn might be one of the last.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hiring telegram - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of this?"
entries.text: What do you make of this?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I wish I could say I'm surprised th..."
entries.text: I wish I could say I'm surprised that there's something not right afoot here... but I'd be lying.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I do hope you find that girl. She m..."
entries.text: I do hope you find that girl. She might be a fool, but she doesn't deserve harm to come to her.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photograph of Deane - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you recognise this woman?"
entries.text: Do you recognise this woman?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, yes. Miss Deane, isn't it? She'..."
entries.text: Oh, yes. Miss Deane, isn't it? She's been about.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you been to an event such as t..."
entries.text: Have you been to an event such as this one before?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Such as this one, with a rake of so..."
entries.text: Such as this one, with a rake of so-called magicians looking to tamper with the very fabric of our world?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "No, I haven't been that unlucky. Lo..."
entries.text: No, I haven't been that unlucky. Looks like my luck's run out, eh?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I couldn't think of a worse use for..."
entries.text: I couldn't think of a worse use for all this know-how if I tried.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mark my words - this little trick o..."
entries.text: Mark my words - this little trick of theirs, if it works, will be devastating.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mark my words - I might be here to..."
entries.text: Mark my words - I might be here to watch from a distance, but that's exactly what I'll do. I'll have nothing to do with that séance.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I've seen it on the wind and I feel..."
entries.text: I've seen it on the wind and I feel it in my bones.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Marriage talk - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've heard talk there's a young lad..."
entries.text: I've heard talk there's a young lady hoping to find a suitable marriage candidate here.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Here? Oh, God bless her!"
entries.text: Here? Oh, God bless her!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Whatever has the world come to?"
entries.text: Whatever has the world come to?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Family - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know much about the Blake fa..."
entries.text: Do you know much about the Blake family?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Can't say I've ever felt the need t..."
entries.text: Can't say I've ever felt the need to give them any time, thinking about them or otherwise.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The Blakes have taken enough from t..."
entries.text: The Blakes have taken enough from this place and the people here.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Manor - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the mano..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the manor?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "They say it was built by the first..."
entries.text: They say it was built by the first Blake to come to Ireland - that he was given the land by Cromwell himself.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It wasn't their land to give or rec..."
entries.text: It wasn't their land to give or receive - but that didn't stop them, now, did it?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Edward Blake - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know about Edward Blake..."
entries.text: What do you know about Edward Blake?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "He was a high-ranking officer in Cr..."
entries.text: He was a high-ranking officer in Cromwell's crusade. I don't recall the exact details.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "What I do know is that he was a sco..."
entries.text: What I do know is that he was a scourge on this place, before and after he was awarded the land.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The worst sort of man; the kind tha..."
entries.text: The worst sort of man; the kind that could put devils to shame.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've heard that you have been known..."
entries.text: I've heard that you have been known to offer people well scrying. What is that, exactly?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, to put it simply, scrying mea..."
entries.text: Well, to put it simply, scrying means looking. Looking for answers, or to somewhere you couldn't otherwise see.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And wells have a lot of power about..."
entries.text: And wells have a lot of power about them, you know. If you ask a question to one, it might give you answers.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If you're lucky, it'll even show yo..."
entries.text: If you're lucky, it'll even show you what you're looking for.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That's what I do - I ask the well f..."
entries.text: That's what I do - I ask the well for answers or information. More often than not, it more than provides.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photo of child - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think you'd be able to lead..."
entries.text: Do you think you'd be able to lead Miss Murphy in well scrying?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It would do her good to see her dau..."
entries.text: It would do her good to see her daughter, but the Magdalene Laundry that took her child - they won't share any information.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I can think of no better cause. You..."
entries.text: I can think of no better cause. You tell Miss Murphy I'm ready whenever she is, and to meet me at the well.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've heard tell that this manor is..."
entries.text: I've heard tell that this manor is haunted... Have you seen anything of the sort?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "There's more spirits here than any..."
entries.text: There's more spirits here than any one place should have, Declan, I can tell you that.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "A generosity of ghosts these past t..."
entries.text: A generosity of ghosts these past two hundred and fifty years.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Started with the bloody wound Cromw..."
entries.text: Started with the bloody wound Cromwell cut into this land...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...and carried on through generatio..."
entries.text: ...and carried on through generations of Edward Blake's depraved descendants.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ritual Markings - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found evidence of a ritual being..."
entries.text: I found evidence of a ritual being performed upstairs.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Did you now? No one has mentioned a..."
entries.text: Did you now? No one has mentioned anything of the sort to me.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That means it's some exclusive, hig..."
entries.text: That means it's some exclusive, high society nonsense, or it's something the person performing it doesn't want anyone else to know about. Hmm...

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter to Sister in Law - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor Callaghan's mother must be p..."
entries.text: Doctor Callaghan's mother must be proud of him following your footsteps?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ha! Oh yes, she's thrilled her doct..."
entries.text: Ha! Oh yes, she's thrilled her doctor son is committed to a life of helping the poor, instead of earning himself a fine income.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Given the chance, the woman would b..."
entries.text: Given the chance, the woman would burn me for a witch, only for my brother who stills her hand.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Séance Purpose - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of the intent of t..."
entries.text: What do you make of the intent of this séance?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I couldn't think of a worse use for..."
entries.text: I couldn't think of a worse use for all this know-how if I tried.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mark my words - I might be here to..."
entries.text: Mark my words - I might be here to watch from a distance, but that's exactly what I'll do. I'll have nothing to do with that séance.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hedonistic Gala - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did you enjoy the masked ball, Miss..."
entries.text: Did you enjoy the masked ball, Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Didn't go. I wasn't about to head t..."
entries.text: Didn't go. I wasn't about to head to a thing like that. I was playing cards with the staff for most of it.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The costumes were something else, t..."
entries.text: The costumes were something else, though! I'll give you all that.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Dreams - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have found my dreams quite distur..."
entries.text: I have found my dreams quite disturbed since coming here.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That doesn't surprise me in the lea..."
entries.text: That doesn't surprise me in the least - there's foul play afoot here with this séance business.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "People dreaming they're wandering t..."
entries.text: People dreaming they're wandering the halls, trying to get out of this place, then end up at the séance instead.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And still they want to attend the d..."
entries.text: And still they want to attend the damn thing? What more warning could they want that it's a bad idea!

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Sketches of Strange Symbol - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've been seeing a sketch of a symb..."
entries.text: I've been seeing a sketch of a symbol around I don't recognise. Here, I made a copy. Does this mean anything to you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That's curious... I don't think I'v..."
entries.text: That's curious... I don't think I've seen it before. Whatever could that mean?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Fetters - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've been told that a ghost require..."
entries.text: I've been told that a ghost requires "fetters" to keep it attached to this world. Would that be right?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That's about the right of it."
entries.text: That's about the right of it.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "There has to be something to keep t..."
entries.text: There has to be something to keep them here. Usually it's some emotional tie.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If a person dies wishing they could..."
entries.text: If a person dies wishing they could have finished some affair of theirs, or with a lot of anger, they're much more likely to return as a spirit.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ms Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If I might ask, Miss Callaghan... A..."
entries.text: If I might ask, Miss Callaghan... Am I right in thinking you're... less than satisfied with the course Doctor Callaghan is taking?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "He should know better than to get i..."
entries.text: He should know better than to get involved with all this high society magic nonsense, Declan. I taught him better than that.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Our craft isn't about social climbi..."
entries.text: Our craft isn't about social climbing or fancy parties, it's about respect and balance.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I think he's losing sight of that f..."
entries.text: I think he's losing sight of that for what it can gain him, instead.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have the impression that perhaps..."
entries.text: I have the impression that perhaps Doctor Callaghan has taken to this sort of high-society event because he doesn't feel respected as things are.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "What makes you say that?"
entries.text: What makes you say that?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "He's an accomplished practitioner,..."
entries.text: He's an accomplished practitioner, isn't he?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "He's one of the best."
entries.text: He's one of the best.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And yet you still consider him your..."
entries.text: And yet you still consider him your apprentice. Perhaps he finds that demeaning?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But I don't mean it like that! I..."
entries.text: But I don't mean it like that! I...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Perhaps I should talk to him."
entries.text: Perhaps I should talk to him.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Unknown Sigil - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've been seeing this sigil about t..."
entries.text: I've been seeing this sigil about the place. A spiral with four lines intersecting it. Have you seen anything of its type?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I don't believe I have, but I'll be..."
entries.text: I don't believe I have, but I'll be sure to look out for it.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Curse - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have heard that Miss Quinn's fami..."
entries.text: I have heard that Miss Quinn's family are under some sort of curse?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, so she's one of those Quinns -..."
entries.text: Ah, so she's one of those Quinns - it all makes sense, now. That's a lot of tragedy for one family... but they did visit it upon themselves, at least in the beginning.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "She seems like a nice girl herself,..."
entries.text: She seems like a nice girl herself, though. I hope it doesn't get her - we could do with more people like her around.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's Room - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know which room Miss Deane w..."
entries.text: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Now, Declan, I might be nosy, but I..."
entries.text: Now, Declan, I might be nosy, but I'm not quite that nosy. Your guess would be as good as mine.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "She couldn't be near me anyway, I'v..."
entries.text: She couldn't be near me anyway, I've not seen her in days.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Skull mask - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You weren't wearing a skull mask to..."
entries.text: You weren't wearing a skull mask to the ball last night, were you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "To the - ? My dear Declan, I wasn't..."
entries.text: To the - ? My dear Declan, I wasn't at the ball. You wouldn't catch me dead at a thing like that.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "No offence meant, of course."
entries.text: No offence meant, of course.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Red hair - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found a red hair inside a fallen..."
entries.text: I found a red hair inside a fallen mask. Does that mean anything to you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, it's not mine, if that's what..."
entries.text: Well, it's not mine, if that's what you're asking. I wasn't at the ball.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I noticed that the well has been co..."
entries.text: I noticed that the well has been covered in these strange symbols. Would you have any idea what they mean?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I should certainly hope so! I'm the..."
entries.text: I should certainly hope so! I'm the one who drew them.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, the land here has suffered, Dec..."
entries.text: Oh, the land here has suffered, Declan. I fear this séance, and all its agendas, may push her past the edge.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But I fear all these short-sighted..."
entries.text: But I fear all these short-sighted people have left us more in need of an optician than a healer.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That well is a pillar of the land -..."
entries.text: That well is a pillar of the land - has been since the time of the gods. If it is safe, the land will be safe.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The symbols are simply protective."
entries.text: The symbols are simply protective.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Miss Callaghan's Components - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Have you had any luck?"
entries.text: Have you had any luck?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Not yet..."
entries.text: Not yet...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, I have faith in you. An dhá s..."
entries.text: Well, I have faith in you. An dhá sheallach has me believing this is the right course of action, however unorthodox it might seem. Godspeed, Declan.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Occurences - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah Declan, you can't actually be as..."
entries.text: Ah Declan, you can't actually be asking me that. Sure, the whole place is mad!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you noticed anything strange s..."
entries.text: Have you noticed anything strange since coming here?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Whispers in walls, laughter outside..."
entries.text: Whispers in walls, laughter outside the windows, and no heat from the fire.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's wall to wall strangeness."
entries.text: It's wall to wall strangeness.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did you know that Miss Deane hails..."
entries.text: Did you know that Miss Deane hails from a powerful Milesian bloodline? That's what I've been hearing, at least.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Does she now? That little... no won..."
entries.text: Does she now? That little... no wonder she...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...Oh, I've no time to spend on bit..."
entries.text: ...Oh, I've no time to spend on bitterness, Declan.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I'll hope she miraculously puts it..."
entries.text: I'll hope she miraculously puts it to good use, and leave it at that.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Coded Papers - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does this ring any bells for you, M..."
entries.text: Does this ring any bells for you, Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "What an intricate sigil..."
entries.text: What an intricate sigil...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It seems to suggest something hidde..."
entries.text: It seems to suggest something hidden, Declan. And perhaps something that would best remain so.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Are you familiar with this book, Mi..."
entries.text: Are you familiar with this book, Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...I am not. And I absolutely don't..."
entries.text: ...I am not. And I absolutely don't want to be.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Whatever those sigils open or close..."
entries.text: Whatever those sigils open or close, I want no part in it.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is that what they say?"
entries.text: Is that what they say?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...Yes. One opens and the other clo..."
entries.text: ...Yes. One opens and the other closes. What - I cannot say, but it's old, powerful, and not for trifling with.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Witchcraft components - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of these? They loo..."
entries.text: What do you make of these? They look like components for a spell or charm of some kind to me.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "For a charm indeed, Declan. But for..."
entries.text: For a charm indeed, Declan. But for good or ill, I couldn't say. Either way, simple magic can be very powerful in the right hands.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Chimney Charm - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found this on the grounds. What d..."
entries.text: I found this on the grounds. What do you make of it?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, look at that. I'd imagine you..."
entries.text: Well, look at that. I'd imagine you found it in a chimney or under some floorboards? Why you're poking around hard-to-reach hiding places is your own business, Declan.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's a simple charm, needs to be cl..."
entries.text: It's a simple charm, needs to be close to the person it's targeting. Looks like it's meant to bind a magic user - stop them from moving or hurting another person, that sort of thing.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mister Callaghan's Components - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was speaking to Doctor Callaghan,..."
entries.text: I was speaking to Doctor Callaghan, and he seems to think these could aid your attempts to heal the well.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, Ruairí. How many times do I hav..."
entries.text: Oh, Ruairí. How many times do I have to tell you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You can try these modern methods al..."
entries.text: You can try these modern methods all you like, but they'll never be as robust or as studied as the old ways.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Quick fixes always come back to bit..."
entries.text: Quick fixes always come back to bite you, Declan. Remember that.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You mentioned you were a Bean Draoí..."
entries.text: You mentioned you were a Bean Draoí? What's that, now?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, it's like a hedge witch. I offe..."
entries.text: Ah, it's like a hedge witch. I offer treatments, both physical and spiritual, to the locals.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And I look after the land too. Real..."
entries.text: And I look after the land too. Really, though, a land and its people are intertwined, so it's all one.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi duties - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me more of your duties..."
entries.text: Can you tell me more of your duties?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, em... What else is there to say..."
entries.text: Oh, em... What else is there to say? Healing of the land, the body, the mind - all that.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Some veterinary work. Blessings on..."
entries.text: Some veterinary work. Blessings on the land and tributes to keep the Other Folk happy. I do the odd bit of scrying for those with the need for it.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And I train successors. Or, at leas..."
entries.text: And I train successors. Or, at least I try. Ruairí's been on and off that path, these days...

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Why do you think the séance is so d..."
entries.text: Why do you think the séance is so dangerous?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Declan. Are you a holy man?"
entries.text: Declan. Are you a holy man?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I am."
entries.text: I am.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Then you'd be of the mind that all..."
entries.text: Then you'd be of the mind that all this, how all this works, is God's will - God's design, yes?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I suppose that would be fair."
entries.text: I suppose that would be fair.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Whatever system you live by has sta..."
entries.text: Whatever system you live by has starts and ends. To pull that apart - with no plan to patch it up, mind, is to open a door that was never meant to be opened.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's what the Greeks called a Pando..."
entries.text: It's what the Greeks called a Pandora's Box.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about Marchion..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about Marchioness Blake?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Mary? I can tell you she didn't car..."
entries.text: Mary? I can tell you she didn't care much for that title.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "We only spoke a few times. She had..."
entries.text: We only spoke a few times. She had trouble conceiving, so she came to me under the dead of night for some alternative help.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The Marquess wouldn't have liked th..."
entries.text: The Marquess wouldn't have liked that sort of thing, then. Funny how death changes us.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I never heard much of how it turned..."
entries.text: I never heard much of how it turned out, but the boy's on the walls, so it must have worked.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "...Not that I doubted it would, min..."
entries.text: ...Not that I doubted it would, mind you!

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Goibniu - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know about the name Goi..."
entries.text: What do you know about the name Goibniu?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "A smithing god, same as Bríd. My un..."
entries.text: A smithing god, same as Bríd. My understanding is his work focused more on war - weapons and armour, you see, whereas her work was more for daily tasks - horseshoes, tools, pots, and the likes.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/fae - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about the fae?"
entries.text: What can you tell me about the fae?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The Other Folk, you mean? I'd be ca..."
entries.text: The Other Folk, you mean? I'd be careful - especially here, now. As we near Samhain, the veil gets thinner and thinner - it's not only ghosts that draw near.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Tuatha Dé Danann - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me about the Tuatha Dé..."
entries.text: Can you tell me about the Tuatha Dé Danann?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The old gods. They are all around u..."
entries.text: The old gods. They are all around us. In the hills, the rivers, the valleys.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I like that. I like when I am angry..."
entries.text: I like that. I like when I am angry with a god, I can go to their house and yell at them.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Just below the surface, where the o..."
entries.text: Just below the surface, where the other place can sometimes be found.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Brid - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me about the goddess B..."
entries.text: Can you tell me about the goddess Bríd?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well. As the Cailleach is the winte..."
entries.text: Well. As the Cailleach is the winter, they say Bríd is the summer. One of the fairest and most loved goddesses.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's said that when her son was kil..."
entries.text: It's said that when her son was killed by Goibniu that she keened the first keening. All other keening since, is her sharing that sorrow with mortalkind and knowing their pain of loss.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/morrigan - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you speak on the Morrigan?"
entries.text: Can you speak on the Morrigan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And what could I tell you? That's s..."
entries.text: And what could I tell you? That's she's a blood-hungry madwoman? Or that she's the great saviour of this land? A mother of monsters and lover of mankind?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Maybe she's all of it, maybe she's..."
entries.text: Maybe she's all of it, maybe she's not, maybe she's that and more. I don't truly know. I don't walk her path, and I've not met her.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The monks who wrote down our ways e..."
entries.text: The monks who wrote down our ways edited our ways. So, is she the villain they made her out to be? Maybe, but I'd wager she was more likely just a powerful and headstrong lass. That's villain enough for those monastic boys.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me anything about the..."
entries.text: Can you tell me anything about the Cailleach?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I've sat on her chair at the spring..."
entries.text: I've sat on her chair at the spring equinox to welcome the days and then again on the autumn one to bid them farewell.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I've crawled through her house on..."
entries.text: I've crawled through her house on  Slieve Gullion and caught a glimpse of the Otherworld.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "In return she sometimes visits me i..."
entries.text: In return she sometimes visits me in my sleep and teaches me a trick or two. It's from her I have my dhá sheallach.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "A bit, aye. It's her I welcome in w..."
entries.text: A bit, aye. It's her I welcome in when I form the circle and make space for intentions to form.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about Tír na n..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about Tír na nÓg?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's the home of the Gods, Declan...."
entries.text: It's the home of the Gods, Declan. And not just the Gods - the Fair Folk, and our dead too.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's sort of underneath us, and it..."
entries.text: It's sort of underneath us, and it isn't - as is the way of such places.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Caverns like Oweynagat, or cairns o..."
entries.text: Caverns like Oweynagat, or cairns of important people, or dolmens.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Significant ways under, down and th..."
entries.text: Significant ways under, down and through.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But it's there enough that coming a..."
entries.text: But it's there enough that coming and going is possible through passageways, found at places of great power, once the day is dark.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Significant ways under and down and..."
entries.text: Significant ways under and down and through.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the hedg..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the hedge maze's well?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I know everything about it! Do you..."
entries.text: I know everything about it! Do you know that the gods themselves would have drunk water from that well?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's been imbued with their power...."
entries.text: It's been imbued with their power. As long as that water is pure, the land around it will prosper.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about Milesian..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about Milesians?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well, that's the race of man who ca..."
entries.text: Well, that's the race of man who came to this island and battled the gods for the right to stay.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Funny - we first fought them, then..."
entries.text: Funny - we first fought them, then we worshipped them. Then we, largely, forgot.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I like that more than worshipping t..."
entries.text: I like that more than worshipping the God that we all lost to in the end, myself.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ruairí is talking more about this a..."
entries.text: Ruairí is talking more about this at 3pm tomorrow, you know. You could do worse than go to that for more.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ruairí is talking more about this a..."
entries.text: Ruairí is talking more about this at 3pm today, you know. You could do worse than go to that for more.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ruairí was talking about today, you..."
entries.text: Ruairí was talking about today, you know. You could do worse than ask him about this.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter from Dr Callaghan - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It seems Doctor Callaghan has been..."
entries.text: It seems Doctor Callaghan has been in recent correspondence with Miss Deane.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That wee scrut! I told him to stay..."
entries.text: That wee scrut! I told him to stay away from her! Writing to her behind my back, no less!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "She'd be the ruin of him!"
entries.text: She'd be the ruin of him!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And you mark my words, I won't let..."
entries.text: And you mark my words, I won't let that happen...

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think it's hard for Ruairí b..."
entries.text: Do you think it's hard for Ruairí being your apprentice for all these years?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Even now, I worry that little shado..."
entries.text: Even now, I worry that little shadow could disappear entirely inside my own.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That'll get you in just as much tro..."
entries.text: That'll get you in just as much trouble as never stopping to think in the first place.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "It's been a long road, yes. He's be..."
entries.text: It's been a long road, yes. He's been in my shadow since he was small.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But, he can still be a bit in his o..."
entries.text: But, he can still be a bit in his own head. Tries to think his way through when he should be feeling instead.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "He'll get there. He's just not ther..."
entries.text: He'll get there. He's just not there yet.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is it true that Miss Deane asked yo..."
entries.text: Is it true that Miss Deane asked you to teach her Irish magic?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The nerve of her. She didn't ask, s..."
entries.text: The nerve of her. She didn't ask, she demanded.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "A means, not an end. It wasn't the..."
entries.text: A means, not an end. It wasn't the path for her.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Not much gets by you, does it Decla..."
entries.text: Not much gets by you, does it Declan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "For her attitude alone I'd reject h..."
entries.text: For her attitude alone I'd reject her, but you can't just learn these things on a course. It's a way of life.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "How do you protect something like t..."
entries.text: How do you protect something like the well and the water?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Normally my work is less abstract...."
entries.text: Normally my work is less abstract. A sick lamb or a boy who needs the cure of a bad cough.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Right?"
entries.text: Right?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Declan, between you, me, and the br..."
entries.text: Declan, between you, me, and the breeze, I'm still figuring that bit out on the job.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "But the gods wouldn't give me a tas..."
entries.text: But the gods wouldn't give me a task I wasn't able for.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/gauge - fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of that strange de..."
entries.text: What do you make of that strange device in the atrium?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That worrisome jar of green energy?..."
entries.text: That worrisome jar of green energy? I've seen it. I've poked it. I've even spilled wine on it, but nothing seems to deter it from whatever it is doing.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I have a bad feeling about it, Decl..."
entries.text: I have a bad feeling about it, Declan.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah Declan. I'm sorry for whatever l..."
entries.text: Ah Declan. I'm sorry for whatever loss you've suffered.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "When I arrived, I thought I saw a w..."
entries.text: When I arrived, I thought I saw a woman washing clothes in the fountain.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The bean nigh, she's called. An ome..."
entries.text: The bean nigh, she's called. An omen of death to come. This is the kind of thing I was warning people about.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If you're seeing her, we'll have de..."
entries.text: If you're seeing her, we'll have death before this weekend is over. If it hasn't already happened.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The bean nigh, she's only clearly v..."
entries.text: The bean nigh, she's only clearly visible to those who're grieving. She's lured by the death to come, but can be seen by those with death's touch still on them - those still grieving for love lost.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Why did you say sorry for my loss?"
entries.text: Why did you say sorry for my loss?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Shadowy Figure - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you think of anything that migh..."
entries.text: Can you think of anything that might explain a large, ghostly figure on the land?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "All this messing has lured some of..."
entries.text: All this messing has lured some of the Fair Folk here. Or maybe awoken one of the Tuatha? ...Ah, don't look at me like a feckless cow, Declan. The Tuatha Dé Danann!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah, now they've gone and done it! I..."
entries.text: Ah, now they've gone and done it! I warned them that nothing good would come of this séance. It's not a ghost, that's for sure - they only come in the one size...

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "The old Gods! Gone from our plain t..."
entries.text: The old Gods! Gone from our plain to the Otherworld, but sure, what kind of god can't walk among its people every now and then?

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh not missing

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Callaghan is present and accou..."
entries.text: Miss Callaghan is present and accounted for. The red hair wasn't hers.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There's only one other person here..."
entries.text: There's only one other person here with hair that colour and length...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Domhnall Ó Finn must be our missing..."
entries.text: Domhnall Ó Finn must be our missing man.

title: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Declan Ward, what on this dying Ear..."
entries.text: Declan Ward, what on this dying Earth is wrong with you?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Fiadh-"
entries.text: Fiadh-

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "That's Miss Callaghan to you! Break..."
entries.text: That's Miss Callaghan to you! Breaking and entering, what-

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Come with me. Mister Varley is goin..."
entries.text: Come with me. Mister Varley is going to have words for you, I promise you that.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Sir, what on this dying earth is wr..."
entries.text: Sir, what on this dying earth is wrong with you?

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "LEAVE"
entries.text: LEAVE

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If you'll excuse me, Marquess Blake..."
entries.text: If you'll excuse me, Marquess Blake.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah. Mister Ward. How can I help?"
entries.text: Ah. Mister Ward. How can I help?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah, a new guest. You would be Miste..."
entries.text: Ah, a new guest. You would be Mister Ward, then?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan..."
entries.text: I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan Blake. A pleasure.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You have the better of me, Sir."
entries.text: You have the better of me, Sir.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Well then, Mister Ward. Welcome to..."
entries.text: Well then, Mister Ward. Welcome to my home and to the Grand Séance. I hope, whatever you are looking for, you find it here.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No, not really - I know nothing mor..."
entries.text: No, not really - I know nothing more than your name. That is why I invited you to lunch today, to meet you before the séance later.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I do hope you will attend."
entries.text: I do hope you will attend.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A shame you did not attend."
entries.text: A shame you did not attend.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I seem to have missed that invite,..."
entries.text: I seem to have missed that invite, Marquess. But now that I'm aware of it, I will do my best to be there.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Thank you for the invite, Marquess...."
entries.text: Thank you for the invite, Marquess. I certainly hope to see you there.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I seem to have missed that invite,..."
entries.text: I seem to have missed that invite, Marquess. My apologies for not attending.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "My apologies for not attending. The..."
entries.text: My apologies for not attending. There is so much to see around the manor that the - well the morning, it just got away from me.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No real harm done, Mister Ward. Wel..."
entries.text: No real harm done, Mister Ward. Welcome to my home and to the Grand Séance. I hope, whatever you are looking for, you find it here.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Of course."
entries.text: Of course.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/catches ward in residence

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Mister Ward! What on earth are you..."
entries.text: Mister Ward! What on earth are you doing in here?!

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Guests are not permitted in the pri..."
entries.text: Guests are not permitted in the private wing. As well you know.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "You may take your bags and leave, S..."
entries.text: You may take your bags and leave, Sir.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/bridge game

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know who attended?"
entries.text: Do you know who attended?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you at the bridge game on Tues..."
entries.text: Were you at the bridge game on Tuesday?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Yes. I have been trying to spend ti..."
entries.text: Yes. I have been trying to spend time with all the event participants. It was a suitable way to meet many at once.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Honestly, not all of them. Miss Cal..."
entries.text: Honestly, not all of them. Miss Callaghan organised it, I believe. Her and her boy - the doctor - were there. Simon... Mister Coventry, too. And... the second table... I cannot recall.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/talks - blake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The guests seem convinced this plac..."
entries.text: The guests seem convinced this place is... haunted... Perhaps, if ghosts are the memory of a place, they are right.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Certainly, she is an old building w..."
entries.text: Certainly, she is an old building with lots of history. I thought perhaps sharing some of that might add... perspective to their... hunt.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A séance is a strange event to host..."
entries.text: A séance is a strange event to host. How did that come to be?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It was the abruptness with which sh..."
entries.text: It was the abruptness with which she was taken. So much left unsaid.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I... lost my wife a few years ago...."
entries.text: I... lost my wife a few years ago. A carriage accident. It was... a difficult time for me.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I found some comfort through visiti..."
entries.text: I found some comfort through visiting a medium.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I would not say it "healed" me, but..."
entries.text: I would not say it "healed" me, but it helped me get on this path.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Naturally, I became interested in t..."
entries.text: Naturally, I became interested in the practice and wanted to do my part in forwarding the field.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have no abilities there, so to sp..."
entries.text: I have no abilities there, so to speak, but I have this manor - and so that is what I offer up.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hotel Finances - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "An event like this must be a real b..."
entries.text: An event like this must be a real boost for the hotel's income?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "One hopes. But this is about more t..."
entries.text: One hopes. But this is about more than profit, Mister Ward - money unrecovered is still money well spent.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I heard of your late wife. My condo..."
entries.text: I heard of your late wife. My condolences.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "My thanks, Mister Ward."
entries.text: My thanks, Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "You know, it was a controversial ma..."
entries.text: You know, it was a controversial marriage. Her family were not of high enough status for my title.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "My Aunt Catherine, God rest her sou..."
entries.text: My Aunt Catherine, God rest her soul, was just glad I had married at all. She felt I had thrown too much of myself into this hotel business.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She was right, of course. After the..."
entries.text: She was right, of course. After the hardships of the famines, I had felt it was important to secure the family house and finances.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But then, if Mary had not come to s..."
entries.text: But then, if Mary had not come to stay here, we would never have met - and so the great wheel turns.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Have you ever felt love, Mister War..."
entries.text: Have you ever felt love, Mister Ward? She unlocked me, is how I would describe it.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She was, is, my everythi--"
entries.text: She was, is, my everythi--

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "...I ...am sorry, Mister Ward. You..."
entries.text: ...I ...am sorry, Mister Ward. You will have to excuse me a moment.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But for whom, with no heirs?"
entries.text: But for whom, with no heirs?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "..."

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If you will forgive my forwardness,..."
