entries.text: If you will forgive my forwardness, but I was not expecting a gala quite like the one of last night.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I assure you, Mister Ward, neither..."
entries.text: I assure you, Mister Ward, neither was I. But these things - rituals, I mean - have, well... rituals.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You mean to say that was part of th..."
entries.text: You mean to say that was part of the séance?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Part of the preparation for it, yes..."
entries.text: Part of the preparation for it, yes. Tonight we perform the séance, but we have been hurtling towards it for some time now.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "With the ball, we crossed one of th..."
entries.text: With the ball, we crossed one of the final thresholds, the point of no return.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Strange Dreams - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Might I ask - is there a history of..."
entries.text: Might I ask - is there a history of people having strange dreams in the manor?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I only dream of my wife and son, Mi..."
entries.text: I only dream of my wife and son, Mister Ward. There is nothing strange about that.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "As for what my ancestors dreamt, I..."
entries.text: As for what my ancestors dreamt, I could not say.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It is likely the time of year and t..."
entries.text: It is likely the time of year and the event playing with my mind, but I could swear I have seen... things. Figures in the distance.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "There have been reports of haunting..."
entries.text: There have been reports of hauntings on the manor and its grounds as far back as my family has held it.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Certainly, I have encountered the o..."
entries.text: Certainly, I have encountered the occasional oddity, myself.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "What do I think they are? In truth,..."
entries.text: What do I think they are? In truth, I do not know. Are they even real? Well... on that, all I can say is the Blake family records are littered with mysterious deaths and insanities that have no other explanation...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Hopefully tonight, we will find out..."
entries.text: Hopefully tonight, we will find out for certain.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Room - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know which room Miss Deane w..."
entries.text: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No. If, for some reason, you must k..."
entries.text: No. If, for some reason, you must know, you might ask the manager. I'm not concerned with such things.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Invitation - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did you personally invite Miss Dean..."
entries.text: Did you personally invite Miss Deane to the manor, Marquess?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The only guest that was invited was..."
entries.text: The only guest that was invited was Miss Mantovani. Her name was enough to bring the rest.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "...I did. A number of guests were i..."
entries.text: ...I did. A number of guests were invited. Then others, like yourself, just... showed up.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Miss Deane's late departure is frus..."
entries.text: Miss Deane's late departure is frustrating enough without her having been invited, frankly.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/map of the region - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Might I ask how much of this area b..."
entries.text: Might I ask how much of this area belongs to you and your family?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I'm unsure any more. We owned quite..."
entries.text: I'm unsure any more. We owned quite a lot a long time ago. Some have been sold over the years, or traded as dowries.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "There are records, but I'd have to..."
entries.text: There are records, but I'd have to go and search them.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has the manor been open to the publ..."
entries.text: Has the manor been open to the public for long?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I took over the titles and lands wh..."
entries.text: I took over the titles and lands when my father died in the mid 1860s.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The manor was over two hundred year..."
entries.text: The manor was over two hundred years old by then, and needed much work.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But the famine did not leave a lot..."
entries.text: But the famine did not leave a lot of spare funds, so I opened the place as a hotel to help finance the renovations. This was in the spring of 1870.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The work is never-ending, so we sta..."
entries.text: The work is never-ending, so we stay open. But it wasn't for that reason alone - it's nice to have people here. When I was young, there were more of us.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "And, I'm told, in my grandfather's..."
entries.text: And, I'm told, in my grandfather's time and before that, there were many families under the roof.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It was not made to sit here idle. I..."
entries.text: It was not made to sit here idle. It is good for the house to have life in it.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/seance contract - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Might I ask how you secured Miss Ma..."
entries.text: Might I ask how you secured Miss Mantovani's talents? It is a long way to go for work, no?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "To be frank, Mister Ward, she was s..."
entries.text: To be frank, Mister Ward, she was secured the way all talent is - money.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But it is an investment I stand beh..."
entries.text: But it is an investment I stand behind, both financially and spiritually.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/vase - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does the vase in these drawings loo..."
entries.text: Does the vase in these drawings look familiar?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have seen it before. I think perh..."
entries.text: I have seen it before. I think perhaps in a family portrait?

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does the manor have catacombs or ot..."
entries.text: Does the manor have catacombs or other underground passages?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Almost certainly, Mister Ward. The..."
entries.text: Almost certainly, Mister Ward. The estate has a long and storied history.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I know of some half-collapsed corri..."
entries.text: I know of some half-collapsed corridors and a closed-in bolthole, but I would not be surprised to learn of more.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Who knows what secrets my ancestors..."
entries.text: Who knows what secrets my ancestors held and what threats they needed to run from.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "And, of course, the place was built..."
entries.text: And, of course, the place was built atop an old settlement, which no doubt has its own secrets to add to the mix...

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/shadowy figure - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have there ever been legends of gia..."
entries.text: Have there ever been legends of giant creatures stalking the manor grounds?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I've heard and read about many supe..."
entries.text: I've heard and read about many supernatural sightings here, but nothing like that. You could ask the staff, perhaps?

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/timetable - blake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Are the silent dinner and séance no..."
entries.text: Are the silent dinner and séance not enough for you, Mister Ward? Certainly I expect they will keep me busy much of the day.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Anything interesting planned for to..."
entries.text: Anything interesting planned for today?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I will make time for Mister Coventr..."
entries.text: I will make time for Mister Coventry's talk, however. It's always interesting to hear an outsider's perspective on one's home.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/recluse - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Your son, Walter - he keeps to hims..."
entries.text: Your son, Walter - he keeps to himself?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "He is not best suited to life in a..."
entries.text: He is not best suited to life in a hotel, but our private residence is large enough that he is never forced to face that reality.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Would he have been different, had t..."
entries.text: Would he have been different, had the accident not happened? His mother was certainly more social than I. Perhaps he would have learned some of that from her.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Might I ask, what actually caused t..."
entries.text: Might I ask, what actually caused the carriage accident?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "...I suppose you might."
entries.text: ...I suppose you might.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It happened three years ago. Mary h..."
entries.text: It happened three years ago. Mary had taken the boy to Gauford for a treat, to see the boats. I suspect there was no reason for it, other than her good heart.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A storm came in that day, quickly...."
entries.text: A storm came in that day, quickly. The driver suggested they return to the manor before it became too severe.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "That this happened on October 31st..."
entries.text: That this happened on October 31st is an irony not lost on me - though it is entirely coincidental.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But they left it too late. The road..."
entries.text: But they left it too late. The roads were muddy, the winds strong. A tree fell, and in his efforts to avoid it, the driver lost control of the carriage.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It tumbled, and Mary was... well, s..."
entries.text: It tumbled, and Mary was... well, she was gone.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The driver succumbed to his own inj..."
entries.text: The driver succumbed to his own injuries a few hours later, bleeding out. No doctor could get here in time to save him.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The driver, bless him, managed to p..."
entries.text: The driver, bless him, managed to pull Walter out and carried him back to the manor.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It must be difficult, your son's in..."
entries.text: It must be difficult, your son's injuries.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am not sure which is worse, Mary'..."
entries.text: I am not sure which is worse, Mary's death or his injuries.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "To know so much of his life has bee..."
entries.text: To know so much of his life has been taken from him. He'll never ride a horse, nor dance with the woman he loves.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Will he find love? Will it matter i..."
entries.text: Will he find love? Will it matter if he does? Or does the Blake line end with him.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I would give anything, do anything,..."
entries.text: I would give anything, do anything, take any risk to undo what has been done to him...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "...if that were an option..."
entries.text: ...if that were an option...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "..."

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Are there many Blakes left?"
entries.text: Are there many Blakes left?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No doubt, some distant relatives ex..."
entries.text: No doubt, some distant relatives exist somewhere, but I don't know of them.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No. The manor was full once, the fa..."
entries.text: No. The manor was full once, the family larger, but it is just Walter and I now.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The numbers dwindle each generation..."
entries.text: The numbers dwindle each generation - tragedy and marriage into other families.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The west of Ireland is very remote..."
entries.text: The west of Ireland is very remote - once a woman has been betrothed, she rarely keeps in touch - and is even less likely to return.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/refusal to remarry - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I am told there is some scandal aro..."
entries.text: I am told there is some scandal around your choice not to remarry?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Is there now? I did my duty, I marr..."
entries.text: Is there now? I did my duty, I married and sired. Perhaps it did not work out as intended, but I am under no further obligation.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have not met another woman like M..."
entries.text: I have not met another woman like Mary. Perhaps our vows were 'until death do us part', but I will face her at God's door as true to her as I ever was.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fall from grace - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "An event like this - it must seem s..."
entries.text: An event like this - it must seem strange to your peers?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Mister Ward... I have no peers."
entries.text: Mister Ward... I have no peers.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "This is my land and my coin. I will..."
entries.text: This is my land and my coin. I will make use of it in any way I wish.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Let the babbling masses complain. I..."
entries.text: Let the babbling masses complain. It only serves to highlight how little they understand. Or dare to understand.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Forgive my discussion of money at a..."
entries.text: Forgive my discussion of money at a time like this, but... surely Miss Mantovani's talents couldn't have come cheap?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No, indeed. But for an event so imp..."
entries.text: No, indeed. But for an event so important as this one, I will only have the best.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And this séance is very important?"
entries.text: And this séance is very important?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Mister Ward... Have you not figured..."
entries.text: Mister Ward... Have you not figured that out by now? The expense, the people, the distance they have come...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It will be one of the most importan..."
entries.text: It will be one of the most important nights in history.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/wilhmena blake - Jblake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But yes, I do recall that she disap..."
entries.text: But yes, I do recall that she disappeared. We have a portrait of her in the lobby, I believe. And, no doubt, something on her in the library, if you are interested.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does the name Wilhelmina Blake mean..."
entries.text: Does the name Wilhelmina Blake mean anything to you?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah. A great-aunt of mine, if I am n..."
entries.text: Ah. A great-aunt of mine, if I am not mistaken. I don't recall much about her - she disappeared long before I arrived into the world.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know about any......"
entries.text: Do you happen to know about any... unusual rumours afflicting the Quinn family?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "You're asking about the curse, of c..."
entries.text: You're asking about the curse, of course.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The Quinns left Ireland before my t..."
entries.text: The Quinns left Ireland before my time, but they still have many holdings here.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Something happened there, and a cur..."
entries.text: Something happened there, and a curse was put on them. I'm told they moved to England to escape it, but to no avail.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "They are still cursed to reach unti..."
entries.text: They are still cursed to reach untimely ends, every one of them. There are not many left. Miss Quinn is one of the last.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fae - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me anything about the..."
entries.text: Can you tell me anything about the fae?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I know the workers on the land leav..."
entries.text: I know the workers on the land leave out tribute to them and blame them when the crops go wrong.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "When a person goes missing, it's of..."
entries.text: When a person goes missing, it's often blamed on them too. Or, when a child has an accident...

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about the stra..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about the strange device in the atrium?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The gauge? It was built for this ev..."
entries.text: The gauge? It was built for this event - it is a measure of our collective psychic energy, a measure of how ready we are to pierce the veil.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "And thus a predictor of the séance'..."
entries.text: And thus a predictor of the séance's success.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It was full when I arrived, but tha..."
entries.text: It was full when I arrived, but that is no longer the case. Will that impact things?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I cannot say for certain, but a ful..."
entries.text: I cannot say for certain, but a fuller reading would be preferable.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I'm sure Miss Mantovani will overco..."
entries.text: I'm sure Miss Mantovani will overcome any obstacles she encounters, however.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/washer woman - blake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have seen this woman. Though she..."
entries.text: I have seen this woman. Though she is no woman - she is a spectre. I see her across the manor. More now as the place fills and the hour draws near.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "When I arrived, I... I saw a woman..."
entries.text: When I arrived, I... I saw a woman washing something in the fountain.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Sometimes I think she is Mary, but...."
entries.text: Sometimes I think she is Mary, but... No...

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/After Mary Blake - Blake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Thank you. Now. Where were we?"
entries.text: Thank you. Now. Where were we?

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/will - blake

entries.label: Ward: "Did you know that Mister Coventry h..."
entries.text: Did you know that Mister Coventry has left all of his earthly possessions to Walter in his will?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Has he? How... unusual. I suppose h..."
entries.text: Has he? How... unusual. I suppose he has no children of his own... He must have taken a shine to the boy.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Still..."
entries.text: Still...

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/cigar burn

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If you don't mind me asking, Marque..."
entries.text: If you don't mind me asking, Marquess, do you happen to know what caused those burns on the library armchair?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I hadn't noticed Mister Ward. I'll..."
entries.text: I hadn't noticed Mister Ward. I'll be sure to tell Mister Varley to have it seen to.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ivy

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Miss McLeod? Ah, yes, the seer. Of..."
entries.text: Miss McLeod? Ah, yes, the seer. Of course - how could I not make time?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Miss McLeod at a..."
entries.text: Have you spoken to Miss McLeod at all?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I had hoped she'd be able to provid..."
entries.text: I had hoped she'd be able to provide insights into our future success, but alas, she seems weakened.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I assume too many powerful minds in..."
entries.text: I assume too many powerful minds in one place, but I could well be wrong.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has Mister Varley been with you lon..."
entries.text: Has Mister Varley been with you long?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Since the beginning. He's a fine ma..."
entries.text: Since the beginning. He's a fine man, a loyal man. I know this event does not sit well with him and the other staff, but they understand it's important to me, and so they work their damndest to make it work. That's the attitude one needs in servants.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Lan Fen

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Missus Lau. The Chinese lady, I pre..."
entries.text: Missus Lau. The Chinese lady, I presume?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know Missus Lau?"
entries.text: Do you know Missus Lau?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She was at a bridge game I attended..."
entries.text: She was at a bridge game I attended last week. A keen player.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She is more interested in what is t..."
entries.text: She is more interested in what is taking place here than she admits. Why the pretence, I do not know.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Skerritt

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Mister Skerritt?"
entries.text: Have you met Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The banker, yes. For a man who has..."
entries.text: The banker, yes. For a man who has never experienced love he has a lot of opinions on what it might be.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I suspect it was his attention that..."
entries.text: I suspect it was his attention that drove Miss Deane off, in the end.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Corentine

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Quinn before?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Quinn before?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Before this event, no. But I have f..."
entries.text: Before this event, no. But I have family who know - or rather, knew - hers. She and I have spoken during her stay. Miss Quinn seems well-versed in her esoteric studies, and I'm glad to have her here.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Caitlin

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Missus Joyce is your housekeeper, y..."
entries.text: Missus Joyce is your housekeeper, yes?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The housekeeper, yes - though not j..."
entries.text: The housekeeper, yes - though not just that. Since my wife's passing, Missus Joyce has carried the burden of being Walter's caretaker.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "With no children of her own, she mo..."
entries.text: With no children of her own, she moved here full-time after her husband's passing. I am grateful for her. I love the boy, but I am no mother.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darragh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister Hunter acts as both the stab..."
entries.text: Mister Hunter acts as both the stable master and groundsman, yes?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The man is a powerhouse. He does th..."
entries.text: The man is a powerhouse. He does the work of five men around here. I have offered to bring in some support for him, but he loves the work - and the solitude it provides.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Seamus

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has the porter, Mister Doyle, been..."
entries.text: Has the porter, Mister Doyle, been here long?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "No - nor do I see him staying here..."
entries.text: No - nor do I see him staying here much longer.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The staff are like a family to one..."
entries.text: The staff are like a family to one another, but he does not seem to feel that way. I do not need friction under my roof.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Please, Marquess, tell me about you..."
entries.text: Please, Marquess, tell me about yourself?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am the ninth Marquess of Doon, fo..."
entries.text: I am the ninth Marquess of Doon, for a start.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But the first to open the building..."
entries.text: But the first to open the building to outsiders.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "What is there to say? I am a dedica..."
entries.text: What is there to say? I am a dedicated father, devoted husband, a man of God, and the host for this séance.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Coventry

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met with Mister Coventry?"
entries.text: Have you met with Mister Coventry?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have tried to meet with each of t..."
entries.text: I have tried to meet with each of the event's guests. Mister Coventry's reason for being here mirrors my own - he has lost a wife.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Hopefully, he too, gets what he wan..."
entries.text: Hopefully, he too, gets what he wants from the séance.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on O Finn

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met with Mister Ó Finn?"
entries.text: Have you met with Mister Ó Finn?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "That's the mountain man, yes? Not y..."
entries.text: That's the mountain man, yes? Not yet, but I intend to speak with him before the séance.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Mantovanni

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "How did you hear about Miss Mantova..."
entries.text: How did you hear about Miss Mantovani?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "In the same way, one learns of any..."
entries.text: In the same way, one learns of any expert - I asked for recommendations. Her name came at the top of most lists, and so I contacted her.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She has proven a delight, and I hav..."
entries.text: She has proven a delight, and I have the utmost faith in her for the task she undertakes.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Fiadh

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know Miss Callaghan?"
entries.text: Do you know Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The local witch? I have heard of he..."
entries.text: The local witch? I have heard of her, of course. Her name always comes up when a crop fails or an animal is sick. The locals call her in to fix things.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I turn a blind eye - they are entit..."
entries.text: I turn a blind eye - they are entitled to handle things as they see fit.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I had considered her as a host for..."
entries.text: I had considered her as a host for this event but based on what I know of the woman, she would have turned me down.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Dupre

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know who Mister Dupré is?"
entries.text: Do you know who Mister Dupré is?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah yes. The voodoo undertaker. It i..."
entries.text: Ah yes. The voodoo undertaker. It is flattering that he has come so far for us. I hope he enjoys his time here.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darcy

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know Missus D'Arcy?"
entries.text: Do you know Missus D'Arcy?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Only by name, through her husband...."
entries.text: Only by name, through her husband. It's a shame he did not join us - I'm told he's quite the accomplished magus.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Father sinnot

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met the priest, Father Sin..."
entries.text: Have you met the priest, Father Sinnott?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am ashamed to say that the few ti..."
entries.text: I am ashamed to say that the few times we have spoken have been... stilted. In truth, I have never spoken to a Catholic priest before and find him... intimidating.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I hope we can find a way to convers..."
entries.text: I hope we can find a way to converse outside of that. I am sure he has much to share that is of value - if only I can find a way to pull it from him.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Cathal

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had time to talk with Cath..."
entries.text: Have you had time to talk with Cathal O'Meara?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "He is the one obsessed with angels,..."
entries.text: He is the one obsessed with angels, yes? That surprised me. I've had dealings with his uncle, and he, at least, seemed perfectly grounded.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Hazel

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You've met Missus Erickson, I assum..."
entries.text: You've met Missus Erickson, I assume?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I... perhaps. I have met a lot of p..."
entries.text: I... perhaps. I have met a lot of people. She must not have made much of an impression.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It must be surprising to have someb..."
entries.text: It must be surprising to have somebody like Mister Toussaint here?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "The debunker? Yes, well - I believe..."
entries.text: The debunker? Yes, well - I believe we have the best chance of achieving our goal when all minds are attuned to it.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "His presence, I fear, might be like..."
entries.text: His presence, I fear, might be like a person singing out of key in a choir - or singing a different song entirely.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A distraction for the rest and a so..."
entries.text: A distraction for the rest and a sour overall experience.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "...Perhaps he is the reason our gau..."
entries.text: ...Perhaps he is the reason our gauge has dropped? Hmmm...

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Arwa

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has Miss Hisham spoken with you?"
entries.text: Has Miss Hisham spoken with you?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She is the lady looking for reparat..."
entries.text: She is the lady looking for reparations for past deeds, is she not?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "How gauche to bring it up here and..."
entries.text: How gauche to bring it up here and now. Does she not care for our greater aim here? She could come and berate me any other week, but not now.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor Callaghan is from the area...."
entries.text: Doctor Callaghan is from the area. Do you know him?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Not especially, but I am glad he ha..."
entries.text: Not especially, but I am glad he has come. I gather his talents are suitably impressive.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has Miss Barbosa talked with you?"
entries.text: Has Miss Barbosa talked with you?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Hmmm? Oh yes. If she were not from..."
entries.text: Hmmm? Oh yes. If she were not from the far side of the world, I would have forgotten her entirely.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "How she ended up here, I do not kno..."
entries.text: How she ended up here, I do not know. She is quite clear that the event holds little interest to her.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Saoirse

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Murphy, has she been with you..."
entries.text: Miss Murphy, has she been with you long?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A few years. She all but grew up he..."
entries.text: A few years. She all but grew up here. She became a woman here, too - sadly. The less said about that, the better.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But that mistake is behind her now,..."
entries.text: But that mistake is behind her now, and she has been given a second chance. The good Lord does not grant a third.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've not yet had the pleasure of me..."
entries.text: I've not yet had the pleasure of meeting your son.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Nor will you. With respect, Sir, I..."
entries.text: Nor will you. With respect, Sir, I do not think this event is suitable for him - too many strange ideas for his young mind.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It is bad enough that I have straye..."
entries.text: It is bad enough that I have strayed down this path. If my wildest dreams come true and I see my wife, then... I will be fit to deal with whatever that does to me.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "But he is just a boy. I fear what s..."
entries.text: But he is just a boy. I fear what seeing her like that might do to him. Or not seeing her - that, too, would be hard on him.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I would do anything to protect that..."
entries.text: I would do anything to protect that boy - and so I have ordered him to stay in our residence until this whole ordeal is over.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Deane

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken much with Miss Dean..."
entries.text: Have you spoken much with Miss Deane?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She left before we'd had a chance t..."
entries.text: She left before we'd had a chance to be introduced. A shame - I gather she is quite the woman, and a capable practitioner of her art.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Tired shoulders - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You look to be carrying the world u..."
entries.text: You look to be carrying the world upon your shoulders, Marquess.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Hmmm. These last few years have not..."
entries.text: Hmmm. These last few years have not been easy. But that will all be in the past, soon. A new day, a new chapter, is only hours away.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Haunted expression - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You seem worried. Is everything alr..."
entries.text: You seem worried. Is everything alright?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Do I now? I suppose it is fair to s..."
entries.text: Do I now? I suppose it is fair to say that I have a lot riding on this event.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Once it is done, it will be nice to..."
entries.text: Once it is done, it will be nice to return to the way things were and relax for a spell.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Proud Stature - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It must be a great privilege to be..."
entries.text: It must be a great privilege to be the Marquess of Doon.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It is but, I cannot lie, the title..."
entries.text: It is but, I cannot lie, the title means less nowadays. The family is smaller, the holdings smaller, still.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It is my hope that turning the mano..."
entries.text: It is my hope that turning the manor into a hotel and hosting this event will play their parts in reinvigorating the role, before I pass it on to Walter.

title: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/watch - Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Keeping an eye on the time, Marques..."
entries.text: Keeping an eye on the time, Marquess?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "This séance has been in planning fo..."
entries.text: This séance has been in planning for some time now. As we near the séance itself, it feels as if time is slowing.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am most eager to get to it."
entries.text: I am most eager to get to it.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Yes?"
entries.text: Yes?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "We did not receive your message, Mi..."
entries.text: We did not receive your message, Mister Ward. Our telegraph machine is broken.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Regardless. I am Vincent Varley, th..."
entries.text: Regardless. I am Vincent Varley, the manager here. We are quite full at present, but we can fit you in.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I'll send word that a room should b..."
entries.text: I'll send word that a room should be prepared, and I'll show you to it as soon as is possible. It shall be no later than midnight.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "But first, we require our guests to..."
entries.text: But first, we require our guests to sign in. If you would...

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "The book, Mister Ward, if you would..."
entries.text: The book, Mister Ward, if you would...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Hello. I'm Declan Ward. I telegramm..."
entries.text: Hello. I'm Declan Ward. I telegrammed ahead.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Yes, we received your message. You..."
entries.text: Yes, we received your message. You failed to mention the late hour of your arrival.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I've been trying to replace the bat..."
entries.text: I've been trying to replace the battery. Were it not for that, I'd have locked up by now.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Now. Mister Ward, was it?"
entries.text: Now. Mister Ward, was it?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Yes. I telegrammed ahead."
entries.text: Yes. I telegrammed ahead.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I see."
entries.text: I see.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I wouldn't be up at this hour, but..."
entries.text: I wouldn't be up at this hour, but I've been trying to replace the battery in the thing. If it were not for that, I'd have locked up before now.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "May I be of service, Mister Ward?"
entries.text: May I be of service, Mister Ward?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "LEAVE"
entries.text: LEAVE

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I need nothing else, thank you."
entries.text: I need nothing else, thank you.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Certainly."
entries.text: Certainly.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Then I shall return to my office. I..."
entries.text: Then I shall return to my office. If you need me again, no doubt you know how to summon me.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "This way, Sir."
entries.text: This way, Sir.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Then please wait here. The staff wi..."
entries.text: Then please wait here. The staff will prepare your room, and I'll be back to show you to it shortly.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Mister Ward. I do hope the earlier..."
entries.text: Mister Ward. I do hope the earlier commotion with the bird didn't disturb your rest?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Is there anything else I can help w..."
entries.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And your fellow guests will be givi..."
entries.text: And your fellow guests will be giving talks throughout the day in the drawing room, located in the west corridor.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "CONFRONT!"
entries.text: CONFRONT!

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "...Yes. I regret to say it, but you..."
entries.text: ...Yes. I regret to say it, but you're right.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Do not get me wrong - I am concerne..."
entries.text: Do not get me wrong - I am concerned for Miss Deane. But I have done what I can, and still cannot find her.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "This séance, the Marquess' obsessio..."
entries.text: This séance, the Marquess' obsession, and the money spent... We need this event to go well or we are homeless.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Now. If you will excuse me. With th..."
entries.text: Now. If you will excuse me. With the telegraph machine broken, I have delivery orders to write for the morning.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If you need me again, you know how..."
entries.text: If you need me again, you know how to summon me.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Thank you for bringing this to my a..."
entries.text: Thank you for bringing this to my attention. Your room should be ready soon, and I'll show you to it then.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Now, if you'll excuse me, I have so..."
entries.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some messages to send before then.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If that's true, and that stash of g..."
entries.text: If that's true, and that stash of gold is somewhere on the grounds, then finding it might just be enough to save the hotel.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Take this - it was found in what re..."
entries.text: Take this - it was found in what remained of the lady's personal belongings, but I've never discovered what it unlocks. It's not much, but it's a start.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I've had no luck, obviously. But yo..."
entries.text: I've had no luck, obviously. But you... you might be able to find it.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It's certainly possible. If that wi..."
entries.text: It's certainly possible. If that will stop you from hindering this investigation, then I will see if I can help.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You see... There are rumours of tre..."
entries.text: You see... There are rumours of treasure somewhere on the estate - a cache of gold from the mid-to-late 1600s.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Grainne, the wife of the original M..."
entries.text: Grainne, the wife of the original Marquess, Edward Blake - she did not... choose to be with him.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "There is breakfast in the dining ha..."
entries.text: There is breakfast in the dining hall from 9am, located in the east corridor here.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "She had hoarded a sum of money, int..."
entries.text: She had hoarded a sum of money, intending to use it to escape her husband...

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "...she stabbed him in his sleep, bu..."
entries.text: ...she stabbed him in his sleep, but he awoke and managed to live long enough to kill her.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "They died together, and the treasur..."
entries.text: They died together, and the treasure has not since been found.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Sir, you have not done what you cou..."
entries.text: Sir, you have not done what you could!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You hid her disappearance - if you..."
entries.text: You hid her disappearance - if you had alerted the police, then a proper search of this place could have been undertaken.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Something may well have happened, o..."
entries.text: Something may well have happened, or happen to her yet, because of your meddling.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You're right, of course."
entries.text: You're right, of course.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "This place, this hotel. It's not ju..."
entries.text: This place, this hotel. It's not just a business - for the staff, it is our home.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And if Miss Deane's situation had g..."
entries.text: And if Miss Deane's situation had gotten out, we would most assuredly be in trouble.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "But there might be another way, one..."
entries.text: But there might be another way, one that frees us from the fate of this séance...

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...at present, mainly this letter...."
entries.text: ...at present, mainly this letter. But once I ask around I should soon learn it there is somethi--

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And on what authority are you carry..."
entries.text: And on what authority are you carrying out this investigation?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was asked to come here and ensure..."
entries.text: I was asked to come here and ensure Miss Deane is okay.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I see. And what makes you think she..."
entries.text: I see. And what makes you think she is not?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I have no choice but to ask you to..."
entries.text: I have no choice but to ask you to leave. Go.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I... Nothing official..."
entries.text: I... Nothing official...

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Well then. I cannot have you interf..."
entries.text: Well then. I cannot have you interfering with this event, worrying our guests with idle speculation when they are trying to focus their minds.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Cash - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You can settle any charges at the f..."
entries.text: You can settle any charges at the front desk, Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ OFFER MONEY ]"
entries.text: [ OFFER MONEY ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ KEEP MONEY ]"
entries.text: [ KEEP MONEY ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'll hold onto this for now."
entries.text: I'll hold onto this for now.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Photograph of Miss Deane - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Ah. Miss Evelyn Deane. Taken in our..."
entries.text: Ah. Miss Evelyn Deane. Taken in our drawing room, I think.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You may deposit your luggage on the..."
entries.text: You may deposit your luggage on the rack to my right.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You may deposit your luggage on the..."
entries.text: You may deposit your luggage on the rack in the lobby.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Our porter will then bring it to yo..."
entries.text: Our porter will then bring it to your room when ready.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "I am sorry about the late hour..."
entries.text: I am sorry about the late hour...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I am sorry about the late hour... I..."
entries.text: I am sorry about the late hour... I misjudged the time needed for the journey.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It happens often enough. If we'd kn..."
entries.text: It happens often enough. If we'd known you were coming, we would have been happy to send the coach out for you.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "The driver knows the route well eno..."
entries.text: The driver knows the route well enough to take some time off the trip.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Perhaps for my departure."
entries.text: Perhaps for my departure.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Perhaps."
entries.text: Perhaps.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It happens often enough. Though usu..."
entries.text: It happens often enough. Though usually not so late in the day.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Our driver knows the routes well. H..."
entries.text: Our driver knows the routes well. He would shorten your return trip.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I will keep that in mind, thanks."
entries.text: I will keep that in mind, thanks.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If you intend on some sightseeing w..."
entries.text: If you intend on some sightseeing while in the area, our stablemaster is on hand to bring you around.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "What amenities does the hotel offer..."
entries.text: What amenities does the hotel offer?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about the hote..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about the hotel's amenities?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are se..."
entries.text: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are served in the dining room.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And usually, we have the telegraph..."
entries.text: And usually, we have the telegraph room for communication. I am sure it will be repaired soon.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "There is a well-stocked library, a..."
entries.text: There is a well-stocked library, a bar, and a drawing room for relaxation, which includes a variety of games and records for your entertainment.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Sadly, the bathhouse is closed at t..."
entries.text: Sadly, the bathhouse is closed at this time of year. The water is too cold to heat.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "Is there anything else out here?"
entries.text: Is there anything else out here?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there much to do outside the man..."
entries.text: Is there much to do outside the manor?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Refreshments can be requested on th..."
entries.text: Refreshments can be requested on the patio. Many of our guests enjoy walking the grounds, and there is a Hedgemaze for your enjoyment. Mister Hunter also offers horse riding sessions, though I believe those are now booked out.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "But if you're asking if there is an..."
entries.text: But if you're asking if there is anything outside of the grounds, no. Gauford, the town you took the carriage from, is our closest point of contact.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I'm afraid this is not Dublin."
entries.text: I'm afraid this is not Dublin.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Of course."
entries.text: Of course.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I am sure you will find the hotel o..."
entries.text: I am sure you will find the hotel offers everything you could need during your stay with us.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Finally, we now have the telegraph..."
entries.text: Finally, we now have the telegraph room up and running again, should you wish to reach out to friends or family.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Asking to write telegram - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister Varley, could I ask you to s..."
entries.text: Mister Varley, could I ask you to send a telegram on my behalf?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Certainly."
entries.text: Certainly.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Who is the recipient, and what is t..."
entries.text: Who is the recipient, and what is the message?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The local carriage service, to ask..."
entries.text: The local carriage service, to ask if their services were employed by someone here late last Tuesday.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "... I see."
entries.text: ... I see.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Do you need another message sent?"
entries.text: Do you need another message sent?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I do not. Thank you."
entries.text: I do not. Thank you.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Do you need a telegram sent, Mister..."
entries.text: Do you need a telegram sent, Mister Ward?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Not right now, no."
entries.text: Not right now, no.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Follow me."
entries.text: Follow me.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Telegram results - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "There."
entries.text: There.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "The carriage service says that they..."
entries.text: The carriage service says that they received no message from us on Tuesday evening or night.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If that's all, I have work to do."
entries.text: If that's all, I have work to do.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/washer woman - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I can assure you that our facility..."
entries.text: I can assure you that our facility has a full laundry. Nothing is washed in the fountain.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You will think me quite mad, Mister..."
entries.text: You will think me quite mad, Mister Varley, but I saw a woman washing something in the fountain.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Perhaps you saw... a bean nigh?"
entries.text: Perhaps you saw... a bean nigh?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It would be fitting for the time of..."
entries.text: It would be fitting for the time of year and the gathering here - though unfortunate for whoever's clothes were being washed.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "...there are entries on the bean ni..."
entries.text: ...there are entries on the bean nigh in the library, along with many more potential apparitions.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Séance flyer - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It looks like you've gone to some t..."
entries.text: It looks like you've gone to some trouble with this event.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "This séance is the first of its kin..."
entries.text: This séance is the first of its kind. It seemed prudent to put some expense into the event.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you follow these sort of spiritu..."
entries.text: Do you follow these sort of spiritualist beliefs yourself?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "No. I simply run the hotel. Such no..."
entries.text: No. I simply run the hotel. Such notions are beyond my station.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What makes this séance distinct fro..."
entries.text: What makes this séance distinct from any other?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "A typical séance allows only limite..."
entries.text: A typical séance allows only limited communication with a ghost. Limited in that a medium is needed - a host, a device, et cetera.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It's believed that, at the right ti..."
entries.text: It's believed that, at the right time of year, with the right collection of people gathered, a more direct form of communication could be achieved.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "As I say, that is the belief. Wheth..."
entries.text: As I say, that is the belief. Whether you believe it, Mister Ward, is up to you.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you really suppose this séance w..."
entries.text: Do you really suppose this séance will be distinct from any other?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Well, I simply run the hotel and wo..."
entries.text: Well, I simply run the hotel and would not be the best source for an in-depth explanation, but I will try my best.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And so those people have been gathe..."
entries.text: And so those people have been gathered here at Samhain, where and when the veil is thinnest, to see if that is true.

entries.label: Ward: "I saw that a Miss Deane signed in a..."
entries.text: I saw that a Miss Deane signed in about a week ago.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I do not wish to discuss another gu..."
entries.text: I do not wish to discuss another guest's affairs, Mister Ward.

entries.text: We use such a guide to translate telegrams via the telegraph machine.

entries.text: Where did you find that?

entries.text: It had fallen to the floor in the lobby.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley

entries.text: I see. Well, I'll make sure that Miss Barbosa receives it.

entries.text: It's quite the statue you have out in the courtyard.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Indeed. It's been there almost as l..."
entries.text: Indeed. It's been there almost as long as the house itself. Though what the subject is, I am unsure.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The portraits in the hallway, they'..."
entries.text: The portraits in the hallway, they're all of the same Blake line?

entries.text: They're of Marquess Blake's ancestors, yes.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If the ancestry intrigues you, you..."
entries.text: If the ancestry intrigues you, you might ask the Marquess himself. He would know best.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Edward Blake was the one to build t..."
entries.text: Edward Blake was the one to build this manor, over two hundred years ago.

entries.text: So Miss Deane left a letter excusing herself?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "She did. She is, after all, free to..."
entries.text: She did. She is, after all, free to do as she likes.

entries.text: So Miss Deane isn't here anymore?

entries.label: Varley: "She left her payment and a letter e..."
entries.text: She left her payment and a letter excusing herself last Tuesday evening.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "She didn't sign out in person?"
entries.text: She didn't sign out in person?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I would assume she meant to, but ha..."
entries.text: I would assume she meant to, but had to leave at an hour when no one was attending the front desk.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Manor contemporary history - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about the mano..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about the manor?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Well, it was built in the mid 1600s..."
entries.text: Well, it was built in the mid 1600s on land awarded to Edward Blake for his part in the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Marquess Jonathan Blake is the late..."
entries.text: Marquess Jonathan Blake is the latest in the line to hold the title, with him and his son, young Master Walter, being the last two members of the line.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It has since been passed down throu..."
entries.text: It has since been passed down through the generations of the Blake family and has survived any number of tragedies.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "That's all I could say, though I su..."
entries.text: That's all I could say, though I suspect there is more information in the library, should you care for more.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "It was the Marquess' initiative to..."
entries.text: It was the Marquess' initiative to open the manor as a hotel in 1870 to pull the place through the difficult post-famine years.

entries.text: Do you happen to get reports of... ghosts, from your guests?

entries.label: Varley: "If you mean to tell me you've seen..."
entries.text: If you mean to tell me you've seen some waif wandering the halls, or a figure in the garden, you would not be the first.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "The manor seems to inspire that sor..."
entries.text: The manor seems to inspire that sort of story.

entries.text: Do you really suppose this séance will be distinct from any other?

entries.text: ... As I say, that is the belief. Whether you believe it, Mister Ward, is up to you.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Soiled telegram - Varley

entries.label: Varley: "Where did you get this? And what on..."
entries.text: Where did you get this? And what on Earth happened to it?

entries.label: Ward: "It was on the floor of the lobby. I..."
entries.text: It was on the floor of the lobby. I assume it had fallen off the front desk.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "But where did the ink... Ugh. Thank..."
entries.text: But where did the ink... Ugh. Thank you, Mister Ward. I'll... see about this.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Another Blake - Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "One of the other guests mentioned m..."
entries.text: One of the other guests mentioned meeting another Blake in London. Would you happen to know of any of the Blake's relations in the city?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I wouldn't. The family's business i..."
entries.text: I wouldn't. The family's business is, with respect, not my concern.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Besides, I imagine there are a grea..."
entries.text: Besides, I imagine there are a great many Blakes unrelated to this Blake family.

title: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Ritual markings - Varley

entries.text: You know, I found some evidence of a ritual upstairs. In the room that was Miss Deane's?

entries.label: Varley: "You did? Ugh, as if there weren't e..."
entries.text: You did? Ugh, as if there weren't enough places for such things... I'll see that it's cleared up.

entries.text: Mister O'Meara tells me he saw Miss Deane late Tuesday night, and that he had the impression she'd been drinking, at that.

entries.label: Varley: "I cannot speak to what Mister O'Mea..."
entries.text: I cannot speak to what Mister O'Meara did or did not see... but I will not discuss any gossip about the guests.

entries.text: I certainly hope that's not the case. I'll double-check that it's not around here somewhere just as soon as I'm able.
