entries.text: Gone missing? Don't be absurd, man. She probably took a turn before she left - you know how women are.

title: Cast/Michael Skerritt/Evidence Presents - Skerritt/resolution - skerritt

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "It does not give me the same clearn..."
entries.text: It does not give me the same clearness of path as my original plans did.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "How do you feel about your decision..."
entries.text: How do you feel about your decision?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But... there is relief in no longer..."
entries.text: But... there is relief in no longer facing my end at the séance tomorrow evening.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But... there is relief in no longer..."
entries.text: But... there is relief in no longer facing my end at the séance tonight.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Perhaps I was too eager for a grand..."
entries.text: Perhaps I was too eager for a grand gesture. A final attempt at success.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I think Miss Deane saw my pain and..."
entries.text: I think Miss Deane saw my pain and guided me as best she could.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But she and I are from a world obli..."
entries.text: But she and I are from a world oblivious to the suffering that exists out there - a world perhaps too caught up in the metaphysical, and not concerned enough with this very real existence and its hardships.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "You, Sir, have given me another pat..."
entries.text: You, Sir, have given me another path. I will follow it earnestly and see where it leads.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "At least, for now, it feels promisi..."
entries.text: At least, for now, it feels promising. It feels good.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I think this is a better path to my..."
entries.text: I think this is a better path to my goal.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "It's not that far from what I do af..."
entries.text: It's not that far from what I do after all, except - and this is the funny bit - you don't expect the loan to be paid back.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I grew up thinking of that as a han..."
entries.text: I grew up thinking of that as a hand-out.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But now, I see it as a transaction...."
entries.text: But now, I see it as a transaction. I pay money to buy legacy.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Oh, don't look at me like that, Mis..."
entries.text: Oh, don't look at me like that, Mister Ward. The Catholics have been buying their way into heaven for centuries - this is the same thing but in a different hat.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "An old leopard can't change his spo..."
entries.text: An old leopard can't change his spots. At least, not right away.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But who knows, maybe my mind will l..."
entries.text: But who knows, maybe my mind will lead and heart follow.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And, if we all get our needs met, w..."
entries.text: And, if we all get our needs met, who cares what the underlying intention is, eh?

title: Cast/Michael Skerritt/Evidence Presents - Skerritt/legacy - Skerritt

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Ahhh..."
entries.text: Ahhh...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Dare I say, Mister Skerritt, you mu..."
entries.text: Dare I say, Mister Skerritt, you must have built some legacy over the years!

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Well... a fellow at my stage always..."
entries.text: Well... a fellow at my stage always thinks that maybe he could do more...

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I am the last of my line, you see...."
entries.text: I am the last of my line, you see. An only child who has had the misfortune to outlive whatever distant relatives I once had.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Of course, I have many friends and..."
entries.text: Of course, I have many friends and achieved no small success in business and brotherhoods I cannot mention.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And I have tried to further the eso..."
entries.text: And I have tried to further the esoteric studies as best as I could

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I think that is what really excites..."
entries.text: I think that is what really excites me about this séance - everyone is so focused on hearing a ghost, any ghost, speak.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Whereas I am fascinated by who the..."
entries.text: Whereas I am fascinated by who the ghost will be.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "To us, it does not matter - yet. We..."
entries.text: To us, it does not matter - yet. We're not summoning a specific ghost, you see. We're going to reach out and grab the closest.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And keep doing so until we find one..."
entries.text: And keep doing so until we find one who will talk to us.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And that ghost, tens - perhaps hund..."
entries.text: And that ghost, tens - perhaps hundreds - of years after their death, will suddenly be a star!

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "We will all want to know their back..."
entries.text: We will all want to know their background, their life - in death, they will be famous! Forever!

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Entire teams will dig into their pa..."
entries.text: Entire teams will dig into their past - their death, their life. Books will be written on them, and their first words from beyond the grave will be immortalised.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "We will all want to know their back..."
entries.text: We will all want to know their background, their life - in death, they will be famous! Forever!

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "A lot of pressure, then, to make su..."
entries.text: A lot of pressure, then, to make sure the name Skerritt carries on once my time comes...

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Now that is a legacy worth dying fo..."
entries.text: Now that is a legacy worth dying for!

entries.text: Haha, don't worry. It was a bit much even for me, and I've been to a few. Usually, one knows everyone at such a party, so there is more trust.

entries.label: Skerritt: "You'll get accustomed to this kind..."
entries.text: You'll get accustomed to this kind of thing, once you spend enough time with the sort of people worth knowing.

entries.label: Ward: "I've found I've had the strangest d..."
entries.text: I've found I've had the strangest dreams since coming here. Have you noticed anything of the sort?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But... Yes, I do dream that I am wa..."
entries.text: But... Yes, I do dream that I am walking these passageways. Seeking... Well, what I am seeking doesn't matter to you.

entries.label: Skerritt: "The strangest thing is that I can w..."
entries.text: The strangest thing is that I can walk properly in them - hahaha!

entries.text: I cannot figure out how to pass them, so I am trapped until I wake, which feels as if it takes time I do not have.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But there are doors - magical doors..."
entries.text: But there are doors - magical doors.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "That's what my dreams feel like, an..."
entries.text: That's what my dreams feel like, anyway.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt

entries.text: But... not one's earthly home. A call back to Our Lord's divine palace.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "You mean, a strange calling to home..."
entries.text: You mean, a strange calling to home?

entries.text: I can't say I have - I'm not much of a scholar.

entries.text: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

entries.text: She's in... Oh... It's slipped my mind, old chap!

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt

entries.text: I'm fairly sure her old paramour, O'Meara, was by her?

title: Cast/Michael Skerritt/Evidence Presents - Skerritt/skerritt's cards - skerritt

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I drew some tarot cards for myself,..."
entries.text: I drew some tarot cards for myself, but I cannot make out the meaning.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And you want my help? Naturally, of..."
entries.text: And you want my help? Naturally, of course. Tell me, then - what cards did you draw?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "And the message is clear - the card..."
entries.text: And the message is clear - the cards are saying there is an important moment in our futures. One in which we can greatly influence things to come, but at some great cost to ourselves.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Will we make that sacrifice when th..."
entries.text: Will we make that sacrifice when the time comes? That is hard to know but speaking for myself, I intend to!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "'The Hanged Man', the 'Ten of Penta..."
entries.text: 'The Hanged Man', the 'Ten of Pentacles', and the 'Death' card... Is that... good?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "By Jove! I've had a similar spread..."
entries.text: By Jove! I've had a similar spread myself recently.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Great cost? Is that what the 'Death..."
entries.text: Great cost? Is that what the 'Death' card implies - the cost of one's life?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Well, it's not always that literal..."
entries.text: Well, it's not always that literal - but it's certainly one interpretation, yes!

title: Cast/Michael Skerritt/Evidence Presents - Skerritt/philanthropy part 2 - skerritt

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "But there is another way to interpr..."
entries.text: But there is another way to interpret it: Instead of sacrificing your life, your remaining time - sacrifice your money.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You have so much wealth, so many co..."
entries.text: You have so much wealth, so many connections - you could really do some good with the time you have left.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mary Blake - she undertook numerous..."
entries.text: Mary Blake - she undertook numerous charitable deeds and has statues erected for her. And more than that, people speak fondly of her.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "She is remembered and loved."
entries.text: She is remembered and loved.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You have the resources to do the sa..."
entries.text: You have the resources to do the same - don't throw your life away. Refocus it. Do some good in this world. Finally.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Marchioness Blake's good reputation..."
entries.text: Marchioness Blake's good reputation did reach as far as London, and was mourned even there as a result...

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I... suppose there has been a gap t..."
entries.text: I... suppose there has been a gap to be filled since her passing. Perhaps I can do something to help there.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "It is a better bet than death..."
entries.text: It is a better bet than death...

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I know about the tarot reading that..."
entries.text: I know about the tarot reading that you received, and I know how you interpreted it.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "...You make a compelling case, Mist..."
entries.text: ...You make a compelling case, Mister Ward. But... would people not see it as disingenuous?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Genuine or not, you can make a much..."
entries.text: Genuine or not, you can make a much-needed difference. And that will be celebrated - you will be celebrated.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And perhaps along the way, you will..."
entries.text: And perhaps along the way, you will find you actually enjoy the good work.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "When I return home, I will reach ou..."
entries.text: When I return home, I will reach out to any foundations that suffered from the Marchioness' death and loss of funding.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "...Hmmm..."
entries.text: ...Hmmm...

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Alright, so! I gave you my word, an..."
entries.text: Alright, so! I gave you my word, and I stand by it now.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "This could bloody well work, you kn..."
entries.text: This could bloody well work, you know! Good chap!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "..."

entries.text: Do you know much about the strange device in the atrium?

entries.text: Ah yes. A spirit gauge, I think? Monitors the amount of spectral activity in the area. More ghosts, better séance.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt

entries.text: ...is that right?

title: Cast/Michael Skerritt/Evidence Presents - Skerritt/dagger - skerritt

entries.label: Skerritt: "Had a few glasses, have you, Mister..."
entries.text: Had a few glasses, have you, Mister Ward? Ready to set the world's wrongs to right, eh?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Are you... are you ready for the en..."
entries.text: Are you... are you ready for the end, Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "It's quite alright. It doesn't both..."
entries.text: It's quite alright. It doesn't bother me.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I onl--"
entries.text: I onl--

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I've had to face up to it, of cours..."
entries.text: I've had to face up to it, of course. I am not getting any younger.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "It absolutely terrified me, of cour..."
entries.text: It absolutely terrified me, of course. Death.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Whoever is ready? Really ready?"
entries.text: Whoever is ready? Really ready?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Well... I suppose I am. Now."
entries.text: Well... I suppose I am. Now.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "I spent a fortune looking for ways..."
entries.text: I spent a fortune looking for ways out. Mundane or magical.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "Sadly, not something money can buy."
entries.text: Sadly, not something money can buy.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "But in the pursuit of a spell, amul..."
entries.text: But in the pursuit of a spell, amulet, or ointment to buy myself more time, I met one of the other guests who is now here - Miss Evelyn Deane.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "We talked. She listened to me, gave..."
entries.text: We talked. She listened to me, gave me readings - she helped me realise what I was scared of.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "She convinced me that I didn't have..."
entries.text: She convinced me that I didn't have to be scared anymore. She showed me a path to controlling the fear.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt
entries.label: Skerritt: "So yes, thanks to her, I am ready f..."
entries.text: So yes, thanks to her, I am ready for the end.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa

entries.text: I... I was captured. Taken by the man who killed my mother.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa

entries.text: I do not know his plans for me.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And I had no intention in finding o..."

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I had no plan. I was lost. By the t..."
entries.text: I had no plan. I was lost. By the time I got to Rio, my face was on posters, so maybe not all of his people burned. A shame.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And so I started a fire. I would ra..."
entries.text: And so I started a fire. I would rather have died in a blaze than let him choose my fate.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "My captor and his crew were not so..."
entries.text: My captor and his crew were not so lucky. And good for them.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That is when I decided it was time..."
entries.text: That is when I decided it was time to leave Brazil. I go to the port a few hours later. There were posters there, too.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So I took one before I left. A souv..."
entries.text: So I took one before I left. A souvenir. A stupid, dangerous souvenir.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: I... hope that was a one time thing?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "The fire? Sim, it was just that one..."
entries.text: The fire? Sim, it was just that one time.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Good. I implore you to keep it that..."
entries.text: Good. I implore you to keep it that way. Otherwise, I will bring you in myself. Understood?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa

entries.text: ...Understood.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "..."

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "My mother, she was in prison. She l..."
entries.text: My mother, she was in prison. She liked the monarchy. I suppose it was what she grew up with. Ingrained.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So after the coup, she was on the w..."
entries.text: So after the coup, she was on the wrong side of things.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She was arrested. Then, after a few..."
entries.text: She was arrested. Then, after a few years, she became sick.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Also, I had no plan. I was caught e..."
entries.text: Also, I had no plan. I was caught escaping. I only got away because I bit the guard who found me.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Pneumonia. They did not even try to..."
entries.text: Pneumonia. They did not even try to treat her. They let her slowly die in prison.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So after she died, I set fire to th..."
entries.text: So after she died, I set fire to their prison.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have not done this kind of thing..."
entries.text: I have not done this kind of thing before, so it was not a good job. Only a little damage was done. Certainly, not enough.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That is when I decided it was time..."
entries.text: That is when I decided it was time to leave Rio. I go to the port a few hours later. The posters were up by then.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So I took one before I left. A souv..."
entries.text: So I took one before I left. A souvenir. A stupid, dangerous souvenir.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I... hope that was a one time thing..."
entries.text: I... hope that was a one time thing?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "The fire? Sim, it was just that one..."
entries.text: The fire? Sim, it was just that one time.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: Good. I implore you to keep it that way. Otherwise, I will bring you in myself. Understood?

entries.text: ...Understood.

entries.text: I thought this might be useful to you, Miss.

entries.text: What? But this is... There is so much detail here. Where did you get this?

entries.text: It's Miss Quinn's work. She's been researching the O'Connor family for a ritual she wants to conduct.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The woman she's focused on, a 'Bidd..."
entries.text: The woman she's focused on, a 'Biddy' Eve O'Connor, had a son who emigrated.

entries.label: Ward: "So, do you think she might borrow t..."
entries.text: So, do you think she might borrow that brooch of yours for her purpose? If she is right, it would not only help her but also confirm we have the right man.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Then how can I refuse? Come, let us..."
entries.text: Then how can I refuse? Come, let us find the Quinn woman.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It's research of the O'Connor famil..."
entries.text: It's research of the O'Connor family. I noticed it bears the same crest as your brooch.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It does not. But Miss Quinn says he..."
entries.text: It does not. But Miss Quinn says her ritual is a matter of life and death - and that she requires an item from that family.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was hoping you would check the da..."
entries.text: I was hoping you would check the date of his departure against that of your father?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes, yes, they line up."
entries.text: Yes, yes, they line up.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But his name is Seamus O'Connor, no..."
entries.text: But his name is Seamus O'Connor, not Shay. A cousin maybe?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Which, it turns out, may be your fa..."
entries.text: Which, it turns out, may be your family.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So this doesn't mean..."
entries.text: So this doesn't mean...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Hang on... I can't believe I didn't..."
entries.text: Hang on... I can't believe I didn't make the connection before now, but Shay is often used as shorthand for Seamus.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "So I have been looking for the wron..."
entries.text: So I have been looking for the wrong name?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It is possible, or we may have the..."
entries.text: It is possible, or we may have the wrong man altogether.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Wait, isn't Shay often used as shor..."
entries.text: Wait, isn't Shay often used as shorthand for Seamus?

entries.text: It would be nice to know he's nearby, even if it can only be for a little while.

entries.text: Really?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That's kind of you. It's kind of yo..."
entries.text: That's kind of you. It's kind of you both. I'll go and talk to him, thank you.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Family crest book - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found a book of family crests, an..."
entries.text: I found a book of family crests, and it would seem the crest on your brooch is the O'Connor family's.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That would make sense... meu mãezin..."
entries.text: That would make sense... meu mãezinha always said my father left it with her, after all.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "O'Connor? Shay O'Connor. That's......"
entries.text: O'Connor? Shay O'Connor. That's... It's good to know.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I'm just damn glad it really was a..."
entries.text: I'm just damn glad it really was a crest. That it was something. Not just some dead end, or worse, wishful thinking.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Thank you, Mister Ward. This is goo..."
entries.text: Thank you, Mister Ward. This is good to know.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I thought you might like to take a..."
entries.text: I thought you might like to take a look at this.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Hm? Why's that, then?"
entries.text: Hm? Why's that, then?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ SHOW HER THE O'CONNOR CREST ]"
entries.text: [ SHOW HER THE O'CONNOR CREST ]

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That's interesting, I suppose... bu..."
entries.text: That's interesting, I suppose... but it doesn't mean anything to me.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That's interesting, I suppose... bu..."
entries.text: That's interesting, I suppose... but it doesn't mean anything to me. I'm not sure it's got anything to do with me.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I'm not only here for this séance,..."
entries.text: I'm not only here for this séance, you know. In the country, I mean. My father's side of the family is Irish, or that's what my mother told me.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I wanted to see where he came from...."
entries.text: I wanted to see where he came from... That sort of thing. The name O'Connor... it is a start.

entries.text: [ SHOW HER THE O'CONALEIGH CREST ]

entries.text: [ SHOW HER THE O'DEORAIN CREST ]

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Land Records - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does this book mean anything to you..."
entries.text: Does this book mean anything to you?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I was reading it, looking for infor..."
entries.text: I was reading it, looking for information on the families that used to live around here.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Quinn gave it to me, but it was no..."
entries.text: Quinn gave it to me, but it was no help. Still, she was good to offer it.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Shay O'Connor - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Now you know your father's real nam..."
entries.text: Now you know your father's real name.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And now I know my grandmother's nam..."
entries.text: And now I know my grandmother's name, too - Eve.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I am Ines Eva Barbosa. A tribute to..."
entries.text: I am Ines Eva Barbosa. A tribute to her, perhaps?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "For what she has done for me this d..."
entries.text: For what she has done for me this day, I will certainly carry on as if that were true.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. Seamus - ironically like the p..."
entries.text: Yes. Seamus - ironically like the porter who annoys me so much.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "My mother said my father was also a..."
entries.text: My mother said my father was also an annoying gringo - cheeky, she said. But she said it with a twinkle in her eye.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She never really let him go, I thin..."
entries.text: She never really let him go, I think...

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Ghost Photography Machine- Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor Callaghan has a camera that..."
entries.text: Doctor Callaghan has a camera that he's modified for taking pictures of spirits.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "A camera can do that? I was right -..."
entries.text: A camera can do that? I was right - this is a house of miracles.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Have you asked him how it works? Wo..."
entries.text: Have you asked him how it works? Would it... work for my father?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I could ask him."
entries.text: I could ask him.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Obrigada."
entries.text: Obrigada.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/O'Connor Family Crest - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The O'Connor family has a crest, as..."
entries.text: The O'Connor family has a crest, as it turns out: one with a tree in its centre.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "A tree? Do you suppose that... Migh..."
entries.text: A tree? Do you suppose that... Might my brooch have one belonged to the O'Connors?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Maybe that's wishful thinking..."
entries.text: Maybe that's wishful thinking...

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Hedonistic Gala - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That was... quite the party."
entries.text: That was... quite the party.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "When I was told to bring something..."
entries.text: When I was told to bring something to wear for the ball, I joked it would be like Carnaval.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Then to find I was not too wrong -..."
entries.text: Then to find I was not too wrong - Valha-me Deus!

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I almost expected it to end in rutt..."
entries.text: I almost expected it to end in rutting!

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I... went looking for Ó Finn but he..."
entries.text: I... went looking for Ó Finn but he seemed to leave early. A shame.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Unknown Sigil - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've seen a drawing around, of... i..."
entries.text: I've seen a drawing around, of... it looks like some sort of a rune to me. A spiral, with four lines intersecting it. Do you know what it is?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Can't say I do. Have you tried aski..."
entries.text: Can't say I do. Have you tried asking one of the scholars? I mean, it has to be something magic, right?

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Sketches of Strange Symbol - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does this symbol mean anything to y..."
entries.text: Does this symbol mean anything to you? I found a drawing of it.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "That doesn't look like much of anyt..."
entries.text: That doesn't look like much of anything to me. It doesn't look like any sort of written word, even. Like...

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Ai, what's the word in English? Thi..."
entries.text: Ai, what's the word in English? This is much too specific for me to know.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "When a picture represents something..."
entries.text: When a picture represents something, you know? Or maybe it's just made up. You never know.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Deane's room - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I don't suppose you know which room..."
entries.text: I don't suppose you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She was -"
entries.text: She was -

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "No, wait. I thought.... Hm. I can't..."
entries.text: No, wait. I thought.... Hm. I can't remember.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Funny. I went there to... get somet..."
entries.text: Funny. I went there to... get something back, but now I cannot recall where it is...

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/timetable - Ines

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I will spend some time in the teleg..."
entries.text: I will spend some time in the telegraph room. It is peaceful there, even when I'm not waiting on a message.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I will spend the morning recovering..."
entries.text: I will spend the morning recovering from the party, I think.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What are your plans for this weeken..."
entries.text: What are your plans for this weekend, Miss Barbosa?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you have any plans for today?"
entries.text: Do you have any plans for today?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "There or thereabouts - I like the l..."
entries.text: There or thereabouts - I like the lobby or atrium, too. There you see people's comings and goings.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I'm meeting Dupré in the gardens at..."
entries.text: I'm meeting Dupré in the gardens at twelve. Then I will see Fiadh's talk at three. I think she will spend it telling everyone they are wrong to be here - that I want to see.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "After that, I will rest in my room..."
entries.text: After that, I will rest in my room before Mantovani talks at five, which I intend to see - maybe it can make some sense of all this!

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Except, gah! There is mass at twelv..."
entries.text: Except, gah! There is mass at twelve.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "...And then there's the silent dinn..."
entries.text: ...And then there's the silent dinner at eight. What to expect from it and the séance? I do not know.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I think I'll take an hour in my roo..."
entries.text: I think I'll take an hour in my room beforehand, I think, to prepare myself.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "After which is dinner, then the mas..."
entries.text: After which is dinner, then the masked ball. Imagine my surprise to find a mini Carnaval here! Then on Sunday...

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Mister Coventry's talk at five, I w..."
entries.text: Mister Coventry's talk at five, I will go to. Before that, lunch.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "...And then there's the silent dinn..."
entries.text: ...And then there's the silent dinner at eight. What to expect from it, I do not know.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Then after that, I'll go to my room..."
entries.text: Then after that, I'll go to my room for the night and leave you all to your séance.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/End of quest - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you think you'll do when th..."
entries.text: What do you think you'll do when the séance is over?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I only hoped to learn my father's n..."
entries.text: I only hoped to learn my father's name - but to see him!

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have what I came for and more."
entries.text: I have what I came for and more.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And I like it here... I like knowin..."
entries.text: And I like it here... I like knowing that I am in my father's homeland - and I have met some people that I might one day call 'friends'.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Forever? Who knows. This event has..."
entries.text: Forever? Who knows. This event has changed my world, and I need time to process all of that.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And now I have the inheritance from..."
entries.text: And now I have the inheritance from Corentine. This is more than the fresh start I came here hoping for.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But all that matters is right now,..."
entries.text: But all that matters is right now, yes? And right now, I'm happy here. I have answers and a home. I cannot ask for more.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Death certificate - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you have much in the way of fami..."
entries.text: Do you have much in the way of family back home?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "None. My mother was an escaped slav..."
entries.text: None. My mother was an escaped slave. She raised me in a Quilombo.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I lived there my whole life - almos..."
entries.text: I lived there my whole life - almost entirely not leaving until slavery was abolished in 1888. Even then, we were slow to trust the outside.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But last year, my mother and I went..."
entries.text: But last year, my mother and I went to Rio to see Christmas there. She was nervous, but I, I was excited!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'm sorry to hear that. It's not lo..."
entries.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It's not long since I lost my last remaining family.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There is a certain type of loneline..."
entries.text: There is a certain type of loneliness in having no family that no friendship or lover can remove.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. I feel... adrift in the world...."
entries.text: Yes. I feel... adrift in the world. Maybe someday I will find something good in that freedom. But... not yet.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She was all I had and, now, she is..."
entries.text: She was all I had and, now, she is dead.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There is a certain type of loneline..."
entries.text: There is a certain type of loneliness in having no family that no friendship or lover can remove.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. I feel... adrift in the world...."
entries.text: Yes. I feel... adrift in the world. Maybe someday I will find something good in that freedom. But... not yet.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "None. My mother bedded a gringo, so..."
entries.text: None. My mother bedded a gringo, so she was cut off from her people.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He then went off to war and died."
entries.text: He then went off to war and died.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'm sorry to hear that. It's not lo..."
entries.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It's not long since I lost my last remaining family.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "We ate oranges and sugared nuts. De..."
entries.text: We ate oranges and sugared nuts. Despite the heat, we even tried a mulled wine.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "As a gift we took a photograph. I a..."
entries.text: As a gift we took a photograph. I am glad we did. It is all I have left of her.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "A man saw us that day, a Captain of..."
entries.text: A man saw us that day, a Captain of the Forest who had run-ins with my mother and her camp.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "His job was to recapture slaves, ba..."
entries.text: His job was to recapture slaves, back when slavery was in full force.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Bitter at having never found our se..."
entries.text: Bitter at having never found our settlement, he followed us back that day.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Then he returned that night with so..."
entries.text: Then he returned that night with some friends, all of them drunk.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "They began to shoot up the place, k..."
entries.text: They began to shoot up the place, killing many - including my mother.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Those they did not kill, they captu..."
entries.text: Those they did not kill, they captured. And so my home was destroyed, and my family killed and scattered.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "My Lord! That is awful!"
entries.text: My Lord! That is awful!

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/Father's Ghost - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You hope to see your father's ghost..."
entries.text: You hope to see your father's ghost?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. And why not? This is a house o..."
entries.text: Yes. And why not? This is a house of miracles, no?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Before coming here, I had no money,..."
entries.text: Before coming here, I had no money, no land, and only a nickname for my father.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Maybe if I keep asking, this house..."
entries.text: Maybe if I keep asking, this house will keep giving?

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/gauge - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you noticed the strange device..."
entries.text: Have you noticed the strange device in the atrium?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Of course, of course. It is made si..."
entries.text: Of course, of course. It is made similar to the odd contraption in the telegraph room. Perhaps they are both made locally?

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Evidence Presents - Ines/washer woman - ines

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Sim, but that is one of the staff,..."
entries.text: Sim, but that is one of the staff, no? What is her name, Caitlin?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "This might sound strange, but have..."
entries.text: This might sound strange, but have you seen a woman on the grounds? Washing clothes?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I called out to her to see what she..."
entries.text: I called out to her to see what she was washing in the horse's trough, but she did not reply.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I left her to it, I do not know the..."
entries.text: I left her to it, I do not know the customs of this place.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Ivy - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss McLeod?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss McLeod?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I talked to her and her chaperone -..."
entries.text: I talked to her and her chaperone - a grown woman with a chaperone!

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I do not know what to make of these..."
entries.text: I do not know what to make of these noble types, but that is new to me.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Varley - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to the manager?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to the manager?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "There was no one to talk to but the..."
entries.text: There was no one to talk to but the staff when I first arrived, so yes.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I think this job, this event, is ha..."
entries.text: I think this job, this event, is hard on him. I could see his demeanour darken as the week rolled on.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I stopped asking him for help with..."
entries.text: I stopped asking him for help with my telegrams to give him, um, space. But then I got stuck dealing with the idiot boy, Mister Doyle.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Lan Fen - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Missus Lau?"
entries.text: Have you met Missus Lau?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Imagine a person like her watching..."
entries.text: Imagine a person like her watching your every move. She is like the McLeod girl's shadow.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She would be hard to get anything p..."
entries.text: She would be hard to get anything passed, I think, and God help anyone who does.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I see a fire in her. I think she co..."
entries.text: I see a fire in her. I think she could do regrettable things to protect her charge.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Skerritt - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Mister Skerritt?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He asked me about the Amazon and ho..."
entries.text: He asked me about the Amazon and how deep in it I lived.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I am thousands of miles away from i..."
entries.text: I am thousands of miles away from it. I have never been. I do not think he meant offence, he is just old and ignorant.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Corentine - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had the opportunity to tal..."
entries.text: Have you had the opportunity to talk to Miss Quinn?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "The girl with the books, yes?"
entries.text: The girl with the books, yes?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Briefly -  we sat together at a mea..."
entries.text: Briefly -  we sat together at a meal.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I mentioned my father was Irish, an..."
entries.text: I mentioned my father was Irish, and she gave me a book of local records. A strange gesture, maybe, but not a bad one.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Caitlin - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to the housekeeper?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to the housekeeper?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Bumped into her sweeping once. She..."
entries.text: Bumped into her sweeping once. She had all sorts of questions. More than usual, I mean.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Less than you, though."
entries.text: Less than you, though.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I did not mind it. I have been here..."
entries.text: I did not mind it. I have been here a while. Overbearing conversation is still conversation.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Darragh - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met the stable master?"
entries.text: Have you met the stable master?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He brought me here in the carriage,..."
entries.text: He brought me here in the carriage, so yes. And I see him around the grounds.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have asked him about the area, bu..."
entries.text: I have asked him about the area, but he is Scottish and does not know the history. I thought it was just a thick Irish accent.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He was not offended. Your people ar..."
entries.text: He was not offended. Your people are close enough, he says.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Anyway, a pleasant sort."
entries.text: Anyway, a pleasant sort.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Seamus - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know much about the porter?"
entries.text: Do you know much about the porter?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I know he is bad at this job! He is..."
entries.text: I know he is bad at this job! He is too busy fawning over that witch, Deane, to get anything right.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Ah... I should not be too hard on h..."
entries.text: Ah... I should not be too hard on him - his eyes are glassy and sad like the people I hid with on the boat out of Brazil.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Of course, he'd fall for anything t..."
entries.text: Of course, he'd fall for anything to offer him a distraction.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He should get out of here, it is no..."
entries.text: He should get out of here, it is not good for him.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Ines - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Tell me about yourself, Miss Barbos..."
entries.text: Tell me about yourself, Miss Barbosa.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "What is there to tell?"
entries.text: What is there to tell?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have already told you I am from R..."
entries.text: I have already told you I am from Rio. Well, I said Brazil, but Rio was my home.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I suppose I am a drifter, now. I ha..."
entries.text: I suppose I am a drifter, now. I have a drifted a long way, yes?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But home is different since the upr..."
entries.text: But home is different since the uprising. Mostly good but not all good. Isn't that the way of such things?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I decide, now is a good time to tra..."
entries.text: I decide, now is a good time to travel. See the world.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Cathal - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Mister O'Meara?"
entries.text: Have you met Mister O'Meara?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes, he tried to... hmm, what do yo..."
entries.text: Yes, he tried to... hmm, what do you call it... "woo" me?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I would break him worse than his ho..."
entries.text: I would break him worse than his horse riding accident.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But, I admire his confidence."
entries.text: But, I admire his confidence.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Ettiene - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Mister Toussaint..."
entries.text: Have you spoken to Mister Toussaint?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He has the most sense of anyone her..."
entries.text: He has the most sense of anyone here.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Open but questioning. I like that."
entries.text: Open but questioning. I like that.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He does not ask personal questions...."
entries.text: He does not ask personal questions. I like that even more.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Evelyn - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know Miss Deane?"
entries.text: Do you know Miss Deane?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "No more than I know you, but alread..."
entries.text: No more than I know you, but already I do not like her.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She knows too much, what business i..."
entries.text: She knows too much, what business is it of hers to know so much?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She is like, like a spy, or a thief..."
entries.text: She is like, like a spy, or a thief! Or maybe she has spies and thieves in her employ.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Whatever the case, she is a sneak t..."
entries.text: Whatever the case, she is a sneak to be watched!

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Dupré - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Mister Dupré?"
entries.text: Have you met Mister Dupré?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Oh yes. We have much in common, me..."
entries.text: Oh yes. We have much in common, me and him. He makes for easy company.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He knows so much about Irish cultur..."
entries.text: He knows so much about Irish culture and mythology but when I asked him about this area and those who lived here? He knows nothing practical, that man.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Still... he understands grief well."
entries.text: Still... he understands grief well.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on D'Arcy - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Missus D'Arcy?"
entries.text: Have you met Missus D'Arcy?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "A wicked woman. I like her a good d..."
entries.text: A wicked woman. I like her a good deal.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She pretends to be into ghosts and..."
entries.text: She pretends to be into ghosts and magic but she is a normal person, really.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Coventry - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Mister Coventry?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to Mister Coventry?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. He knows a good deal of this a..."
entries.text: Yes. He knows a good deal of this area and its history. I'm interested in that.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He is what I imagine talking to a g..."
entries.text: He is what I imagine talking to a grandfather is like - including the musty smell.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Hazel - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Missus Erickson?"
entries.text: Have you met Missus Erickson?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have. She's offered to give me a..."
entries.text: I have. She's offered to give me a private séance, but I do not want such a thing.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Ruairi - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Doctor Callaghan..."
entries.text: Have you spoken to Doctor Callaghan at all?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes and no. It was good to talk to..."
entries.text: Yes and no. It was good to talk to someone actually from the area.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "They gave me much advice and much t..."
entries.text: They gave me much advice and much to think about.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But I did not get much sense of the..."
entries.text: But I did not get much sense of the doctor himself in these talks. His aunt does not give him much room to be.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I asked him about his camera, but s..."
entries.text: I asked him about his camera, but she kept dismissing it as modern nonsense, so I learned nothing.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I hope he finds a way to get her of..."
entries.text: I hope he finds a way to get her off his back. It is not good to have bad relations with family.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Carmela - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Mantovani?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Mantovani?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Yes. I wanted to know more about th..."
entries.text: Yes. I wanted to know more about this séance, so I asked her.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She had more time for me than expec..."
entries.text: She had more time for me than expected. She is good with people.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And we talked about tarot, of cours..."
entries.text: And we talked about tarot, of course. When I told her I didn't want a reading, she laughed, and said that it was alright.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She said to enjoy the here and now,..."
entries.text: She said to enjoy the here and now, instead. With that, I agree.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Fiadh - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Callaghan?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Wherever you go - Brazil, Ireland,..."
entries.text: Wherever you go - Brazil, Ireland, anywhere - there's always aunties sticking their nose into things.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "But I cannot help but like these wo..."
entries.text: But I cannot help but like these women. Society says, "This is not for you, you are an old lady with old ideas."

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And they say, "Try, then, to keep m..."
entries.text: And they say, "Try, then, to keep me out".

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "My mother was not an aunt to anyone..."
entries.text: My mother was not an aunt to anyone, but in this way - she was an auntie.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Saoirse - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to the cook - Miss..."
entries.text: Have you spoken to the cook - Miss Murphy?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She is a quiet girl, so not much ta..."
entries.text: She is a quiet girl, so not much talking with her. She seemed upset that I am not one of your, eh, feiticeira. Eh, a magic... person.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I said to her, magic is done by liv..."
entries.text: I said to her, magic is done by living fully... taking the moments that come to us as openly as we can. Well, she did not care for that.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Arwa - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Miss Hisham?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to Miss Hisham?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have. I do not like her - she mak..."
entries.text: I have. I do not like her - she makes the hairs on the back of my neck stand up.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "It is not anything she does or says..."
entries.text: It is not anything she does or says. Just...

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I do not know what it is. If you to..."
entries.text: I do not know what it is. If you told me she was a ghost herself, I would almost believe you!

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Father Sinnott - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Father Sinnott?"
entries.text: Have you met Father Sinnott?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I am a Catholic; of course we have..."
entries.text: I am a Catholic; of course we have spoken! But what would a priest want from a thing like this?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Surely he, more than anyone, has en..."
entries.text: Surely he, more than anyone, has enough authority on what lies after death?

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Ó Finn - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I don't suppose you've spoken to Mi..."
entries.text: I don't suppose you've spoken to Mister Ó Finn?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "Am I going to ignore such a man as..."
entries.text: Am I going to ignore such a man as him? I do not think so.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And what a relief, to talk to a man..."
entries.text: And what a relief, to talk to a man with a sense of humour. I'm getting so tired of everyone being so polite.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Blake - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to the Marquess at..."
entries.text: Have you spoken to the Marquess at all?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I have. I wanted some guidance on t..."
entries.text: I have. I wanted some guidance on the history of this area, of the people from it.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He was polite but brief. Sent me to..."
entries.text: He was polite but brief. Sent me to the libraries, which was helpful but not very friendly.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Character Presents - Ines/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you aware that Marquess Blake..."
entries.text: Were you aware that Marquess Blake has a son?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "The boy in the paintings, yes?"
entries.text: The boy in the paintings, yes?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I don't suppose a child has much bu..."
entries.text: I don't suppose a child has much business being here. It is no wonder he is kept away from all of this.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Analysis Presents - (to) Ines/Foreign fashion - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I notice you're picking up some of..."
entries.text: I notice you're picking up some of the local fashion.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I left in a hurry and packed light."
entries.text: I left in a hurry and packed light.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "What would you have me do, freeze?"
entries.text: What would you have me do, freeze?

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Analysis Presents - (to) Ines/Irish keepsake - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Your brooch, it looks to carry a st..."
entries.text: Your brooch, it looks to carry a story?

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "It was my father's, or maybe his mo..."
entries.text: It was my father's, or maybe his mother's? He didn't bring much with him when he left Ireland.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "And he had even less on him the day..."
entries.text: And he had even less on him the day he died, defending my mother.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "My mother took this and ran. She pa..."
entries.text: My mother took this and ran. She passed it to me so I would have something of his.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "She kept it and gave it to me. It f..."
entries.text: She kept it and gave it to me. It feels right to wear it here.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "It was my father's, or maybe his mo..."
entries.text: It was my father's, or maybe his mother's? He didn't leave much when he went to fight, but he left this.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "He told my mother he would be back..."
entries.text: He told my mother he would be back for it, but he never returned. He did not make it out of Paraguay.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "gringo"
entries.text: gringo

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Analysis Presents - (to) Ines/Windburnt Skin - Ines

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I can see the weather here is not a..."
entries.text: I can see the weather here is not agreeing with you...

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "You can tell, eh? I'm not used to a..."
entries.text: You can tell, eh? I'm not used to all this wind and rain; it has more bite than the dogs back home.

title: Cast/Ines Barbosa/Ward in room - Ines

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "What the-?!"
entries.text: What the-?!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Barbosa-"
entries.text: Miss Barbosa-

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "No! There are enough strange things..."
entries.text: No! There are enough strange things creeping around the manor without you in the mix.

entries.speaker: Miss Barbosa
entries.label: Ines: "I'll be informing the manager of th..."
entries.text: I'll be informing the manager of this immediately.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Ettiene conversation

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Un moment, Monsieur?"
entries.text: Un moment, Monsieur?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Hello again, Monsieur Ward. Can I h..."
entries.text: Hello again, Monsieur Ward. Can I help you?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "LEAVE"
entries.text: LEAVE

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Take care, Monsieur."
entries.text: Take care, Monsieur.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That's all."
entries.text: That's all.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Choice: "CONFRONT!"
entries.text: CONFRONT!

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Quite right. Excellent."
entries.text: Quite right. Excellent.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I had planned to do it myself, but..."
entries.text: I had planned to do it myself, but once I saw you, I knew you would have to help, Detective...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "So you do know who I am?"
entries.text: So you do know who I am?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Indeed. I'm an investigator of my o..."
entries.text: Indeed. I'm an investigator of my own sort, you see? It would be foolish of me to enter a new country and not read the papers, n'est-ce pas?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "As for my own investigation, I have..."
entries.text: As for my own investigation, I have focused on Madame Hazel Erickson.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I'll get to the heart of it. She is..."
entries.text: I'll get to the heart of it. She is an out-and-out fraud. About this, I have no trace of a doubt.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "But... My belief alone is not quite..."
entries.text: But... My belief alone is not quite enough - I still lack evidence.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Here, take this key. It will let yo..."
entries.text: Here, take this key. It will let you into room 19, Madame Erickson's room. There you can find something that proves the case, of this I am sure.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What makes you think I'd do a thing..."
entries.text: What makes you think I'd do a thing like that?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "That's your job, is it not? And......"
entries.text: That's your job, is it not? And... you would want to keep your presence here quiet, no?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "You won't hear a thing further abou..."
entries.text: You won't hear a thing further about your presence once you have aided me.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Here - the key. I shall see you bac..."
entries.text: Here - the key. I shall see you back with evidence inside the hour, yes?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And how do you expect me to get int..."
entries.text: And how do you expect me to get into Missus Erickson's room safely?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I believe I heard her discussing he..."
entries.text: I believe I heard her discussing her plans with Monsieur Ó Finn. You might consider listening in...

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Allow me to even the playing field."
entries.text: Allow me to even the playing field.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I am Etienne Toussaint, a debunker..."
entries.text: I am Etienne Toussaint, a debunker of fraudulent mystics.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "And it is the topic of fraud I wish..."
entries.text: And it is the topic of fraud I wish to speak with you on...

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "You would be... Declan Ward, correc..."
entries.text: You would be... Declan Ward, correct?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That's all."
entries.text: That's all.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I think not, Monsieur. We are not d..."
entries.text: I think not, Monsieur. We are not done talking yet.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Otherwise... Well, I will have to m..."
entries.text: Otherwise... Well, I will have to make an announcement at breakfast. You'll be out not long after, I assure you.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Hauntings, eavesdrop

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "...But I thought you didn't believe..."
entries.text: ...But I thought you didn't believe in the whole idea? Ghosts, mystics - aren't you out for us and all our dealings?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Au contraire! I am quite the believ..."
entries.text: Au contraire! I am quite the believer. I think you would agree that disproving all this would be quite the task, eh?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I am sceptical - of this, you are c..."
entries.text: I am sceptical - of this, you are correct. I concern myself with the falsified cases - which I believe to be the majority of cases.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "But to deny it all? Especially in a..."
entries.text: But to deny it all? Especially in a place such as this? Impossible!

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "That is not what I want to hear! I..."
entries.text: That is not what I want to hear! I was hoping for assurances that it was all smoke and mirrors, as they say.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "But not the staff, even - some litt..."
entries.text: But not the staff, even - some little boy!

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "What I want from you is something a..."
entries.text: What I want from you is something about 'mould in the walls', making my brain rot to the point of hallucination.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Would a rotting brain be of more co..."
entries.text: Would a rotting brain be of more comfort, hmm?

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "...He was a very creepy child."
entries.text: ...He was a very creepy child.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "I could have sworn there was someon..."
entries.text: I could have sworn there was someone in my room last night, when I was almost asleep.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Photograph of Deane - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to recognise this wom..."
entries.text: Do you happen to recognise this woman?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "That would be Mademoiselle Evelyn D..."
entries.text: That would be Mademoiselle Evelyn Deane.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "She's attending the event, though I..."
entries.text: She's attending the event, though I haven't seen her for some time... Perhaps she's taken to her room?

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Séance advert - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think the séance's claims co..."
entries.text: Do you think the séance's claims could be true?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "That they can actually summon a gho..."
entries.text: That they can actually summon a ghost and talk to it directly?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "You ask the wrong man, Monsieur!"
entries.text: You ask the wrong man, Monsieur!

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "But many things were considered imp..."
entries.text: But many things were considered impossible until they were done, non?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I have witnessed many strange thing..."
entries.text: I have witnessed many strange things in my line of business. From what I know of her, if it can be done, then Mademoiselle Mantovani can do it.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Marriage talk - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've overheard it said that one of..."
entries.text: I've overheard it said that one of the young ladies here is hoping to find a suitor.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Here? What a thought... But I suppo..."
entries.text: Here? What a thought... But I suppose, one looks for those they have a kinship with, given the chance. Hm.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Well... Should it ever come up, I'l..."
entries.text: Well... Should it ever come up, I'll have to give the young lady my best wishes in the matter.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Telegram for Ines - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I'm something of an investigator, M..."
entries.text: I'm something of an investigator, Monsieur Ward, but I am decent about it.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "This is best delivered to the madem..."
entries.text: This is best delivered to the mademoiselle herself.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/The staff say Miss Deane left - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was talking to the staff, and the..."
entries.text: I was talking to the staff, and they said that Miss Deane checked out last Tuesday.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "They - she did? That seems... I don..."
entries.text: They - she did? That seems... I don't know the lady well myself, but that does seem out of character.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I do hope she's well..."
entries.text: I do hope she's well...

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Ghosts - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Increasingly, I think I see strange..."
entries.text: Increasingly, I think I see strange things around this manor.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "The power of suggestion will do thi..."
entries.text: The power of suggestion will do things to the mind, Monsieur Ward.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Figments of the imagination, perhap..."
entries.text: Figments of the imagination, perhaps, but perhaps we'd best err on the side of a believer for now, and leave them be, non?

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/The Séance's Purpose - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What's your opinion on the intent t..."
entries.text: What's your opinion on the intent to trap a ghost?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "There seem to be two beliefs on the..."
entries.text: There seem to be two beliefs on the matter among the mystics. Either that it will make for an interesting evening, or that it is playing with fire.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Everyone has their reasons, I suppo..."
entries.text: Everyone has their reasons, I suppose. If I were a mystic, I would hope mine were good, to attempt such a thing. Or perhaps I simply wouldn't care.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "But as it is? It's an interesting s..."
entries.text: But as it is? It's an interesting study.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Hm, I'm getting predictable. I can..."
entries.text: Hm, I'm getting predictable. I can hear it, too.

entries.text: Do you know anything about the Freemasons?

entries.text: They're a fraternal order valuing ritual and secrecy, and they require initiates to be male - hence, fraternal - and believe in a higher power.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Perhaps I could tell you more, but..."
entries.text: Perhaps I could tell you more, but for their secrecy.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Whether they actually dabble in the..."
entries.text: Whether they actually dabble in the great powers of the universe, or are just another gentleman's club, depends on who you ask.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "As for what I think? I won't do you..."
entries.text: As for what I think? I won't do you the disservice of belabouring the point.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Second sight - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know anything abou..."
entries.text: Do you happen to know anything about Miss McLeod's second sight?

entries.text: Ah, Mademoiselle McLeod. I don't doubt something troubles her - or even that she interprets it as visions. I know about this, of course.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "But, I find it more likely that she..."
entries.text: But, I find it more likely that she's suffering from some sort of chronic nervous fits than that she is spontaneously gaining foresight.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "My telling her so will do no good -..."
entries.text: My telling her so will do no good - but I wonder if introducing her to the idea might do some good.

title: Cast/Ettiene Toussaint/Evidence Presents - Ettiene/Ritual markings - Ettiene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: I found some evidence of a ritual conducted upstairs.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Is that so? Hm, that's curious. Tha..."
entries.text: Is that so? Hm, that's curious. That will be one of the sincere practitioners, most likely.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Someone intent on putting on a show..."
entries.text: Someone intent on putting on a show would do just that... or at least leave evidence it was them. Did you find any such thing?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "No, I didn't."
entries.text: No, I didn't.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Then it would see you stumbled onto..."
entries.text: Then it would see you stumbled onto something that wasn't meant for you.

entries.text: Apparently Monsieur O'Meara saw Miss Deane wandering the halls on Tuesday night. He said it seemed as if she'd been drinking.

entries.label: Ettiene: "That's... odd. I spoke to her on Tu..."
entries.text: That's... odd. I spoke to her on Tuesday evening, and she had a drink or two, but not enough that you would notice it.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Well, I suppose I saw earlier on. T..."
entries.text: Well, I suppose I saw earlier on. That could well have changed by whenever Monsieur O'Meara saw her.

entries.text: I have noticed handprints on my mirror as if it were cold. Not the strangest thing - or, at least, I have seen stranger through my work.

entries.text: Is that so? That's... hm. She seemed so set on this Séance...

entries.text: Mm. Perhaps it's another member of the family...?

entries.text: I suppose, unless they visit the event or Marquess Blake confirms it, we won't know for certain.

entries.text: Something ought to be done for her, then!

entries.text: The depravities of mankind are not new to me. I've seen - indeed, experienced first hand - magic and its beliefs used to justify many terrible things.

entries.text: But what shakes me in this case is the reasoning.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint

entries.text: Her own humanity meant so little to her. This is what upsets me. But, it is done.
