entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've heard talk about this manor be..."
entries.text: I've heard talk about this manor being haunted. Have you encountered anything of the sort?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have, yes. It's the crying in the..."
entries.text: I have, yes. It's the crying in the hallways that bothers me the most.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That - and the damp patches in the..."
entries.text: That - and the damp patches in the wallpaper. That, I would attribute just to this being an old building... except that the patches seem to move...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Séance's Purpose - Ruairi

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think the séance is going to..."
entries.text: Do you think the séance is going to be successful?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "In terms of whether or not we'll be..."
entries.text: In terms of whether or not we'll be successful in binding a ghost?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I don't know exactly what method Mi..."
entries.text: I don't know exactly what method Miss Mantovani is planning on using, so I couldn't comment on that specifically...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But I would imagine we stand a dece..."
entries.text: But I would imagine we stand a decent chance.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Deane's leaving letter - Ward

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It appears Miss Deane really did le..."
entries.text: It appears Miss Deane really did leave a letter as her way of signing out.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I suppose, whatever she was leaving..."
entries.text: I suppose, whatever she was leaving for, it must have been urgent.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Second Sight - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about this 'Se..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about this 'Second Sight'?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Miss McLeod's tradition, you mean?"
entries.text: Miss McLeod's tradition, you mean?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Usually you wouldn't see folk magic..."
entries.text: Usually you wouldn't see folk magic amongst the nobility... but I suppose, when it is an inherited gift, there's nothing to stop it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "If you can call it folk magic if it..."
entries.text: If you can call it folk magic if it's innate... I wonder. I suppose that might be a matter of opinion.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Anyhow. I can't say I'm familiar wi..."
entries.text: Anyhow. I can't say I'm familiar with the Scottish tradition, but it sounds like... involuntary divination, I suppose.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Ritual markings - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There is evidence of a ritual being..."
entries.text: There is evidence of a ritual being conducted upstairs, in one of the empty rooms.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That's... bizarre. If a person want..."
entries.text: That's... bizarre. If a person wanted to perform a ritual, here, and wanted to do so privately... why not do so in their own room?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Freemasons - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you happen to know anything abou..."
entries.text: Do you happen to know anything about the Freemasons?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have no insider knowledge, if tha..."
entries.text: I have no insider knowledge, if that's what you're asking. One needs an invitation to join, and that's not something I have.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Besides, if I were a member, I coul..."
entries.text: Besides, if I were a member, I couldn't tell you about it. I believe that's how it goes...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Mister O'Meara statement - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister O'Meara mentioned he saw Mis..."
entries.text: Mister O'Meara mentioned he saw Miss Deane on Tuesday night - and that she might have been drinking quite heavily, at that.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh? He didn't check to see if he wa..."
entries.text: Oh? He didn't check to see if he was alright?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I gather he didn't want to overstep..."
entries.text: I gather he didn't want to overstep his mark.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That's fair, I suppose... but I wou..."
entries.text: That's fair, I suppose... but I would feel better knowing she was alright.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Bedroom skeleton key - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Jesus Christ, Ward, why do you have..."
entries.text: Jesus Christ, Ward, why do you have that?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Strange occurences - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had anything... unexplaina..."
entries.text: Have you had anything... unexplainable happen to you while you were staying here?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Calling anything unexplainable migh..."
entries.text: Calling anything unexplainable might be a point of contention... but I won't pretend nothing comes to mind when you ask.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Unless someone is putting them ther..."
entries.text: Unless someone is putting them there, which would be... unsettling... I keep finding the bones of small animals under the rug in my room.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Not many... but more than I can com..."
entries.text: Not many... but more than I can comfortably account for.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Mister Doyle's statement - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister Doyle mentioned that he over..."
entries.text: Mister Doyle mentioned that he overheard Miss Deane arguing with someone in the gardens.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I... have never worked as staff at..."
entries.text: I... have never worked as staff at a hotel, but it feels improper that the porter would be sharing gossip, no?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Provided she wishes it to be so, Mi..."
entries.text: Provided she wishes it to be so, Miss Deane's affairs are her own.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Mysterious figure in window - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I noticed a figure in the window as..."
entries.text: I noticed a figure in the window as I was walking back to the manor. It looked like a young boy.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know if the Blakes have any..."
entries.text: Do you know if the Blakes have any children?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've lived in this area all my life..."
entries.text: I've lived in this area all my life, and worked here for a decade. I've never heard of the Blakes having any children - a son or otherwise.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Goibniu - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Does the name Goibniu mean anything..."
entries.text: Does the name Goibniu mean anything to you?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Certainly. He's one of Ireland's ol..."
entries.text: Certainly. He's one of Ireland's old gods. People focus on his smithing but he was also the hospitaller of the Tuatha Dé Danann.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's said one of his meals could pr..."
entries.text: It's said one of his meals could protect you from sickness and decay. That he brewed an ale that would grant immortality to any who drank it.

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "Aye, a smith god and hospitaller of..."
entries.text: Aye, a smith god and hospitaller of the Tuatha. It's said one of his meals could protect you from sickness and decay.

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "I wouldn't mind some of that protec..."
entries.text: I wouldn't mind some of that protection going into winter, ha!

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Along with this, he was a healer of..."
entries.text: Along with this, he was a healer of sorts. He crafted living metal limbs to bring mobility to any of the Tuatha who needed them.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Fae - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know about the fae?"
entries.text: What do you know about the fae?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well, the name can refer to a few t..."
entries.text: Well, the name can refer to a few things. Generally, though, the fae are thought to be inhabitants of the Otherworld.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's unclear if they can cross over..."
entries.text: It's unclear if they can cross over at will, or if they are trapped here looking for a way home.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They are seen more often in the dar..."
entries.text: They are seen more often in the dark, rural parts of the land, where the cities and towns haven't invaded the land as throughly.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They are most 'real', most present,..."
entries.text: They are most 'real', most present, on this plane at this time of year. Samhain. A worry for us, as Miss Mantovani and co. undertake to pierce the veil. Might they see this as a way home?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Hopefully not."
entries.text: Hopefully not.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Tuatha Dé Danann - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know of the Tuatha Dé D..."
entries.text: What do you know of the Tuatha Dé Danann?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Literally, it means The Folk of the..."
entries.text: Literally, it means The Folk of the Goddess Danú.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They are the race that preceded hum..."
entries.text: They are the race that preceded humanity in Ireland. While we know where they are now - or where they ended up, as such - where they came from originally is unknown.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They are somewhat analogous to gods..."
entries.text: They are somewhat analogous to gods, though that is more dependant on the specific character, rather than their race.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Or maybe a better way to put it is..."
entries.text: Or maybe a better way to put it is they were all god-like, but what god-like means is subjective.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Goddess Bridget - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you know about the goddess..."
entries.text: What do you know about the goddess Bríd?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The goddess? Let's see... A member..."
entries.text: The goddess? Let's see... A member of the Tuatha Dé Danann, the goddess of wisdom, healing, poetry, livestock... Any number of things.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She's sometimes thought to have two..."
entries.text: She's sometimes thought to have two sisters of the same name with other domains, and sometimes they're all attributed to the one Bríd.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You'll find her linked to the Saint..."
entries.text: You'll find her linked to the Saint, Brigid, too. I can tell you that for free.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Dead End - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I took the time to retrace Miss Dea..."
entries.text: I took the time to retrace Miss Deane's steps from Tuesday night, and it seems that she never left at all. Her trail ends in the hedge maze.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Do you mean to say something happen..."
entries.text: Do you mean to say something happened to her?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Surely you must be mistaken... even..."
entries.text: Surely you must be mistaken... even a haunted manor does not just make people disappear.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/The Hermetic Order - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the Herm..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They're a semi-secret society based..."
entries.text: They're a semi-secret society based in London, primarily interested in high magic.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A number of the guests, as it happe..."
entries.text: A number of the guests, as it happens, are members.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Stargazing - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you stargazing in the botanic..."
entries.text: Were you stargazing in the botanic house on Tuesday?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I was. Why do you ask?"
entries.text: I was. Why do you ask?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was wondering if you'd happened t..."
entries.text: I was wondering if you'd happened to see Miss Deane while you were there.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "No, I didn't. I saw her at dinner,..."
entries.text: No, I didn't. I saw her at dinner, but we went our separate ways for the evening after that.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Bridge Game _Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I hear there was a bridge game the..."
entries.text: I hear there was a bridge game the other evening. Did you play?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I did. Missus D'Arcy dragged me in..."
entries.text: I did. Missus D'Arcy dragged me in on my aunt's suggestion. Mister Skerritt was meant to play, but he was preoccupied in the library and left them down a player on short notice.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Enough for two tables. Miss Barbosa..."
entries.text: Enough for two tables. Miss Barbosa, Miss Quinn, and Missus Lau were there. Marquess Blake joined us, too, as did Mister Coventry.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did many attend?"
entries.text: Did many attend?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/cigar burns - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Thankfully Miss Quinn saw Mister Sk..."
entries.text: Thankfully Miss Quinn saw Mister Skerritt fall asleep and caught the cigar before it caused more damage than it did. I thought I was being summoned to check the old coot's health, but they wanted me to replace him at the bridge table instead...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Normally when I tell somebody to pu..."
entries.text: Normally when I tell somebody to pull back on their drinking or their smoking lest they cut their life short, I don't mean it quite so literally.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know who might be responsibl..."
entries.text: Do you know who might be responsible for the cigar burns in the library?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Ent schd - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I must confess, I've not gone to mu..."
entries.text: I must confess, I've not gone to much. Once the sun is down I've been watching the stars and during the day I've talked with whomever I could. Really, other than the bridge game on Tuesday I've gone to nothing.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/talk schd - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah yes. The talks. I though it woul..."
entries.text: Ah yes. The talks. I though it would do the attendees good to know of our gods, the Tuatha Dé Danann.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Given the magical nature of our gat..."
entries.text: Given the magical nature of our gathering, I thought especially people might want to learn of the wrath of our war-witch and death goddess, The Morrigan.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Or The Cailleach - also considered..."
entries.text: Or The Cailleach - also considered a witch - whose time begins on the eve of Samhain, when she ushers in the dark half of the year.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course, they might take these th..."
entries.text: Of course, they might take these things as mere tales, ghost stories for the night that is in it, and not warnings of the dangers of disturbing the natural order, but we'll see...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Medical certificate - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor Callaghan, I was wondering i..."
entries.text: Doctor Callaghan, I was wondering if you would parse a medical code for me. What does the code U0.33 signify.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A code of U0.33 in records would in..."
entries.text: A code of U0.33 in records would indicate miscarriage, if the issue is not written out in full. I assume this is a purely academic enquiry?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It is."
entries.text: It is.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Thank God for that. As you were, th..."
entries.text: Thank God for that. As you were, then.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Memento Mori - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the Quin..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the Quinn family having... an unusual number of deaths?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah. So Miss Quinn is one of the Qui..."
entries.text: Ah. So Miss Quinn is one of the Quinns, is she? I presume that's why you're asking. What an awful hand...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Yes, the Quinns have the unfortunat..."
entries.text: Yes, the Quinns have the unfortunate distinction of bearing a curse, one that's supposedly about a century old, now.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'd heard they had a presence in th..."
entries.text: I'd heard they had a presence in these circles, but I couldn't be certain they and our Miss Quinn were the same.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And that they are... How awful."
entries.text: And that they are... How awful.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Ines wants photograph - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Barbosa is after a photograph..."
entries.text: Miss Barbosa is after a photograph of her late father.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think that's something you'd..."
entries.text: Do you think that's something you'd be able to do for her?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know how I might be able to..."
entries.text: Do you know how I might be able to get something like that?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You're looking for spirit photograp..."
entries.text: You're looking for spirit photography, there. And it just so happens I might well be able to help you.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course - but I will need her fat..."
entries.text: Of course - but I will need her father's name to summon him for the photograph.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'll find out what his name was."
entries.text: I'll find out what his name was.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Excellent. Let me know when you do."
entries.text: Excellent. Let me know when you do.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I will need her father's name to su..."
entries.text: I will need her father's name to summon him for the photograph.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/O'Connor research

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I recovered some information on Mis..."
entries.text: I recovered some information on Miss Barbosa's family, courtesy of Miss Quinn.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It seems Miss Barbosa's father's na..."
entries.text: It seems Miss Barbosa's father's name was Seamus 'Shay' O'Connor.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well, better not to have me, of all..."
entries.text: Well, better not to have me, of all people, spring that on her. Take it to Miss Barbosa, and see what she wants to do.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Hedonistic Gala - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I can't say I was expecting a ball...."
entries.text: I can't say I was expecting a ball... quite like that one.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Me neither. Thankfully I got a whif..."
entries.text: Me neither. Thankfully I got a whiff of the drink and knew something was off. Since they alter one's mind state, knowing you've taken a hallucinogen can lead to a very different experience than not knowing...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You didn't take it, then?"
entries.text: You didn't take it, then?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That is... not what I said."
entries.text: That is... not what I said.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Strange Dreams - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've found I have the strangest dre..."
entries.text: I've found I have the strangest dreams staying here.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Mmm. You, as well? My aunt and I ha..."
entries.text: Mmm. You, as well? My aunt and I have found we're having overlapping thoughts from our dreams.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's the séance, of course. I alway..."
entries.text: It's the séance, of course. I always end up there. Or maybe it's the house itself? Either way, it's fascinating and I intend to find out more.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And such strange symbols, too! Stuf..."
entries.text: And such strange symbols, too! Stuff we've not encountered before, but if we both draw the patterns without describing them to one another, they match!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you walking down a corridor? S..."
entries.text: Were you walking down a corridor? Sealed doors and improbable windows?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I didn't recall anything like that..."
entries.text: I didn't recall anything like that before, but now that you've said it, I do.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Unknown Sigil - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I saw a sigil in my dream... a spir..."
entries.text: I saw a sigil in my dream... a spiral with four lines intersecting it. Does that sound like anything you might recognise?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Nothing... comes to mind, no. Curio..."
entries.text: Nothing... comes to mind, no. Curious.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Curse - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do I understand right, that Miss Qu..."
entries.text: Do I understand right, that Miss Quinn's family is under some sort of curse?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah. She's of the same Quinns, I tak..."
entries.text: Ah. She's of the same Quinns, I take it?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have heard something about that -..."
entries.text: I have heard something about that - a family cursed with misfortune and early graves.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A damned shame it has Miss Quinn. I..."
entries.text: A damned shame it has Miss Quinn. I don't... especially enjoy her company, but she doesn't deserve that.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Deane's Room - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you recall which room Miss Deane..."
entries.text: Do you recall which room Miss Deane was staying in?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I don't think so. No, if she ever m..."
entries.text: I don't think so. No, if she ever mentioned it, it's slipped my mind.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Was she in the east wing? I feel li..."
entries.text: Was she in the east wing? I feel like she wasn't that far from where we are?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "What an odd thing to forget..."
entries.text: What an odd thing to forget...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Cathal's Laudanum - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I... saw Mister O'Meara taking some..."
entries.text: I... saw Mister O'Meara taking some laudanum. No small amount, too. Is there a danger in that, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course there is, but I worry mor..."
entries.text: Of course there is, but I worry more about why he's taking it at that volume.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Some people get a dependancy for th..."
entries.text: Some people get a dependancy for the stuff, it's true. But he's using it to mask the pain of his various foolhardy risks.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A riding accident here, a beating i..."
entries.text: A riding accident here, a beating in an alleyway there - people talk, and it seems this poor young man has something of a death wish...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Shadowy Figure - Ruairi

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Any other place, or person, and you..."
entries.text: Any other place, or person, and you might find yourself in a white jacket.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor - if I told you I had seen a..."
entries.text: Doctor - if I told you I had seen a large, shadowy figure on the grounds - what would you say?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But... here? Me? I'd say if it's tr..."
entries.text: But... here? Me? I'd say if it's truly large, then it's not a mortal's ghost. Perhaps you're seeing the echo of an old god, one of the Tuatha Dé Danann?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Buried Messages - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I believe the dream contains buried..."
entries.text: I believe the dream contains buried messages. Ones of home and of the séance. I think the feelings of the former are being applied to the latter.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Fascinating. I will say that neithe..."
entries.text: Fascinating. I will say that neither Fiadh or myself had much interest in attending the séance itself, but now that we are here - we feel almost compelled to.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Altered Reality - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I entered the dream using the lucid..."
entries.text: I entered the dream using the lucid technique - when I returned, the hotel appeared to have been altered.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Minor changes - some paintings in m..."
entries.text: Minor changes - some paintings in my room altered to reflect the dream, and it was only a short while before the illusion faded.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "So the dream is... altering how the..."
entries.text: So the dream is... altering how the dreamers see the place? To further enforce the dream's desire?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But where is it coming from and wha..."
entries.text: But where is it coming from and what does the source want?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That was only my second experience..."
entries.text: That was only my second experience of the dream.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Lucid Dreaming - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about lucid dr..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about lucid dreaming, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Funny you should say... I have a pl..."
entries.text: Funny you should say... I have a plan to try it here. I thought maybe it would help me understand these strange dreams.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have a record in my room that I b..."
entries.text: I have a record in my room that I borrowed from the drawing room towards that end... but I keep forgetting to ask the staff to bring a gramophone up to my room.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They had a second suitable record t..."
entries.text: They had a second suitable record there, I noticed, should you wish to try it yourself?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh, and you should use an anchor -..."
entries.text: Oh, and you should use an anchor - something to focus on to ensure your dream is what you want it to be.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Maybe Miss Deane's journal would wo..."
entries.text: Maybe Miss Deane's journal would work? That's what started me on this course, after all...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A picture of a person, if you want..."
entries.text: A picture of a person, if you want to summon your mental image of them into the dream. Or a scent. Or, well, there are any number of things you could use - even a book on a topic could work!

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Shared Dreams - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I believe that people at the manor..."
entries.text: I believe that people at the manor are experiencing the same dream - shared to some extent.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I think something similar. I had in..."
entries.text: I think something similar. I had intended to try some lucid dreaming to get a better handle on the dream itself, but I keep getting sidetracked.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I must get around to asking the sta..."
entries.text: I must get around to asking the staff for a gramophone. I found a record in the drawing room and I intend to use its music as a sleep aid. Fingers crossed something comes of it.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Magical Grimoire - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you seen this book before, Doc..."
entries.text: Have you seen this book before, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...No. Though there is some terribl..."
entries.text: ...No. Though there is some terribly strong magic in these pages, Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Whatever those sigils open or close..."
entries.text: Whatever those sigils open or close, I cannot say - but they radiate power, even off the page.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "This is the kind of thing I'd leave..."
entries.text: This is the kind of thing I'd leave for the experts. Speaking as an expert, of sorts.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well, Oscail means open. Dún would..."
entries.text: Well, Oscail means open. Dún would be close, or shut.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me what these sigils m..."
entries.text: Can you tell me what these sigils mean?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did you know that Miss Deane comes..."
entries.text: Did you know that Miss Deane comes from powerful blood?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...I didn't. Though I'd expect noth..."
entries.text: ...I didn't. Though I'd expect nothing less from a practitioner of her calibre.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Blood counts for more than it shoul..."
entries.text: Blood counts for more than it should, I know. But magically, certainly, hers seems unparalleled.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Coded Papers - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Has this pattern any meaning to you..."
entries.text: Has this pattern any meaning to you, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah. I looks to be a sigil, Mister W..."
entries.text: Ah. I looks to be a sigil, Mister Ward. You can tell it was cast by a skilled practitioner, too, with so little trace shown. I must admit I am envious - I have not gotten quite that good, myself.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Whoever crafted it has almost certa..."
entries.text: Whoever crafted it has almost certainly written something they didn't want read.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/spirit camera - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've seen one of these before, at a..."
entries.text: I've seen one of these before, at a fair. A... camera, I believe?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A good eye, Mister Ward, and only p..."
entries.text: A good eye, Mister Ward, and only partially wrong.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It is a camera, yes, but one modifi..."
entries.text: It is a camera, yes, but one modified to work as a spirit camera.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well... I modified it to work bette..."
entries.text: Well... I modified it to work better as one. Any camera, in the right circumstances, can capture a spirit, of course.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But my lens filters the image throu..."
entries.text: But my lens filters the image through complex geometry made of peridot, selenite, black tourmaline, labradorite, lapis lazuli and clear quartz stones to both bring out the spirit and protect against it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I thought, what better place to rea..."
entries.text: I thought, what better place to really put this device to the test than here.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "These halls and - dare I say, the p..."
entries.text: These halls and - dare I say, the people here - are likely crawling with spirits.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've even set up a darkroom in my q..."
entries.text: I've even set up a darkroom in my quarters so I can quickly develop images. This way people can take away a copy, should they wish.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Would you care for a picture? See w..."
entries.text: Would you care for a picture? See who or what haunts you? Aha!

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Excellent! Come. In my room I have..."
entries.text: Excellent! Come. In my room I have everything needed to take and develop your picture quickly.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course. It is not for everybody...."
entries.text: Of course. It is not for everybody. You know where I am should you change your mind!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Lead the way."
entries.text: Lead the way.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ YES ]"
entries.text: [ YES ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ NO ]"

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've even set up a darkroom in my q..."
entries.text: I've even set up a darkroom in my quarters so I can quickly develop images. This way people can take away a copy, should they wish.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Carmela's Health

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you noticed, too, that Miss Ma..."
entries.text: Have you noticed, too, that Miss Mantovani seems unwell...?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You must know I can't discuss my pa..."
entries.text: You must know I can't discuss my patients' private medical information with just anyone.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I keep their files well protected,..."
entries.text: I keep their files well protected, so don't get any ideas. I won't be a source of gossip about the woman.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Mary Blake - Ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Did you ever meet Marchioness Blake..."
entries.text: Did you ever meet Marchioness Blake?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Perhaps if I'd been back I'd have d..."
entries.text: Perhaps if I'd been back I'd have delivered the boy. Not sure who did in the end.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "No, I was away for most of her time..."
entries.text: No, I was away for most of her time here. And when I wasn't, well, I don't really move in those circles.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I mainly knew of her through her wo..."
entries.text: I mainly knew of her through her work at the Blake Foundation. I was especially impress with her efforts to raise literacy rates in the region.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She seemed a good sort. She, and he..."
entries.text: She seemed a good sort. She, and her foundation, are greatly missed, no doubt.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/morrigan - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me much about the Morr..."
entries.text: Can you tell me much about the Morrigan?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The phantom queen. Look, Mister War..."
entries.text: The phantom queen. Look, Mister Ward, it's important to note that we have three sources for all this - the writings of Catholic Monks, so an agenda has to be acknowledged there...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And the third?"
entries.text: And the third?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The second are followers who believ..."
entries.text: The second are followers who believe to have had encounters with the entities in question. Again, those with an agenda.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Pure fiction. Entertainment inspire..."
entries.text: Pure fiction. Entertainment inspired by the first two sources. But the problem is they all become intertwined. And all are as true and false as one another. So take everything you hear with that in mind.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "So, the Morrigan. A powerful goddes..."
entries.text: So, the Morrigan. A powerful goddess and war-witch who can strike fear into the hearts of her foes and bolster the courage of those on her side.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Many a war was won or lost based on..."
entries.text: Many a war was won or lost based on her favour. And that's how she is often painted - a war goddess. But she is more than that.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She is a triple goddess, so when al..."
entries.text: She is a triple goddess, so when all aspects are viewed together, a softer image comes up - a protector goddess. A fierce one, yes, but a protector nonetheless.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Cailleach - Ruairi

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "An Cailleach - or, as she is someti..."
entries.text: An Cailleach - or, as she is sometimes unfavourably called, the winter hag. Her time is upon us - she rules from Samhain to Bealtaine.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me much about the Cail..."
entries.text: Can you tell me much about the Cailleach?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Samhain being commonly known now as..."
entries.text: Samhain being commonly known now as Halloween. Bealtaine is May first, and is ruled over by Bríd.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She ushers in the cold, the dark, t..."
entries.text: She ushers in the cold, the dark, the wet. She guides the old and sick to the Otherworld in that time. Then come May, she is gone again to rest.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/tir na nog - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about Tír na n..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about Tír na nÓg?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'll assume that you know it's the..."
entries.text: I'll assume that you know it's the old Irish afterlife, as such. Or, since you are a Catholic, our version of Heaven.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I say 'our' as Irish people, but al..."
entries.text: I say 'our' as Irish people, but also, this is what I believe in. So, do take what I say with that grain of salt.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "There are many things that separate..."
entries.text: There are many things that separate it from Heaven, of course. I think the most significant is its accessibility.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Catholics have to die to get to Hea..."
entries.text: Catholics have to die to get to Heaven, but we pagans can find a way to the Otherworld by less... final means.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's not a truly physical place, of..."
entries.text: It's not a truly physical place, of course, and defies physical rules. You can access it via the sea or via passageways on the land.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "To be clear, I am not talking mytho..."
entries.text: To be clear, I am not talking mythologically here. Yes, there are stories of that - young Oisín of the Fianna went and came back hundreds of years later, of course.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But we, you and I, could hop on hor..."
entries.text: But we, you and I, could hop on horses and get to a passageway by the day's end - and it would need to be day's end for they are stronger at night.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But going there and coming back are..."
entries.text: But going there and coming back are not the same thing. So, I have only gotten close, and that was enough for me.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Once mankind learns to fly - and ma..."
entries.text: Once mankind learns to fly - and mark my words, we will - we may find gateways up there, too.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have even experimented with enter..."
entries.text: I have even experimented with entering it via the dream space - but, I digress.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have gotten close to the threshol..."
entries.text: I have gotten close to the threshold to the Otherworld a few times. It's part of my training.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I can't recall quite which, but som..."
entries.text: I can't recall quite which, but some faiths took the idea of Heaven is "up there" very literally, crossover between birds and angels, et cetera, et cetera.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Or, if Fiadh is right and this is a..."
entries.text: Or, if Fiadh is right and this is a place of power then we could remove the need for horses, entirely.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Ines' dad's name - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Barbosa is after a photograph..."
entries.text: Miss Barbosa is after a photograph of her late father.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you think that's something you'd..."
entries.text: Do you think that's something you'd be able to do for her?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know how I might be able to..."
entries.text: Do you know how I might be able to get something like that?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You're looking for spirit photograp..."
entries.text: You're looking for spirit photography, there. And it just so happens I might well be able to help you.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course - but I will need her fat..."
entries.text: Of course - but I will need her father's name to summon him for the photograph.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I will need her father's name to su..."
entries.text: I will need her father's name to summon him for the photograph.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have it already. His name was Sea..."
entries.text: I have it already. His name was Seamus 'Shay' O'Connor.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Seamus O'Connor? Alright then. Why..."
entries.text: Seamus O'Connor? Alright then. Why don't we find Miss Barbosa and go get set up?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Timetable - Ruairi

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What are your plans for this Saturd..."
entries.text: What are your plans for this Saturday, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What are you up to this Sunday, Doc..."
entries.text: What are you up to this Sunday, Doctor?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm glad you asked, Mister Ward. Pe..."
entries.text: I'm glad you asked, Mister Ward. Perhaps I can rope you into joining the talks.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well, I plan to get some fresh air..."
entries.text: Well, I plan to get some fresh air in my lungs.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...Though she does like to chat, so..."
entries.text: ...Though she does like to chat, so I suspect we'll be in the dining room until right before her talk.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Then it's back to the bar for a few..."
entries.text: Then it's back to the bar for a few hours to kill some time until the 'main event'.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm attending all of them you know..."
entries.text: I'm attending all of them you know - there's ones at eleven, three and five today. I actually plan to spend much of the day in the drawing room.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Then there's Mister Coventry's talk..."
entries.text: Then there's Mister Coventry's talk at five. And before that, of course, mine! The drawing room at three, Mister Ward, if you wish to attend.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh, and my Aunt Fiadh is doing the..."
entries.text: Oh, and my Aunt Fiadh is doing the one at three. You should attend. Ah, and I have lunch plans with her at one.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Otherwise, I think I'll be in the b..."
entries.text: Otherwise, I think I'll be in the bar all evening. I need to get myself ready for the ball, so to speak. As for tomorrow...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have to wonder if my spirit camer..."
entries.text: I have to wonder if my spirit camera might capture things my eyes will not...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I hope to get plenty of pictures in..."
entries.text: I hope to get plenty of pictures in the stables. The horses certainly have a fondness for staring at empty space.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Thankfully, Fiadh and I are aligned..."
entries.text: Thankfully, Fiadh and I are aligned now. I'm no longer worried about the séance.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/bean draoí duties

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What are the duties of your role?"
entries.text: What are the duties of your role?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's somewhere between being a prie..."
entries.text: It's somewhere between being a priest and a doctor. Some faith work, some healing. Really, it's helping people in whatever way they need.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course, there is less need now...."
entries.text: Of course, there is less need now. The old ways die more each year, and doctors are more commonplace. Still, everyone needs a trusted friend. In many ways, that's the real core of the work.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/seance aftermath - Ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Your aunt thinks the séance could b..."
entries.text: Your aunt thinks the séance could be dangerous?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She doesn't think that Mister Ward."
entries.text: She doesn't think that Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She knows it."
entries.text: She knows it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They intend to unravel the order of..."
entries.text: They intend to unravel the order of the universe. Now, I am all for progress myself.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But there is no scientific method,..."
entries.text: But there is no scientific method, no rigorous testing.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Just some good intentions and a lot..."
entries.text: Just some good intentions and a lot of people to be caught in the crossfire if things go wrong.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Well Symbols - Ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the symb..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the symbols on the well?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah, that's Aunt Fiadh's work. You s..."
entries.text: Ah, that's Aunt Fiadh's work. You should ask her about that.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Well - Ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know anything about the well..."
entries.text: Do you know anything about the well in the hedge maze?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I do. It's old, very old. From befo..."
entries.text: I do. It's old, very old. From before this place was built. Probably not the only bit of antiquity around, either.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's Fiadh's belief that the well i..."
entries.text: It's Fiadh's belief that the well is the lifeblood of this entire region. I am inclined to agree with her.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/aunt's shadow - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you been apprenticing under Fi..."
entries.text: Have you been apprenticing under Fiadh for long?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have. For too long, in truth. I h..."
entries.text: I have. For too long, in truth. I have learned everything she has to teach me but still I am an apprentice.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She does not like my modern approac..."
entries.text: She does not like my modern approach to the role. She believes it distracts me from the work. But to adapt is the work!

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "If only I could get her to see - mo..."
entries.text: If only I could get her to see - modern problems require modern solutions!

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/witchcraft materials - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I found a pile of twigs and horse h..."
entries.text: I found a pile of twigs and horse hair - does this have any meaning to you?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Hmmm, either you have a magpie buil..."
entries.text: Hmmm, either you have a magpie building a nest or somebody is practising witchcraft.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But horsehair... maybe the stables..."
entries.text: But horsehair... maybe the stables is a good place to check?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/witchcraft charm - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What does this look like to you?"
entries.text: What does this look like to you?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A magical charm. It could be protec..."
entries.text: A magical charm. It could be protective, but the rough materials, the way it is wrapped - my guess is a binding spell.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/record - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know much about using music..."
entries.text: Do you know much about using music to aid with dreams?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A bit. I'm actually trying somethin..."
entries.text: A bit. I'm actually trying something along those lines myself.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I... my dreams here. They are diffe..."
entries.text: I... my dreams here. They are different to normal. So I am going to try and enter them more... consciously. It's a technique called Lucid Dreaming.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/fiadh componants

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you think of anything your aunt..."
entries.text: Can you think of anything your aunt might be missing to help her with her work at the well?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A hundred things, Mister Ward, but..."
entries.text: A hundred things, Mister Ward, but only one that matters - modernity.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The séance is modern magic. She can..."
entries.text: The séance is modern magic. She cannot protect against it without modern tools.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "If only she would accept my help!"
entries.text: If only she would accept my help!

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Milesians - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you know of the Milesians?"
entries.text: Do you know of the Milesians?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Know of them? I am one, Mister Ward..."
entries.text: Know of them? I am one, Mister Ward. As are you, presumably.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "They are the race of men who came h..."
entries.text: They are the race of men who came here and wrestled the right to settle from the gods.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I do love the country, but some day..."
entries.text: I do love the country, but some days I wish our ancestors had sailed to somewhere warmer...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/ru letter to deane- Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Miss Deane mentioned that you offer..."
entries.text: Miss Deane mentioned that you offered to teach her some Irish magic?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Not so loud! I, eh, don't want ever..."
entries.text: Not so loud! I, eh, don't want everyone looking for tutelage.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...In truth, I did. And so you don'..."
entries.text: ...In truth, I did. And so you don't go digging around any further, I did so behind Fiadh's back. She was against it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But, then again, she is against eve..."
entries.text: But, then again, she is against everything! It would have been a move that strengthened my own position in London, which in turn would strengthen what I could bring back to protect the land here in Ireland.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "We cannot dig our heels in and hope..."
entries.text: We cannot dig our heels in and hope the world doesn't outgrow us. To do so would be a failure in our duty.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/photo of miss deane - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you recognise this picture?"
entries.text: Do you recognise this picture?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course I do, I took it. Maybe a..."
entries.text: Of course I do, I took it. Maybe a week ago? Evelyn must have dropped it - you should return it to her.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/rejected request - ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I gather that Miss Deane was intere..."
entries.text: I gather that Miss Deane was interested in learning Irish magic from your aunt?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...She was. Fiadh rejected her, tho..."
entries.text: ...She was. Fiadh rejected her, though. That's all there is to that.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/bean draoí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You're Fiadh's apprentice?"
entries.text: You're Fiadh's apprentice?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I am. I am trained to handle all of..."
entries.text: I am. I am trained to handle all of her duties. Of course, I lack her experience. But I have my medical training and new techniques to give me an edge.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "When you take over, will you still..."
entries.text: When you take over, will you still be a Bean Draoí?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...Of course not, Mister Ward. I wo..."
entries.text: ...Of course not, Mister Ward. I would just be the Draoí.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Ru's componants

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "This is your bag of spells, then?"
entries.text: This is your bag of spells, then?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Not sure I would refer to it as suc..."
entries.text: Not sure I would refer to it as such, but it's not entirely untrue, either.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Please, do what I cannot and help m..."
entries.text: Please, do what I cannot and help me convince my aunt that I am ready to... I suppose you could say, graduate.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/drugs in room - Ru

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh, the malaria treatment? Well, ma..."
entries.text: Oh, the malaria treatment? Well, malaria and fever, I suppose I should say.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Doctor, can you tell me much about..."
entries.text: Doctor, can you tell me much about Quinine powder?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh... It can cause all manner of si..."
entries.text: Oh... It can cause all manner of side effects. Temporary blindness, confusion, dulled senses - unless a person is chasing that kind of thing, then I would say not.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Would a person use it for another r..."
entries.text: Would a person use it for another reason?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/gauge - Ru

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What do you make of that odd device..."
entries.text: What do you make of that odd device in the atrium?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Now that is a thing. I've been stud..."
entries.text: Now that is a thing. I've been studying it. The readings have been growing as we draw nearer to the séance.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The veil thinning? Maybe..."
entries.text: The veil thinning? Maybe...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But for that, I would have expected..."
entries.text: But for that, I would have expected a steady grow. One that only peaked on the 31st.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "No, this has climbed by ones and tw..."
entries.text: No, this has climbed by ones and twos. My theory is that its increases are linked to guest arrivals.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And I should note that it finally f..."
entries.text: And I should note that it finally filled the night you arrived...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/washer woman - Ru

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Hmmm... Well, assuming the staff ha..."
entries.text: Hmmm... Well, assuming the staff haven't gone mad, then I would think what you saw was a bean nigh.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "When I arrived I saw the damndest t..."
entries.text: When I arrived I saw the damndest thing - a woman washing clothes in the fountain.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Tell me, was she washing a garment?"
entries.text: Tell me, was she washing a garment?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "She was."
entries.text: She was.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I... didn't think to check."
entries.text: I... didn't think to check.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A shame, it might have told us who..."
entries.text: A shame, it might have told us who was to die.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The bean nigh, or washer woman, for..."
entries.text: The bean nigh, or washer woman, foretells the death of a person.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And those who see her... well, they..."
entries.text: And those who see her... well, they too feel the touch of death.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That is to say they are still in mo..."
entries.text: That is to say they are still in mourning over death, however long ago it happened.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Since you saw her, well... I am sor..."
entries.text: Since you saw her, well... I am sorry for whatever loss has befallen you.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...Thank you. But surely everyone s..."
entries.text: ...Thank you. But surely everyone should see her? We've all felt loss at some point in our lives?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Felt it, yes, but haunted by it? Pe..."
entries.text: Felt it, yes, but haunted by it? Perhaps 'haunted' isn't the right term, our location considered.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "When my father died, for example, I..."
entries.text: When my father died, for example, I was sad. But I have let that go. I am still sad for his passing but I am not weighted down by it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That is the difference."
entries.text: That is the difference.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A shawl. I do not know whose it was..."
entries.text: A shawl. I do not know whose it was.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Ruarí/Resolution - Ru

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well yes, but also no."
entries.text: Well yes, but also no.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I think it is safe to say your meth..."
entries.text: I think it is safe to say your methods worked.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "We succeeded not through my methods..."
entries.text: We succeeded not through my methods, but through Fiadh's and mine.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "There is a lesson there for me. I w..."
entries.text: There is a lesson there for me. I was too focused on the future.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But when we forget the past we don'..."
entries.text: But when we forget the past we don't learn from it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And we repeat the mistakes of it."
entries.text: And we repeat the mistakes of it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And! We only got there because you..."
entries.text: And! We only got there because you stepped in.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm grateful, of course, but also d..."
entries.text: I'm grateful, of course, but also deeply ashamed.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "That I might have let my duty to th..."
entries.text: That I might have let my duty to the land and its people down, because of ego...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "So, in all - I am proud of what we..."
entries.text: So, in all - I am proud of what we have achieved here, and I am proud of what it has taught me.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And, if you will do me the honour,..."
entries.text: And, if you will do me the honour, I am proud to call you a friend.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The honour, Doctor, is all mine."
entries.text: The honour, Doctor, is all mine.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ivy - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had the opportunity to mee..."
entries.text: Have you had the opportunity to meet Miss McLeod?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She was flighty until I promised I..."
entries.text: She was flighty until I promised I wouldn't try and diagnose her with anything.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She has the sight and I think that'..."
entries.text: She has the sight and I think that's left her in hot water with doctors before.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I told her Fiadh has similar, so I..."
entries.text: I told her Fiadh has similar, so I was well used to it. After that, she warmed up considerably.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She's a nice girl. I'm glad I've ha..."
entries.text: She's a nice girl. I'm glad I've had the opportunity to meet her.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Varley - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met the manager?"
entries.text: Have you met the manager?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I mean, in a manner of speaking."
entries.text: I mean, in a manner of speaking.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He's busy, certainly, but he seems..."
entries.text: He's busy, certainly, but he seems like a decent man.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "His family are all like that, thoug..."
entries.text: His family are all like that, though. They're from up our way and everyone of them is less fun than a wake.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Lan Fen - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had the opportunity to spe..."
entries.text: Have you had the opportunity to speak with Missus Lau?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "We met over drinks. She is an intel..."
entries.text: We met over drinks. She is an intelligent woman. It's not often I meet a lady with an interest in science.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "True, she's more scholar than scien..."
entries.text: True, she's more scholar than scientist, but that doesn't make the conversation much less interesting.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Sadly, she left in a hurry. Just as..."
entries.text: Sadly, she left in a hurry. Just as Miss Deane came to talk with me. Shame, I think they could have gotten on.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Skerritt - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to Mister Skerritt?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "We have spoken some. I find he has..."
entries.text: We have spoken some. I find he has a similar way about him to many gentlemen I meet in professional circumstances.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Outwardly pleasant. Perhaps a littl..."
entries.text: Outwardly pleasant. Perhaps a little old fashioned...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "...some of the old fashions hold ov..."
entries.text: ...some of the old fashions hold over better than others, wouldn't you say?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm not at all sure what Miss Deane..."
entries.text: I'm not at all sure what Miss Deane sees in him but they seem to have some sort of dynamic going on.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Corentine - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken with Miss Quinn?"
entries.text: Have you spoken with Miss Quinn?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Yes. She had Fiadh and I to tea."
entries.text: Yes. She had Fiadh and I to tea.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She is looking for some local histo..."
entries.text: She is looking for some local history and hoped we could help.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Sadly we could not, but I am sure s..."
entries.text: Sadly we could not, but I am sure she'll find what she seeks in the libraries here.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Caitlin - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken to the housekeeper?"
entries.text: Have you spoken to the housekeeper?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Hah, that I have. She was very inte..."
entries.text: Hah, that I have. She was very interested in the goings-on in Gauford. She is from there - she grew up alongside Fiadh, in fact.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I told her Fiadh might know more -..."
entries.text: I told her Fiadh might know more - but she said she'd rather talk to me. She doesn't like the old ways much, I'd wager.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I gave her what updates I had. All..."
entries.text: I gave her what updates I had. All this "ungodliness" seems to infuriate her - it was rather entertaining.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Darragh - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Mister Hunter, isn't it? I've been..."
entries.text: Mister Hunter, isn't it? I've been out that way a bit to take some shots, so we're talked a bit. Seems a good sort. Fiadh likes him.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken with the groundskee..."
entries.text: Have you spoken with the groundskeeper?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm sure she'd make introductions,..."
entries.text: I'm sure she'd make introductions, if you wanted.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Seamus - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met the porter?"
entries.text: Have you met the porter?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have. He was very friendly at fir..."
entries.text: I have. He was very friendly at first but cooled off when it became clear I wasn't the kind of doctor he was hoping for.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Which is one who is happy to dole o..."
entries.text: Which is one who is happy to dole out medicine freely and unquestioningly.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ines - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Barbosa?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Barbosa?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You hear so much about where our pe..."
entries.text: You hear so much about where our people have spread to these past few decades - it is fascinating to learn something firsthand.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And what a journey her father has b..."
entries.text: And what a journey her father has been on! Her too, for that matter.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She is here to dig into his past. I..."
entries.text: She is here to dig into his past. I am sad to say I could be no help.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I did try to offer her a picture, b..."
entries.text: I did try to offer her a picture, but Fiadh stomped all over that...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ettiene - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you had the opportunity to mee..."
entries.text: Have you had the opportunity to meet Mister Touissant?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "As a matter of fact, I had a very p..."
entries.text: As a matter of fact, I had a very pleasant conversation with him just the other day.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "His reputation precedes him, of cou..."
entries.text: His reputation precedes him, of course, but I found him quite reasonable.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Then again, I suppose I am not the..."
entries.text: Then again, I suppose I am not the sort of person he hunts. There is something to be said for turning out the fakes.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Cathal - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Mister O'Meara?"
entries.text: Have you met Mister O'Meara?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have spoken with him. It's an......"
entries.text: I have spoken with him. It's an... interesting case, his, isn't it?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He'd not be the first person I've m..."
entries.text: He'd not be the first person I've met who has claimed to have spoken with angels. And yet... somehow...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Let me tell you this - I took a pic..."
entries.text: Let me tell you this - I took a picture of him upon request. It... came out overexposed - or some of it did.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But was it exposure? Or... did I ca..."
entries.text: But was it exposure? Or... did I capture the thing on camera? I think I might be inclined to believe the latter...

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Dupré - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken with Mister Dupré?"
entries.text: Have you spoken with Mister Dupré?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have. He asked me if I knew anyth..."
entries.text: I have. He asked me if I knew anything about Irish mythology, and that's quite a topic.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I am impressed with his knowledge o..."
entries.text: I am impressed with his knowledge on the matter. He has some mind on him.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He seems like a good man. You'll fi..."
entries.text: He seems like a good man. You'll find that many people who take up a position like his are.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Deane - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Deane?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Deane?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "We met in London some time ago. I h..."
entries.text: We met in London some time ago. I had travelled for a conference, and attended a séance to meet an acquaintance.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I met Miss Deane there, and she was..."
entries.text: I met Miss Deane there, and she was very interested to hear about my tradition. We've been in contact, by way of letter, since.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I was looking forward to talking to..."
entries.text: I was looking forward to talking to her more, here, I heard word that she had recently returned from some expedition in India, but I haven't seen her recently.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She wanted to speak to Fiadh, too,..."
entries.text: She wanted to speak to Fiadh, too, but she said she had no interest in taking her on as a student.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well. Yes. We met once or twice. Sh..."
entries.text: Well. Yes. We met once or twice. She asked me to tutor her. In Irish magic. Me, not Fiadh.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I turned her down, of course. Would..."
entries.text: I turned her down, of course. Wouldn't be right. I turned her down, you see?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I know her, yes."
entries.text: I know her, yes.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She's a gifted practitioner by all..."
entries.text: She's a gifted practitioner by all accounts but she is a bit full of herself, don't you think?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I think she could stand to be taken..."
entries.text: I think she could stand to be taken down a peg or two.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on D'Arcy - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Missus D'Arcy?"
entries.text: Have you met Missus D'Arcy?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have. It was a bit of a whirlwind..."
entries.text: I have. It was a bit of a whirlwind. She's quite the personality.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I mean that as a compliment, mind y..."
entries.text: I mean that as a compliment, mind you. Though I do get the feeling she was hiding something from me.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She seems very much the sort who'd..."
entries.text: She seems very much the sort who'd want her picture taken but she was dead set against it - she paled at the idea.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Coventry - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I don't suppose you've met Mister C..."
entries.text: I don't suppose you've met Mister Coventry?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Briefly - we didn't speak much. He'..."
entries.text: Briefly - we didn't speak much. He's very polite, but I notice he can say a lot without sharing much.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You see it in patients all the time..."
