entries.text: You see it in patients all the time. They think they can talk around why they want some mercury.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It makes me wonder what he is tryin..."
entries.text: It makes me wonder what he is trying so hard not to say.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "When all they need to do is admit t..."
entries.text: When all they need to do is admit they caught syphilis in a brothel.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Hazel - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken with Missus Erickso..."
entries.text: Have you spoken with Missus Erickson?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've said hello. Rather, she introd..."
entries.text: I've said hello. Rather, she introduced herself. I don't usually interest myself in her brand of mysticism, but she seemed so earnest...

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "She told me she'd heard of me, even..."
entries.text: She told me she'd heard of me, even. She must have her ear to the ground... my tradition doesn't often get a second look in the city.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ruairí - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Tell me about yourself, Doctor Call..."
entries.text: Tell me about yourself, Doctor Callaghan.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Hm... Really?"
entries.text: Hm... Really?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well! I'm a local to the area, and..."
entries.text: Well! I'm a local to the area, and I mostly practice here, but I trained in Dublin. I still find reason to travel there, now and then.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "As for my... less strictly scientif..."
entries.text: As for my... less strictly scientific interests, there has long been a tradition of folk magic in Ireland.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Situation depending, of course. Not..."
entries.text: Situation depending, of course. Not everyone takes kindly to magic. But then again, not everyone takes kindly to medicine.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "So these days, I practice my own br..."
entries.text: So these days, I practice my own brand of magic and medicine as something of a dual craft.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Carmela - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Mantovani?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Mantovani?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "You know, I have. I've been fortuna..."
entries.text: You know, I have. I've been fortunate enough to spend some time with her.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'd never had the pleasure before t..."
entries.text: I'd never had the pleasure before this event, but I've found conversation with her to be intriguing. She has some fascinating insights into our work here.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's a shame she's only in this par..."
entries.text: It's a shame she's only in this part of the world every now and then.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What can you tell me about Miss Cal..."
entries.text: What can you tell me about Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Fiadh is my aunt on my father's sid..."
entries.text: Fiadh is my aunt on my father's side, and she's been teaching me in the old ways almost as long as I can remember.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I wasn't the only one of her nieces..."
entries.text: I wasn't the only one of her nieces and nephews she gave instruction to, of course, but I was the best at it, and had the determination to follow it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have been her... apprentice nearl..."
entries.text: I have been her... apprentice nearly all my life. She's a very talented woman, with a rightful place of honour in the community - their Bean Draoí.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Stubborn as a mule and occasionally..."
entries.text: Stubborn as a mule and occasionally hot-headed, to be sure, but we can't be all virtue, I suppose.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've been warding thresholds, scryi..."
entries.text: I've been warding thresholds, scrying in wells, and charming work tools since I could read and write.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Sinnott - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you spoken with Father Sinnott..."
entries.text: Have you spoken with Father Sinnott?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I... don't have a lot to discuss wi..."
entries.text: I... don't have a lot to discuss with priests. They tend to find my approach to things to be... unorthodox.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I am surprised to see a man of the..."
entries.text: I am surprised to see a man of the cloth at the event. I do not buy his "just keeping an eye on things" line, not for one moment.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met Miss Hisham?"
entries.text: Have you met Miss Hisham?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I have, as it happens. She's a fasc..."
entries.text: I have, as it happens. She's a fascinating woman, and incredibly sharp.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Very clued in, too. I think if she..."
entries.text: Very clued in, too. I think if she could focus, she would make a great leader for her people. Lord knows they'll need people like her in the coming years.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But right now, she has that way abo..."
entries.text: But right now, she has that way about her - the kind that people get when they are a little... too lost in the magical side of things.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Which is strange as she is no magic..."
entries.text: Which is strange as she is no magician and not really into all that. Maybe she's just caught up in the atmosphere of the séance?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Saoirse - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Have you met the cook, Miss Murphy?"
entries.text: Have you met the cook, Miss Murphy?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Only in the loosest of senses, but..."
entries.text: Only in the loosest of senses, but she was a lot warmer with Fiadh.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've gotten wind she had some visit..."
entries.text: I've gotten wind she had some visits from one of the local doctors a year or so ago. I never got the details but perhaps her coldness comes from that?

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Blake - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You are from the area, Doctor. Do y..."
entries.text: You are from the area, Doctor. Do you know the Marquess at all?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "No, not really. I left for my studi..."
entries.text: No, not really. I left for my studies a long time ago, and when I came back, I had no reason to visit this place.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The man I see now, though, bears no..."
entries.text: The man I see now, though, bears no resemblance to the vibrant man I recall from my youth.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on O'Finn - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Can you tell me much about Mister Ó..."
entries.text: Can you tell me much about Mister Ó Finn?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Ah yes. Our druid friend. He's alri..."
entries.text: Ah yes. Our druid friend. He's alright. His heart's in the right place but his code of conduct is so dated.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He needs to be more open to progres..."
entries.text: He needs to be more open to progress. I think he would achieve more if he were.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you aware that Marquess Blake..."
entries.text: Were you aware that Marquess Blake has a son?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He didn't, of course, when I left f..."
entries.text: He didn't, of course, when I left for my studies. I first heard of the boy after the accident - they needed a doctor to help him with his lingering damages.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Anyway, I received a letter asking..."
entries.text: Anyway, I received a letter asking me to consider returning home for the task, but nothing came of it. I assume they went with somebody resident to the region.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Probably a blessing, in hindsight...."
entries.text: Probably a blessing, in hindsight. I don't need to travel between here and Dublin any more than I do already.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "He was in the carriage, the one tha..."
entries.text: He was in the carriage, the one that killed his mother, you see. Came out alive but at some cost, I gather.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've never actually met the Blakes..."
entries.text: I've never actually met the Blakes before this event, but I do know of Blake's son. A few years ago, the Marquess was looking for a doctor for him, on account of the accident and its lingering damage.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Anyway, I was considered for the ta..."
entries.text: Anyway, I was considered for the task, but I think they chose a local doctor. I heard nothing more after a few back and forths.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Scent of antiseptic - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Forgive me for asking, but are your..."
entries.text: Forgive me for asking, but are your hands okay?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh, ha! Yes, they are. I work with..."
entries.text: Oh, ha! Yes, they are. I work with chemicals - carbolic acid to sterilized wounds and various others to develop pictures. It has left my hands looking worse for wear, though.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Good quality suit - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was admiring your suit. It looks..."
entries.text: I was admiring your suit. It looks very well made.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It's seen better days, I'm sure, bu..."
entries.text: It's seen better days, I'm sure, but a local doctor hardly makes enough for a new one at the drop of the hat. Unfortunately.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Anyway, thank you. Frankly, I'm con..."
entries.text: Anyway, thank you. Frankly, I'm concerned I'm underdressed, so I appreciate the compliment.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Are you...? Ah, you're being sincer..."
entries.text: Are you...? Ah, you're being sincere. I see.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Do you often wear that pin?"
entries.text: Do you often wear that pin?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Oh? Ah, this. You know, it's habit...."
entries.text: Oh? Ah, this. You know, it's habit. Settles patients. I forgot I even had it on.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But I'm not here as a practising do..."
entries.text: But I'm not here as a practising doctor, so I can afford it for a few days.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well, this is Ireland. A strong sen..."
entries.text: Well, this is Ireland. A strong sense of guilt and shame has been bred into even the freest of us.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I'm a pagan myself, but this is Ire..."
entries.text: I'm a pagan myself, but this is Ireland. A strong sense of guilt and shame has been bred into even the freest of us.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I've seen one of these before, at a..."
entries.text: I've seen one of these before, at a fair. A... camera, I believe?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A good eye, Mister Ward, and only p..."
entries.text: A good eye, Mister Ward, and only partially wrong.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "A good eye, Sir, and only partially..."
entries.text: A good eye, Sir, and only partially wrong.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "It is a camera, yes, but one modifi..."
entries.text: It is a camera, yes, but one modified to work as a spirit camera.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Well... I modified it to work bette..."
entries.text: Well... I modified it to work better as one. Any camera, in the right circumstances, can capture a spirit, of course.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "But my lens filters the image throu..."
entries.text: But my lens filters the image through complex geometry made of peridot, selenite, black tourmaline, labradorite, lapis lazuli and clear quartz stones to both bring out the spirit and protect against it.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I thought, what better place to rea..."
entries.text: I thought, what better place to really put this device to the test than here.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "These halls and - dare I say, the p..."
entries.text: These halls and - dare I say, the people here - are likely crawling with spirits.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I've even set up a darkroom in my q..."
entries.text: I've even set up a darkroom in my quarters so I can quickly develop images. This way people can take away a copy, should they wish.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Would you care for a picture? See w..."
entries.text: Would you care for a picture? See who or what haunts you? Aha!

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ YES ]"
entries.text: [ YES ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ NO ]"

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Excellent! Come. In my room I have..."
entries.text: Excellent! Come. In my room I have everything needed to take and develop your picture quickly.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Of course. It is not for everybody."
entries.text: Of course. It is not for everybody.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Lead the way."
entries.text: Lead the way.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/camera after ward's image taken

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "There you go. As simple as that."
entries.text: There you go. As simple as that.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Now, if you would care to follow me..."
entries.text: Now, if you would care to follow me to my room, I will develop the image for you.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Lead the way."
entries.text: Lead the way.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Now... Stand still. This will only..."
entries.text: Now... Stand still. This will only take a moment.

title: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Mister Ward? How exactly did you ge..."
entries.text: Mister Ward? How exactly did you get into my room?

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "I promise you, there's nothing in h..."
entries.text: I promise you, there's nothing in here that would be of value to a common thief.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A common thief? But-"
entries.text: A common thief? But-

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "If you have a better justification,..."
entries.text: If you have a better justification, you can give it to the manager.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "Sir? How exactly did you get into m..."
entries.text: Sir? How exactly did you get into my room?

entries.text: Let's see here...

entries.text: "No communication received Tues 24 from the Manor. Regards."

entries.label: Ward: "It seems like Miss Deane didn't sen..."
entries.text: It seems like Miss Deane didn't send for a carriage that night... nor did anyone else, for that matter.

entries.text: I could contact the exchange and confirm, I don't know how to send a message with this. It has to be entered in Morse code.

entries.text: The staff likely send messages on guests' behalves. One of them must know Morse, or have a guide to help with it...

entries.text: I wonder if Miss Deane would have used this to call for a ride off the manor grounds?

entries.text: Perhaps I can use that Morse code guide I have to contact the exchange and ask?

entries.text: It seems to be working now.

entries.text: The manager might wish to know.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It seems to be stationery - ink, pa..."
entries.text: It seems to be stationery - ink, paper for the machines - and so on.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: Used to type up incoming messages for the guests.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I could have sworn this page was bl..."
entries.text: I could have sworn this page was blank, but instead there is something here in Irish.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: The typewriter I noticed some strange writing on. The page has been disposed of.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If only the language hadn't been ta..."
entries.text: If only the language hadn't been taken from us.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If only I could speak the language."
entries.text: If only I could speak the language.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "If only the language hadn't been sy..."
entries.text: If only the language hadn't been systematically wiped out by the British Empire.

title: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/use but no morse book

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Let's see here..."
entries.text: Let's see here...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have no idea how to use this. I w..."
entries.text: I have no idea how to use this. I would need a user manual or some aid...

entries.text: I can hear nothing.

entries.text: A copy of 'How the Other Half Lives'. It seems to be a book of photojournalism from the Americas.

entries.text: What was that?

entries.text: Signs of the building's age.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have everything I need to make a..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I don't have the means to make a sa..."
entries.text: I don't have the means to make a salt solution, but maybe I can find some substitutes?

entries.label: Ward: "Hmmm, but why did the paper start t..."
entries.text: Hmmm, but why did the paper start to burn? It says here I need it to be salt-soaked. That might stop it burning.

title: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/envelopes

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "But I don't think I'm done with my..."
entries.text: But I don't think I'm done with my questions, Mister Dupré. I want to know more about your practice.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "It would be my pleasure."
entries.text: It would be my pleasure.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "After breakfast, would you join me..."
entries.text: After breakfast, would you join me for some air out front?

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Of course."
entries.text: Of course.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Would you believe that he's somewha..."
entries.text: Would you believe that he's somewhat of an expert on all things related to death?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Declan Ward. Pleased to meet you bo..."
entries.text: Declan Ward. Pleased to meet you both.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "More than that, evidently! We were..."
entries.text: More than that, evidently! We were just talking about this "Grand Séance" and I'm trying to understand what it is that makes it so grand.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "She means I am an undertaker."
entries.text: She means I am an undertaker.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Allow me to introduce Missus Olivia..."
entries.text: Allow me to introduce Missus Olivia D'Arcy. And I am Lloyd Dupré.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Aaah!"
entries.text: Aaah!

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh dear... I've made a right hames..."
entries.text: Oh dear... I've made a right hames of this... Don't fret, nothing's broke.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Do you need help, Missus Joyce?"
entries.text: Do you need help, Missus Joyce?

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh no, Sir, thank you. I managed to..."
entries.text: Oh no, Sir, thank you. I managed to drop it, I can manage to pick it back up, I'm sure.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "But those cases are debunked at wor..."
entries.text: But those cases are debunked at worst and uncorroborated at best - there is no way to prove, beyond doubt, the medium did not make it up.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Now. In any records of direct sight..."
entries.text: Now. In any records of direct sightings - and this is true of my own... encounters - the ghosts do not, can not, speak for themselves.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "But, I could have sworn I'd left my..."
entries.text: But, I could have sworn I'd left my key here...? Maybe I dropped it?

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Oh, my key. I should put that back..."
entries.text: Oh, my key. I should put that back in my purse before I forget it.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "I'm sorry, Mister Dupré - we will h..."
entries.text: I'm sorry, Mister Dupré - we will have to postpone that conversation. Once we're finished here, I'll need to go to reception and ask whether anyone has turned in my key.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "The hope is that Miss Mantovani, wi..."
entries.text: The hope is that Miss Mantovani, with the right time, place, and people around her, will cut out the middleman - or middlewoman in this case - and have the spirit speak for itself!

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Tomorrow night, the veil between wo..."
entries.text: Tomorrow night, the veil between worlds will be at its thinnest. And it's especially thin here, in this part of the country.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Then the hotel... it's not without..."
entries.text: Then the hotel... it's not without its storied history. Plenty of uncrossed souls in these walls.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "That, of course, is where the dange..."
entries.text: That, of course, is where the danger lies...

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Danger?"
entries.text: Danger?

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Of course, Madam. I'll be in the co..."
entries.text: Of course, Madam. I'll be in the courtyard, should you find time to join me.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "To the courtyard, then, Missus D'Ar..."
entries.text: To the courtyard, then, Missus D'Arcy.

title: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Care to join us, Sir? If you don't..."
entries.text: Care to join us, Sir? If you don't mind me speaking for you both, of course?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "No, it's alright. Maybe he knows so..."
entries.text: No, it's alright. Maybe he knows something about Miss Hisham's friend?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]"
entries.text: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ JOIN THEM ]"
entries.text: [ JOIN THEM ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You're very kind, but I don't have..."
entries.text: You're very kind, but I don't have the time, just now. Thank you, all the same.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Please. Declan Ward, thank you for..."
entries.text: Please. Declan Ward, thank you for letting me join.

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "Miss Deane. Evelyn Deane. Have you..."
entries.text: Miss Deane. Evelyn Deane. Have you met her?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Yeah, okay. Now, Miss Hisham, who i..."
entries.text: Yeah, okay. Now, Miss Hisham, who is your friend?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Is this a joke? Did Eve... Miss Dea..."
entries.text: Is this a joke? Did Eve... Miss Deane put you up to this?

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "I don't..."
entries.text: I don't...

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Mister O'Meara! Please!"
entries.text: Mister O'Meara! Please!

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Sorry, sorry. Yes, I know Miss Dean..."
entries.text: Sorry, sorry. Yes, I know Miss Deane. We have... history...

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Hmpf. What about her, Miss Hisham?"
entries.text: Hmpf. What about her, Miss Hisham?

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "Thank you. I was meant to meet her..."
entries.text: Thank you. I was meant to meet her yesterday. Or the day before? It's... cloudy.

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "But I haven't seen her. And I asked..."
entries.text: But I haven't seen her. And I asked the staff, and, after blank stares, I was told she had left.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "She left? That doesn't seem correct..."
entries.text: She left? That doesn't seem correct. Why would she go? She lives for this stuff!

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "A family matter, maybe?"
entries.text: A family matter, maybe?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ ADMIT KNOWING HER FATHER ]"
entries.text: [ ADMIT KNOWING HER FATHER ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ ADMIT YOU NEVER MET HER ]"
entries.text: [ ADMIT YOU NEVER MET HER ]

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "Do you know her, Sir?"
entries.text: Do you know her, Sir?

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "As much as I know any of you three,..."
entries.text: As much as I know any of you three, I'm afraid. We talked at the afternoon tea on Tuesday - which turned into afternoon drinks, which turned into my needing a slow start on Wednesday.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "I thought maybe she sent you down h..."
entries.text: I thought maybe she sent you down here to make fun at my expense. It would be the sort of thing she would find amusing.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Tuesday, you say?"
entries.text: Tuesday, you say?

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "You, Mister Ward? Do you know her?"
entries.text: You, Mister Ward? Do you know her?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I have had... dealings with her fat..."
entries.text: I have had... dealings with her father.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "With Rupert? You must be a shady de..."
entries.text: With Rupert? You must be a shady devil then, Mister Ward!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "No. I only arrived yesterday. If sh..."
entries.text: No. I only arrived yesterday. If she has left, then I've missed my chance to meet her.

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "Hmm. Very well. I hope she is okay...."
entries.text: Hmm. Very well. I hope she is okay. I overheard that the telegraph machine is recovered. I'll send something to her home, so she can contact me on her return.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Ha, I'm only making fun. Mister Dea..."
entries.text: Ha, I'm only making fun. Mister Deane is a... hardfisted businessman. Certainly, I doubt you know him from church.

entries.speaker: Miss Hisham
entries.label: Arwa: "Please excuse me."
entries.text: Please excuse me.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Of course. I'll take this opportuni..."
entries.text: Of course. I'll take this opportunity to make my leave, as well.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "You are correct there, Mister O'Mea..."
entries.text: You are correct there, Mister O'Meara. I don't know much about his daughter - does the apple fall far from the tree?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...I'm sorry that I cannot help you..."
entries.text: ...I'm sorry that I cannot help you, Miss Hisham, but I'll keep an eye out.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Me too. This whole meal has left me..."
entries.text: Me too. This whole meal has left me painfully upset.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Of course. I'll take this opportuni..."
entries.text: Of course. I'll take this opportunity to make my leave, as well.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Ohhh..."
entries.text: Ohhh...

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Yes and no, I suppose. She certainl..."
entries.text: Yes and no, I suppose. She certainly has his drive and forceful personality. And disdain for the Man Upstairs.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "But she is less interested in mater..."
entries.text: But she is less interested in material things than he.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "It is very easy to not care about m..."
entries.text: It is very easy to not care about material things when you have so much of them to hand.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "..."

title: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I understand the concern, Signorina..."
entries.text: I understand the concern, Signorina, I do... Oh, but - Mister Ward, would you like to join us?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "We were just talking about... well,..."
entries.text: We were just talking about... well, whether this séance is such a good idea. You're welcome to join us, if you like.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]"
entries.text: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ JOIN THEM ]"
entries.text: [ JOIN THEM ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I wish I could, but I don't have th..."
entries.text: I wish I could, but I don't have the time just now. Please excuse me.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'd be delighted to. Is there doubt..."
entries.text: I'd be delighted to. Is there doubt about the séance?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Consider yourself excused."
entries.text: Consider yourself excused.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Sì, Signorina Callaghan has concern..."
entries.text: Sì, Signorina Callaghan has concerns about it taking place.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "If you ask me, Mister Ward, there's..."
entries.text: If you ask me, Mister Ward, there's nothing good to come of this. Best to leave these lands be. They're unsettled enough already...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "But it is one spirit, mio amica, am..."
entries.text: But it is one spirit, mio amica, among many, apprehended for less than an hour. If I thought it would cause much trouble, I would not do it.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "And it is the Marquess' home. Surel..."
entries.text: And it is the Marquess' home. Surely he would not invite me to do such a thing if it would cause trouble in his ancestral home.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Hmph. I'm not sure the Marquess kno..."
entries.text: Hmph. I'm not sure the Marquess knows what's good for him.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ ASK MISS CALLAGHAN'S REASONING ]"
entries.text: [ ASK MISS CALLAGHAN'S REASONING ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ ASK ABOUT MISS MANTOVANI'S INVITA..."
entries.text: [ ASK ABOUT MISS MANTOVANI'S INVITATION ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What is it that has you so concerne..."
entries.text: What is it that has you so concerned, Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Ah... See, this was once sacred gro..."
entries.text: Ah... See, this was once sacred ground. There are portals - ways to the Otherworld, underground all over the country. But this place housed a significant one.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I worry that when our medium here c..."
entries.text: I worry that when our medium here calls forth something from the other side, she'll call the wrong thing...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Tsk! You offend me - I am a better..."
entries.text: Tsk! You offend me - I am a better medium than that! *cough* *cough*

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You'll call out in a place you don'..."
entries.text: You'll call out in a place you don't know where things you don't know walk. They are tricksters - they can call back in any way that pleases you!

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Am I right to assume that Marquess..."
entries.text: Am I right to assume that Marquess Blake invited you here himself?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Yes. He contacted me directly and i..."
entries.text: Yes. He contacted me directly and insisted I host his séance.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "He said he had heard of my ability..."
entries.text: He said he had heard of my ability and could settle for no less. - how could I refuse that, Signor?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "That is... strange, I must admit, b..."
entries.text: That is... strange, I must admit, but I do not find I can refuse. And besides, everything I know about séances...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Even with what we are planning, the..."
entries.text: Even with what we are planning, there is nothing to suggest there will be trouble.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I understand the concern, Signorina..."
entries.text: I understand the concern, Signorina, I do... Ah, but - this man would like to join us, yes?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "You know my thoughts on it."
entries.text: You know my thoughts on it.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I will do my best for you, Signorin..."
entries.text: I will do my best for you, Signorina, I promise.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Well... Ah, that more people were a..."
entries.text: Well... Ah, that more people were as reasonable. Thank you for that, at least, Miss Mantovani.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Please, my name is Carmela."
entries.text: Please, my name is Carmela.

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "Excuse my interrupting... but I hav..."
entries.text: Excuse my interrupting... but I have to wonder. If what Miss Callaghan says is true, and there is a gateway here, and this séance is the first of its sort...

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "I think that would suggest then, if..."
entries.text: I think that would suggest then, if something unexpected were to happen, it could well happen here. Is that not so?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I suppose that is true."
entries.text: I suppose that is true.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Exactly! This entire event is meddl..."
entries.text: Exactly! This entire event is meddling in factors we cannot - even those of us who know the land - know the outcome of.

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "Which would make for a fascinating..."
entries.text: Which would make for a fascinating revelation, would it not, Miss Callaghan?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh, for pity's sake..."
entries.text: Oh, for pity's sake...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I could say, amica mia, that it is..."
entries.text: I could say, amica mia, that it is only one spirit. One among many, apprehended for less than an hour.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Were it to cause much trouble-- *co..."
entries.text: Were it to cause much trouble-- *cough* I would not do it.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "This is, of course, a lie!"
entries.text: This is, of course, a lie!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "How can I say it is safe when it ha..."
entries.text: How can I say it is safe when it has not been done before? Of course, I would risk this!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "And the Marquess, he sees value in..."
entries.text: And the Marquess, he sees value in that risk, too.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I worry that when our medium here c..."
entries.text: I worry that when our medium here calls forth something from the other side, she'll put something askew we can't put right again.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "How could I refuse that, Signor? He..."
entries.text: How could I refuse that, Signor? He has never told me the specifics as to why he requires it... he avoided the question when I asked.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Were you the only invited guest?"
entries.text: Were you the only invited guest?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Signor! You offend me! I am the mai..."
entries.text: Signor! You offend me! I am the main event, no? Am I not enough for you?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "I got no invite."
entries.text: I got no invite.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Haha, and now I understand why!"
entries.text: Haha, and now I understand why!

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "How can you know 'til it's done?"
entries.text: How can you know 'til it's done?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "And right now, you seem most eager..."
entries.text: And right now, you seem most eager to succeed at any cost!

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "Excuse my interrupting... a portal...."
entries.text: Excuse my interrupting... a portal... underground?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "As such, aye."
entries.text: As such, aye.

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "Do you know a way to it?"
entries.text: Do you know a way to it?

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Oh. That's long lost, since the inv..."
entries.text: Oh. That's long lost, since the invasions.

entries.speaker: Miss Callaghan
entries.label: Fiadh: "Not that I'd tell a man of God, eve..."
entries.text: Not that I'd tell a man of God, even if it wasn't. Hasn't your kind plundered our myths enough?

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott
entries.label: FatherSinnott: "Mmmm..."
entries.text: Mmmm...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "I do not know? Perhaps they were in..."
entries.text: I do not know? Perhaps they were invited, or perhaps my reputation precedes me! *cough*

title: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah, you would be... Mister Ward? Th..."
entries.text: Ah, you would be... Mister Ward? Thank you for accepting my invitation.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]"
entries.text: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ JOIN HIM ]"
entries.text: [ JOIN HIM ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I'm afraid I cannot. Please excuse..."
entries.text: I'm afraid I cannot. Please excuse me, Marquess.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Ah, Mister Ward. Good to speak with..."
entries.text: Ah, Mister Ward. Good to speak with you again. I trust you are enjoying your time with us here at the manor?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "You will join me for lunch, then?"
entries.text: You will join me for lunch, then?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Yes, thank you for the offer."
entries.text: Yes, thank you for the offer.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I will admit, it is not often that..."
entries.text: I will admit, it is not often that I get to dine with nobility.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "What brought you here, Mister Ward?"
entries.text: What brought you here, Mister Ward?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I beg your pardon?"
entries.text: I beg your pardon?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Are you a student of the occult? Yo..."
entries.text: Are you a student of the occult? You are a working man, so I do not think you are here to climb social ladders?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Perhaps you... lost... somebody?"
entries.text: Perhaps you... lost... somebody?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I..."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ EVELYN DEANE ]"
entries.text: [ EVELYN DEANE ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ BROTHER ]"
entries.text: [ BROTHER ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ THE TENANTS ]"
entries.text: [ THE TENANTS ]

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "[ STAY SILENT ]"
entries.text: [ STAY SILENT ]

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I lost my... brother. Eamonn."
entries.text: I lost my... brother. Eamonn.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "We were firemen."
entries.text: We were firemen.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I came here looking for Evelyn Dean..."
entries.text: I came here looking for Evelyn Deane.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Deane? Ah, yes, the departed girl...."
entries.text: Deane? Ah, yes, the departed girl. You must have been disappointed to find her gone when you arrived.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "You are one of the throng of men wh..."
entries.text: You are one of the throng of men who seemed to be chasing her.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "She sounds like a fascinating woman..."
entries.text: She sounds like a fascinating woman. I wish I'd been able to meet her.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Were?"
entries.text: Were?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I stopped. After a blaze took him."
entries.text: I stopped. After a blaze took him.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I know fishermen who think that whe..."
entries.text: I know fishermen who think that when the sea takes them, it's their time to go.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I never met a fireman who felt the..."
entries.text: I never met a fireman who felt the same about flames.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am sorry for your loss."
entries.text: I am sorry for your loss.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "My wife... She... died in a carriag..."
entries.text: My wife... She... died in a carriage accident. Same one that crippled our boy.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Me too."
entries.text: Me too.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I lost my wife. She... died in a ca..."
entries.text: I lost my wife. She... died in a carriage accident. Same one that crippled our boy...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A loss it is, then."
entries.text: A loss it is, then.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "It's okay. I know it can be hard to..."
entries.text: It's okay. I know it can be hard to speak on these things.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Do you know there were reports of o..."
entries.text: Do you know there were reports of over one hundred different ghosts wandering these grounds?

entries.text: Eventually... he asked to stop coming.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake

entries.text: Maybe 'gave up' is being unfair on myself, given this event.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I..."

entries.text: In another life, I was a fireman.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "..."

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "..."

entries.text: But not her.

entries.text: The silent dinner, Mister Ward. Will you invite your brother to it?

entries.text: Well, I hope that whatever solace you seek here, you find it.

entries.text: I... think I will, yes.

entries.text: ...No. I have made my peace with what happened to him. He's best left resting in the past.

entries.label: JBlake: "I shall have the housekeeper lay a..."
entries.text: I shall have the housekeeper lay a place out for him, then. It is at 8pm sharp this evening. You would not want to miss him, should he come.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I wish I had your wisdom and your r..."
entries.text: I wish I had your wisdom and your resolve, Mister Ward.

entries.label: JBlake: "I also hope you are wrong and that..."
entries.text: I also hope you are wrong and that I am right to try to speak with her again. We shall see, as they say.

entries.label: JBlake: "Now. If you will excuse me, there i..."
entries.text: Now. If you will excuse me, there is a lot to prepare for later on. Good day, Mister Ward.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There were lives lost along the way..."
entries.text: There were lives lost along the way.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Inevitable in that work. Inevitable..."
entries.text: Inevitable in that work. Inevitable in the conditions people are forced to live in, work in.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "But one... one fire, I cannot let g..."
entries.text: But one... one fire, I cannot let go.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I carry those lives with me still...."
entries.text: I carry those lives with me still. Perhaps forever.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am sorry for your loss, though I..."
entries.text: I am sorry for your loss, though I am sure you saved more lives than slipped through your fingers.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That is probably true. But I had to..."
entries.text: That is probably true. But I had to leave the job after that. I couldn't face the flames without seeing them. And it is not a role that forgives hesitation.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I imagine not. I..."
entries.text: I imagine not. I...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Not long after that, I gave up, too..."
entries.text: Not long after that, I gave up, too.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I have somehow convinced myself tha..."
entries.text: I have somehow convinced myself that if all this is true - this business with the séance, maybe I can see her again. Speak with her... again...

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan..."
entries.text: I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan Blake. We haven't had much chance to speak since you arrived.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "A shame. I had hoped to sit with al..."
entries.text: A shame. I had hoped to sit with all the guests before the séance, but I cannot force you to join me.

entries.text: Has it now?

entries.text: How odd. I wonder what caused that?

entries.text: I... suppose I shouldn't stare... Varley said it upsets them...

entries.text: Where did this come from? Did my secret employer manage to get this to me? But who are they?

entries.text: Missus Joyce, I assume.

entries.text: Lord save me, I cannot get used to this...

entries.text: The ghost from the hedge maze!

entries.text: Laura? She returned for this - despite being freed...

entries.text: Is that Mary Blake? Why is she facing away?

entries.text: I did not think... that you could actually... could actually...

entries.text: Perhaps it's a good time to investigate, since the Marquess and most of the guests appear to be here...

entries.text: A moment, Mister Ward?

entries.label: Cathal: "Unless I am mistaken, you told me e..."
entries.text: Unless I am mistaken, you told me earlier that you knew Evelyn?

entries.text: Whereas just now you've claimed not to know her at all?

entries.text: So... which is it?

entries.text: ...In truth, I don't know Miss Deane. I told you she left... well, somebody brought me here to find out why.

entries.text: Her leaving does seem suspicious. She loves these things.

entries.text: ...as I mentioned, she was out of it when I saw her. I'd said she was at the bar - and that is likely true.

entries.text: But she may well have been there getting something from the barman, the porter - Doyle.

entries.text: He's a bit of a user, and Evelyn always finds those. Anyone with a supply can share a supply.

entries.text: If this is the dinner then it is eight pm - an hour earlier than it should be. And... What was I doing?

entries.text: If so, then I won't waste it.

entries.text: ...I'm dead.

entries.text: How?

entries.text: --please, Sir, call them 'The Other Crowd', 'Other Folk', or similar unless you want to draw their eye to this place.

entries.text: My apologies, Madame. These Other Folk, they differ from the winged fairies of children's stories, oui?

entries.text: As much as you and I differ from a wild animal, yes.

entries.text: There are several distinct groups of people that must be considered when talking about Irish mythology.

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt

entries.text: Thank you, Marquess. Not to turn things gruesome, but is it true? What do they say about the walled-up rooms?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "..."

entries.text: Certainly, it is said that Percival Blake bricked away people who crossed him, but no proof was ever found.

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Spending too much time digging arou..."
entries.text: Spending too much time digging around in our library, eh Mister Skerritt?

entries.speaker: Marquess Blake
entries.label: JBlake: "Unless he magicked the evidence awa..."
entries.text: Unless he magicked the evidence away, I think we can lay these rumours to rest.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "In the First Cycle, there are the T..."
entries.text: In the First Cycle, there are the Tuatha De Danann, a race of god-like entities.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The stories of the Second Cycle are..."
entries.text: The stories of the Second Cycle are primarily concerned with the ancient kingdoms that once made up the land.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "The Third Cycle centres around the..."
entries.text: The Third Cycle centres around the exploits of hunters and bards, led by the hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "And finally, there is the fourth cy..."
entries.text: And finally, there is the fourth cycle - the Cycle of Kings. The fourth cycle is also that in which we find the story of the Milesians, our forefathers.

entries.speaker: Doctor Callaghan
entries.label: Ruairí: "These are the people who would win..."
entries.text: These are the people who would win a battle against the Tuatha Dé Danann, and consign them to the Otherworld.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré

entries.text: It is my opinion that characters of gods hold particular sway across the world if they have a domain that is common to the human experience.

entries.text: And while we no longer live in an age of warriors and great battles, such as that the Mórrigan was said to oversee…

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Bríd, goddess of poets, would surel..."
entries.text: Bríd, goddess of poets, would surely still have domain with the authors of our age...

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "And one must imagine the spirit of..."
entries.text: And one must imagine the spirit of Giobniu would be found in the Industrial Revolution that makes so much possible.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré

entries.text: The domains of gods are not lost, not to those that would worship them. They simply change.

entries.speaker: Mister Dupré
entries.label: Dupré: "Across time and continents, their d..."
entries.text: Across time and continents, their domains still hold meaning even if they take forms we no longer recognise. Such is the nature of things.

entries.text: The body of Christ.

entries.text: A... men.

entries.speaker: Miss Murphy
entries.label: Saoirse: "..."

entries.speaker: Father Sinnott

entries.text: ... Does something trouble you, my child?

entries.text: By their nature, they are hard to define. And yet, even in their... elusive... ness... Questo funzionerà... we find them everywhere.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "By their many names, they are all a..."
entries.text: By their many names, they are all across the world. There are many formations...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Some echo the grief they left upon..."
entries.text: Some echo the grief they left upon the world and are blind to the living. *cough*

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "While others are vengeful and aggre..."
entries.text: While others are vengeful and aggressive.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Regardless. No single spectre exper..."
entries.text: Regardless. No single spectre experienced has been able to directly communicate.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "But tomorrow night - ah tomorrow ni..."
entries.text: But tomorrow night - ah tomorrow night we intend to change this!

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "So, I am sure you all know this lan..."
entries.text: So, I am sure you all know this land came into the Blake family in the 1650s after Cromwell's invasion.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "What I found interesting was what c..."
entries.text: What I found interesting was what came before...

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "This land was a place of worship an..."
entries.text: This land was a place of worship and innovation.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "A gathering spot for scholars and e..."
entries.text: A gathering spot for scholars and engineers, and artists to work on understanding and advancement - the betterment of their people.

entries.speaker: Mister Coventry
entries.label: Coventry: "Easy pickings for Edward Blake. No..."
entries.text: Easy pickings for Edward Blake. No doubt he and Cromwell cared very little for any knowledge held by 'primitive pagans'...

entries.text: Do I recognise your name from a London show, Miss McLeod?

entries.text: I don't do shows, but London, perhaps. I've spent a while there.

entries.text: Do you attend many, Sir?

entries.speaker: Mister Skerritt

entries.text: Only the ones that seem worthwhile. Even the odd séance or two, but never on this scale.

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod

entries.text: There just haven’t been any. That’s what I hear, anyhow. I haven’t been living more than a couple of years in London, so I could have missed something…

entries.speaker: Missus Lau

entries.text: No, no, I believe you’re right – I’ve never seen anything of the sort, and I’ve seen my fair share of London’s mystic attractions.

entries.text: I thought I might do you the favour of telling you who you’re likely to meet, Miss McLeod, while you’re here.

entries.label: Ward: ""Extracted in India from the bark o..."
entries.text: "Extracted in India from the bark of the Cinchona tree, quinine was used in 17th-century South America as a treatment for malaria and fevers. Through British trade networks, quinine became commonplace in Irish medicine as a general fever remedy. It can be purchased from chemists and apothecaries in pre-mixed tinctures and tonics, as well as in pill and powder form."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Quinine sulphate powder is often s..."
entries.text: "Quinine sulphate powder is often sold in small quantities without the need for a prescription. Due to its dreadfully bitter taste, it is recommended to mix it with water, sugar, or spirits for easier consumption."

entries.label: Ward: ""In high doses, its side effects ma..."
entries.text: "In high doses, its side effects may include dizziness, numbness, and dulling of the senses. In severe cases, it can cause nausea, confusion, and temporary blindness. Yet quinine remains the preferred option for many, as its side effects are less harmful and addictive than most opioid alternatives."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Although its distribution has been..."
entries.text: "Although its distribution has been regulated since 1868, along with opiates and arsenic-based substances, high doses of quinine can still be obtained in Ireland from local chemist shops upon presentation of a physician’s order."

entries.text: "With this, and several cities (Cork and Waterford among them) founded by Viking settlers, Munster has long had a tradition of transformative visitations."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Not least of these being the colon..."
entries.text: "Not least of these being the colonisation of the region by the English in the 16th century, a most significant venture by the Crown."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Leinster region."
entries.text: Look up the Leinster region.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The easternmost province of Irelan..."
entries.text: "The easternmost province of Ireland, Leinster was home to many Celtic Tribes, most notably the Laighin to which the province owes its name."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Vikings made their arrival to Irel..."
entries.text: "Vikings made their arrival to Ireland and by the mid-9th Century had transitioned from raiding to settling, with Dublin being their most significant settlement - serving as a major trade center and later becoming a Norse-Gaelic kingdom. This would not last, as the Vikings were later driven out by native Irish rulers."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Leinster has seen a long history o..."
entries.text: "Leinster has seen a long history of territorial battles, ranging from the arrival of Anglo-Normans in the late 12th Century - leading to the broader invasion of English forces - to a Gaelic resurgence in the middle ages, followed by the Tudors solidifying English control over Ireland by the 16th Century."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""More recently, the Cromwellian Con..."
entries.text: "More recently, the Cromwellian Conquest landed in Dublin with twelve thousand troops and travelled north to begin an assault that would later be known as the Siege of Drogheda, or the ‘Drogheda Massacre’. Its surviving rebels being transported to the overcrowded gaol of Dundalk, where they were left to starve and die. This would only be the beginning of Oliver’s devastating campaign on Irish soil."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This region housed a collection of..."
entries.text: "This region housed a collection of small Kingdoms and dynasties, with the Hill of Tara in particular, located in Mide (later named ‘Meath’), holding significant spiritual and political power as the seat of the High Kings of Ireland."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Blake Manor."
entries.text: Look up the Blake Manor.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Construction on Blake Castle began..."
entries.text: "Construction on Blake Castle began in 1652, on land awarded to the veteran soldier Edward Blake."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It was a matter of no small undert..."
entries.text: "It was a matter of no small undertaking or finance, and the work continued over generations."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It is said that the manor was buil..."
entries.text: "It is said that the manor was built on ground the local residents considered to have once been sacred, but records of this do not exist."

entries.text: Both collections of sheet music and instructions on how to play instruments are here.

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/2 - Irish History

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Nothing right now..."
entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A catalogue of events throughout Ir..."
entries.text: A catalogue of events throughout Ireland's past, studies on its people, and census data is found here.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there anything I want to look up..."
entries.text: Is there anything I want to look up?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Year of Slaughter."
entries.text: Look up the Year of Slaughter.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Tsunami of 1755."
entries.text: Look up the Tsunami of 1755.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Great Freeze."
entries.text: Look up the Great Freeze.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The first of Ireland's three famine..."
entries.text: The first of Ireland's three famines. Crop and herd damage from the Great Freeze resulted in massive shortages in milk and food.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "In the winter of 1739 a violent sto..."
entries.text: In the winter of 1739 a violent storm hit Ireland. The resultant drop in temperature was so drastic, that liquids froze indoors.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Massive earthquakes in Portugal se..."
entries.text: "Massive earthquakes in Portugal sent a tsunami north that hit the southern and western parts of Ireland."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Great Famine."
entries.text: Look up the Great Famine.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It's less than fifty years since t..."
entries.text: "It's less than fifty years since the Great Hunger that lasted from '45 to '52."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There are no official records of ho..."
entries.text: There are no official records of how cold it got but some measurements taken by enthusiasts claim it dropped as low as minus twenty degrees.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Records suggest that as high as twe..."
entries.text: Records suggest that as high as twenty percent of the then population died.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It was a higher proportion of lives..."
entries.text: It was a higher proportion of lives lost than from the Great Famine nearly a century later.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It seems to have reached as far up..."
entries.text: "It seems to have reached as far up as Connemara, where this manor is built."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Untold thousands died here from th..."
entries.text: "Untold thousands died here from the tsunami. The earthquake itself claimed the lives of over one-hundred-thousand Portuguese."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Anyone surviving something like tha..."
entries.text: Anyone surviving something like that can't but have deep scars. My own parents refused to talk of it and grew dark when it was mentioned.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A blight wiped out the potato crop..."
entries.text: "A blight wiped out the potato crops. Most of the population relied on that to survive, as the English rule exported every other resource from the country - peas, beans, rabbits, fish, honey, and more."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Ontop of this, the English Corn La..."
entries.text: "Ontop of this, the English Corn Laws blocked the import of any grain, despite the obvious need for relief."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The full loss of life from this pe..."
entries.text: "The full loss of life from this period is yet unknown, but deaths are estimated to be around one million, with another million fleeing the country on coffin ships bound for America, Canada, Australia, and more."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It is unknown how long it will take..."
entries.text: It is unknown how long it will take the country to recover.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the symbol on Miss Barbosa'..."
entries.text: Look up the symbol on Miss Barbosa's brooch >

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There's a book here on family crest..."
entries.text: There's a book here on family crests. This might have what I need.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up standing stones."
entries.text: Look up standing stones.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Standing stones, or menhir, are la..."
entries.text: "Standing stones, or menhir, are large, deliberately placed stones found around the world, but especially in Ireland."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""There is no consensus on the purpo..."
entries.text: "There is no consensus on the purpose of standing stones; there are no records detailing it, nor any surviving traditions that can be reliably traced."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""However, there are several theorie..."
entries.text: "However, there are several theories as to their purpose. Those most commonly held would posit that they marked the boundaries of territories."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Or, that they had ritual significa..."
entries.text: "Or, that they had ritual significance to old druidic religion."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Some menhir - cloch fhada in the I..."
entries.text: "Some menhir - cloch fhada in the Irish tongue - are found to be inscribed with a long-forgotten, and therefore indiscernible, language."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the O'Connor family."
entries.text: Look up the O'Connor family.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "While there are several branches of..."
entries.text: While there are several branches of the O’Connor family, a notable lineage in the Connacht Region seems to have been almost destroyed in the late 1700s.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A devoutly Catholic line, there are..."
entries.text: A devoutly Catholic line, there are indications that their covertly held belief was betrayed to the Crown, resulting in their execution.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Those remaining family members were..."
entries.text: Those remaining family members were scattered to the winds, and if any remain, their current whereabouts are unknown.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Ogham carvings."
entries.text: Look up Ogham carvings.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Keening."
entries.text: Look up Keening.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Keening, or lamenting over the dea..."
entries.text: "Keening, or lamenting over the dead, is an ancient custom practised in Ireland, with origins tracing back to Eastern nations."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Irish word for keening, "cine,..."
entries.text: "The Irish word for keening, "cine," closely resembles the Hebrew "cina," both meaning lamentation or weeping with clapping of hands."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Traditionally, Irish bards led the..."
entries.text: "Traditionally, Irish bards led the funeral songs, that addressed the deceased’s genealogy, rank, possessions, virtues and vices. But over time, hired mourners - often women - took over."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Till about the middle of the last..."
entries.text: "Till about the middle of the last century, the custom was very generally adhered to in Ireland, as well in families of the highest condition, as among those of the lower orders."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Of late years, the custom has fall..."
entries.text: "Of late years, the custom has fallen greatly into disuse, and is now of rare occurrence, except in some very few old families, and among the peasantry, and has become more of a wordless, mournful cry"

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Magdalene Asylum."
entries.text: Look up the Magdalene Asylum.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Magdalene Asylum originates from c..."
entries.text: "Magdalene Asylum originates from convent-run institutions for “fallen” women, which began in 13th-century Italy."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Mary Magdalene was an ideal symbol..."
entries.text: "Mary Magdalene was an ideal symbol for the institutions as she is often associated with repentance, devotion, and the power of grace.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A network of convents and institut..."
entries.text: "A network of convents and institutions expanded across Italy and Catholic Europe, providing secluded spaces for women seeking penance, particularly former prostitutes."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In 18th-century England, philanthr..."
entries.text: "In 18th-century England, philanthropists founded institutions like the Magdalene Hospital, adapting Catholic models to Protestant contexts for the care and rehabilitation of vulnerable women."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This was later brought to Ireland..."
entries.text: "This was later brought to Ireland by a Protestant philanthropist, Lady Arabella Denny, who founded Ireland’s first Magdalene Asylum in 1767."

entries.text: Topics such as physics, astronomy, geology, and more are stored here.

entries.text: Look up waveforms.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In physics, it is understood that..."
entries.text: "In physics, it is understood that there are some forces that move in a manner akin to, or best portrayed by, a charted wave."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This is what waveforms are; the vi..."
entries.text: "This is what waveforms are; the visual representation of a force that moves (that is, increases and decreases on some axis) periodically (over time)."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Whether this wave is a visual inte..."
entries.text: "Whether this wave is a visual interpretation of a literal wave, or a less literal, visual representation of the increase-decrease of a quality..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...is to be determined by the grap..."
entries.text: "...is to be determined by the graph itself, or failing that, any good scientist’s common sense."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Tomes on the mind and its workings...."
entries.text: Tomes on the mind and its workings. I see titles on asylums, mental disorders and phrenology alongside books on stoicism, existentialism, and nihilism.

entries.text: Look up lucid dreaming.
