entries.text: Look up dreams.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Psychologists and scientists are s..."
entries.text: "Psychologists and scientists are still trying to understand the true nature and depth of the subject but, as with any mystery, it has drawn its fair share of enthusiasts who find meaning in the symbolism involved."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Perhaps I could try this technique..."
entries.text: Perhaps I could try this technique and use the knowledge of the shared dreams as my anchor? I could use Miss Deane's journal to represent that.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Dreams are part of the sleep exper..."
entries.text: "Dreams are part of the sleep experience and act as a way to process one's experiences of that day."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""They are often abstract and someti..."
entries.text: "They are often abstract and sometimes surreal and range from pleasant to frightening."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Since dreams are mercurial and oft..."
entries.text: "Since dreams are mercurial and often soon forgotten after sleep, many people turn to lucid dreaming to better control and recall."

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/3 - World History

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Accounts from across the globe as t..."
entries.text: Accounts from across the globe as to the key events and figures throughout all recorded time.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Nothing right now..."
entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there anything I want to look up..."
entries.text: Is there anything I want to look up?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Oliver Cromwell."
entries.text: Look up Oliver Cromwell.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Instrumental in the execution of K..."
entries.text: "Instrumental in the execution of King Charles I and the brief period in which England became a commonwealth in the 1600s..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Even in his homeland, Cromwell was..."
entries.text: "Even in his homeland, Cromwell was a controversial figure, infamous for his ban on the celebration of Christmas among many such joyful activities..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...as they were thought to distrac..."
entries.text: "...as they were thought to distract from the worship of God."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""While widely disliked in England,..."
entries.text: "While widely disliked in England, his legacy in Ireland is significantly darker and more bloody."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In what became known as the "Cromw..."
entries.text: "In what became known as the "Cromwellian Conquest", Cromwell lead what amounted to a massacre across Ireland in the form of a conquest."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""He spared no quarter, going so far..."
entries.text: "He spared no quarter, going so far as to order the deaths of even those who had sheltered in churches, such as in the Siege of Drogheda."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Brazilian Revolution."
entries.text: Look up the Brazilian Revolution.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Portugal claimed control over Brazi..."
entries.text: Portugal claimed control over Brazil in 1500 and ruled it as a colony for three centuries.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "When the Portuguese royal family fl..."
entries.text: When the Portuguese royal family fled there in 1807

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Paraguay War, also known as Th..."
entries.text: "The Paraguay War, also known as The War of the Triple Alliance, lasted from 1864 to 1870."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Paraguay War."
entries.text: Look up the Paraguay War.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The results of the Uruguay War wer..."
entries.text: "The results of the Uruguay War were the cause of the conflict between Paraguay and Brazil, which led to the Paraguay War."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Paraguay was defeated in 1869 but..."
entries.text: "Paraguay was defeated in 1869 but resorted to guerrilla warfare for another 14 months, resulting in significant destruction and loss of life among both military and civilians."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In March 1870, the war concluded w..."
entries.text: "In March 1870, the war concluded with the death of Paraguayan president Francisco Solano López, leaving the country open to occupation by foreign troops."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Brazilian Naval Revolts were l..."
entries.text: "The Brazilian Naval Revolts were led by admirals Custódio José de Melo and Saldanha da Gama against President Floriano Peixoto's rule."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Brazilian Revolt."
entries.text: Look up the Brazilian Revolt.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The tensions started in November 1..."
entries.text: "The tensions started in November 1891, and resulted in a 7 month long revolt that ended on March 1894."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""With many naval ships in the hands..."
entries.text: "With many naval ships in the hands of rebels, the government resorted to forming an improved fleet called the "paper fleet" to respond."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This turmoil resulted in bloody co..."
entries.text: "This turmoil resulted in bloody conflicts across Brazil."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Mardi Gras."
entries.text: Look up Mardi Gras.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Mardi Gras, meaning "Fat Tuesday,"..."
entries.text: "Mardi Gras, meaning "Fat Tuesday," is celebrated on the day before Ash Wednesday, marking the beginning of Lent."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It has its origins in French Catho..."
entries.text: "It has its origins in French Catholic tradition and was brought to North America by the Le Moyne brothers in the late 17th century."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The tradition of having parades du..."
entries.text: "The tradition of having parades during the celebration in New Orleans started in 1853 and has been continued ever since."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Masks and costumes are often donne..."
entries.text: "Masks and costumes are often donned by the participants of the festival in celebratory colours to invoke the vibrancy of life."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Carnival."
entries.text: Look up Carnival.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Carnival is a lively celebration t..."
entries.text: "Carnival is a lively celebration that emphasizes the joy of life before the Christian season of Lent."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Unlike Mardi Gras, Carnival is not..."
entries.text: "Unlike Mardi Gras, Carnival is not limited to just one day, spanning from January to March, with festivities culminating on the Tuesday before Ash Wednesday."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The celebrations are marked by vib..."
entries.text: "The celebrations are marked by vibrant floats, elaborate costumes, and massive parades with the rhythm, participation, and style of costumes differing from region to region."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Quilombos are settlements establis..."
entries.text: "Quilombos are settlements established by escaped Afro-Brazilian slaves. Many of the settlement’s residents live in poverty"

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Quilombolas."
entries.text: Look up the Quilombolas.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""These communities originated durin..."
entries.text: "These communities originated during the 16th century in Brazil, when Afro-Brazilian slaves fled brutal conditions on sugar plantations in Brazil."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It is said that Aqualtune, an Ango..."
entries.text: "It is said that Aqualtune, an Angolan princess and general who was enslaved during a Congolese war, escaped with some of her soldiers and founded Palamares, which is one of the largest quilombos in Brazil."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Capitães-do-mato, which translates..."
entries.text: "Capitães-do-mato, which translates to Captain of the Forest, were free men, usually of limited financial means, tasked with hunting and recapturing escaped slaves in Brazil."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Captain of the Forest."
entries.text: Look up the Captain of the Forest.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Their main job was to return fugit..."
entries.text: "Their main job was to return fugitives to their masters and to destroy quilombo settlements, receiving monetary rewards in return."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Most capitães-do-mato were freed s..."
entries.text: "Most capitães-do-mato were freed slaves themselves, which put them above slaves but still low in social prestige and made them resented by captives."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Despite their authority, they were..."
entries.text: "Despite their authority, they were generally looked down upon and remained close to the social position of those they pursued."

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/8 - Religion

entries.text: Look up Gnosticism.

entries.text: Copies of the bible sit here with core texts of other faiths. It's interesting to see this so openly displayed - to some this would be blasphemous.

entries.text: "The Celtic cross is distinguished from the Latin cross by the circle, or "nimbus", around its intersection."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Its formation is attributed to Ire..."
entries.text: "Its formation is attributed to Ireland, France, and Great Britain, and it gained prominence in medieval art."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: "Its designation as the "Celtic Cross" is relatively recent, perhaps reflective of its historic use among Irish missionaries."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward

entries.text: Look up Celtic religious symbols.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""There are a number of designs syno..."
entries.text: "There are a number of designs synonymous with Celtic culture and spirituality. I list here a few."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Triskelion: Three spirals join..."
entries.text: "The Triskelion: Three spirals joined together at their outermost points and the centre of the design."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Thought to represent the physical..."
entries.text: "Thought to represent the physical world, the spirit world, and the afterlife - or alternatively, birth, life, and death."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Triquetra: An ancient symbol o..."
entries.text: "The Triquetra: An ancient symbol of a tri-pointed endless knot, now understood to represent the Holy Trinity."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Dara Knot: A complicated squar..."
entries.text: "The Dara Knot: A complicated square knot without end. Associated with Saint Patrick, patron saint of Ireland..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...the Dara Knot is a symbol of un..."
entries.text: "...the Dara Knot is a symbol of unity and peace."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward

entries.text: Look up the resurrectix.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Where a crucifix depicts Jesus Chr..."
entries.text: "Where a crucifix depicts Jesus Christ in His crucifixion, and so speaks to His sacrifice and the forgiveness bestowed upon Humanity for it..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A resurrectix is the crucifix's co..."
entries.text: "A resurrectix is the crucifix's counterpart; the cross upon which Jesus was crucified, with no depiction of the Lord upon it."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The resurrectix, then, is an empty..."
entries.text: "The resurrectix, then, is an empty cross - the Lord having departed it - and in this, it signifies hope, eternal life, and triumph over death."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Samhain."
entries.text: Look up Samhain.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Samhain, approximately pronounced..."
entries.text: "Samhain, approximately pronounced Sah-wen, is a Gaelic festival traditionally occurring on the first of November..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...towards the end of the harvest..."
entries.text: "...towards the end of the harvest season and at the beginning of winter."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Believed to be born of pagan tradi..."
entries.text: "Believed to be born of pagan tradition, the festival represents a time in the year where the boundaries between the mundane world and the Otherworld would weaken..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...and as such many traditions ass..."
entries.text: "...and as such many traditions associated with the festival are thought to be protective, to ward away the spirits that would otherwise broach the boundary and cause the living harm."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""During this time, spirits were to..."
entries.text: "During this time, spirits were to be appeased with offerings of food and drink, so that they would leave the living in peace throughout the rest of the year."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up draoi."
entries.text: Look up draoi.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The native Irish word for a tradit..."
entries.text: "The native Irish word for a traditional practitioner of magic and ritual, a draoi (pronounced dree)..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...might be considered equivalent..."
entries.text: "...might be considered equivalent to a wizard or sorcerer, perhaps one with religious prestige within their community."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""However, their nature remains the..."
entries.text: "However, their nature remains the source of speculation, as they remain a feature of antiquity."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""While the author of this book has..."
entries.text: "While the author of this book has encountered rumour of their continued existence, I was unable to verify their truthfulness."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up pagan sacred sites."
entries.text: Look up pagan sacred sites.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""While much of the knowledge of sit..."
entries.text: "While much of the knowledge of sites of religious significance to the pre-Christian pagans has been lost, there are several that have been identified across the country."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Stone circles apparently construct..."
entries.text: "Stone circles apparently constructed for ritual purpose abound, and burial sites such as those found in Newgrange suggest a reverence for the movements of the heavens."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Some old sacred sites seem to have..."
entries.text: "Some old sacred sites seem to have been co-opted into modern tradition..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...as there remains a tradition of..."
entries.text: "...as there remains a tradition of lone oak trees being best left undisturbed so as not to upset Otherworldly spirits."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A superstition which does not hold..."
entries.text: "A superstition which does not hold the same prevalence and longevity in other parts of the United Kingdom."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Nothing right now..."
entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up The Ten Commandments."
entries.text: Look up The Ten Commandments.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A list of tenets central to Judaism..."
entries.text: A list of tenets central to Judaism and Christianity.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "1. I am the Lord thy God, thou shal..."
entries.text: I am the Lord thy God, thou shalt have no other gods before me; Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; Thous shalt keep the Lord's Day holy; Honor thy father and thy mother; Thou shalt not kill; Thou shalt not commit adultery; Thou shalt not steal; Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour; Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife; Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's good.

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/12 - World Mythology

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Books on the various mythologies ac..."
entries.text: Books on the various mythologies across the world, though the focus is heavily on the classics and Egypt.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward

entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there anything I want to look up..."
entries.text: Is there anything I want to look up?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Vampires."
entries.text: Look up Vampires.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Undead humans who survive by drain..."
entries.text: "Undead humans who survive by draining the blood of the living."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A common supernatural element in m..."
entries.text: "A common supernatural element in most European cultures."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Examples include the Albanian shtr..."
entries.text: "Examples include the Albanian shtriga, Greek vrykolakas, Romanian strigoi, and Irish abhartach."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Irish abhartach was called a d..."
entries.text: "The Irish abhartach was called a dwarf for its child-like proportions."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Despite its anger and blood thirst..."
entries.text: "Despite its anger and blood thirst, its subjects were drawn to it, as if under a spell."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""They are nigh-impossible to kill,..."
entries.text: "They are nigh-impossible to kill, being vulnerable only to wood from the yew tree."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Even then, once killed it needs to..."
entries.text: "Even then, once killed it needs to be buried upside down and weighed down with a stone of such a size that it would take at least five good men to move it."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""For these reasons is said that onc..."
entries.text: "For these reasons is said that once a land is plagued by an abhartach they are never to truly be free from it; that it will return to feed on generation after generation."

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/10 - Irish Folklore

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A section on Irish folklore and gho..."
entries.text: A section on Irish folklore and ghost tales.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Nothing right now..."
entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there anything I want to look up..."
entries.text: Is there anything I want to look up?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up turnip heads."
entries.text: Look up turnip heads.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Towards the end of October and wit..."
entries.text: "Towards the end of October and with the approach of Halloween, it is not uncommon to see carved lanterns adorning doorsteps and windowsills."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In Ireland and Scotland both, ther..."
entries.text: "In Ireland and Scotland both, there is a long-held tradition of carving a face into turnips, and putting a lit candle inside them."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The tradition is thought to stem f..."
entries.text: "The tradition is thought to stem from the Irish folktale of "Stingy Jack", a spirit barred from both heaven and hell and forced to walk the earth eternally."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Whether this is true or not, these..."
entries.text: "Whether this is true or not, these carved turnips are thought to serve a practical purpose."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It is thought that on Halloween ni..."
entries.text: "It is thought that on Halloween night, the veil between life and death is thin, and spirits walk to earth - many with ill intent."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""These turnips are carved into grot..."
entries.text: "These turnips are carved into grotesque faces and lit as lanterns to ward off any spirits that would do the living harm."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the bean sídhe."
entries.text: Look up the bean sídhe.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The bean-sídhe, often Anglicized a..."
entries.text: "The bean-sídhe, often Anglicized as "banshee", is a faerie woman who portends death."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""She is often said to appear in a g..."
entries.text: "She is often said to appear in a grey cloak and a green dress, with eyes red from crying."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""To hear her keening means there wi..."
entries.text: "To hear her keening means there will soon be a death in one's life - typically on that same night - and frequently of a loved one or family member."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Aoi Sí."
entries.text: Look up the Aoi Sí.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Aoi Sí means 'People of the mound'..."
entries.text: "Aoi Sí means 'People of the mound' and covers all entities that come from the Other World."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This covers the Fae Folk, the old..."
entries.text: "This covers the Fae Folk, the old gods, and any of the other range of creatures from that place."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""For some, ghosts are also included..."
entries.text: "For some, ghosts are also included as the Other World encompasses the Irish land of the dead."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The fae themselves range in power..."
entries.text: "The fae themselves range in power from god-like, legendary figures, to the types more thought to commonly occur and roam the landscape..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...often looking to cause mischief..."
entries.text: "...often looking to cause mischief or harm, such that to invite their attention is considered bad luck."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The nature of the fae, as with hum..."
entries.text: "The nature of the fae, as with humanity’s, varies by instance, but an estimate can be made by the type of the fae in question."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Some look to cause harm; some are..."
entries.text: "Some look to cause harm; some are portents of ill-tidings, but do not seem to cause it themselves..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...and some (though these cases ar..."
entries.text: "...and some (though these cases are occasional) may even be beneficial to those encountering them."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Regardless, it is widely held that..."
entries.text: "Regardless, it is widely held that the safest course of interaction with the fae is not to interact with them at all."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Fear Gorta."
entries.text: Look up the Fear Gorta.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The fear gorta, (literally a “man..."
entries.text: "The fear gorta, (literally a “man of hunger”) is a type of apparition that is linked to the Great Famine."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""(Though there are alternate accoun..."
entries.text: "(Though there are alternate accounts that consider it an omen of further famines to come)."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Taking the form of a starving pers..."
entries.text: "Taking the form of a starving person, the fear gorta is a spirit of hunger, who will follow people to ask for food."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Should it catch its prey, it will..."
entries.text: "Should it catch its prey, it will not hesitate to consume them to satisfy its hunger."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the washer woman."
entries.text: Look up the washer woman.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The washer woman, or the bean nigh..."
entries.text: "The washer woman, or the bean nigh, is an instance of the Other Folk providing unwelcome news without exhibiting aggression or violence."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The apparition is said to appear b..."
entries.text: "The apparition is said to appear before battle, where she will be seen washing the bloody armour of those to die, as if they are already dead."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Is it said she appears at battlegr..."
entries.text: "Is it said she appears at battlegrounds as she feeds off of grief. Perhaps, this is why she shows visions of those to die?"

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Always unsuccessful in quenching i..."
entries.text: "Always unsuccessful in quenching its hunger, it then seeks out a new victim..."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Suibne."
entries.text: Look up Suibne.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Madness of Suibne tells the st..."
entries.text: "The Madness of Suibne tells the story of Suibne mac Colmain, a king of the Dál nAraidi (a region in the Northeast or Ireland), who tried to expel Bishop Ronan from church activities on his land."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Suibne eventually attempts to murd..."
entries.text: "Suibne eventually attempts to murder the Bishop and succeeds in killing the Bishop’s psalmists with a spear."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In response, Bishop Ronan cursed S..."
entries.text: "In response, Bishop Ronan cursed Suibne that he would wander the land like a bird, and second, that he would eventually die by the spear, just as he had killed the monk"

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The tale describes how Suibne wand..."
entries.text: "The tale describes how Suibne wandered the world as a madman, moving from tree to tree until he eventually dies in the very way the curse was detailed."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Throughout his mad wanderings, Sui..."
entries.text: "Throughout his mad wanderings, Suibne occasionally stops at each location to recite a poem. Some say that anyone who sees the bird or hears the poems will themselves be driven to madness."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""They are believed by the Irish to..."
entries.text: "They are believed by the Irish to live in this world, largely apart from humanity and the mundane... but not entirely."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward

entries.text: Explorations into the fields of archaeology, its changes over the past hundred years, and information on some of the biggest sites and finds in that period.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up canopic jars."
entries.text: Look up canopic jars.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Canopic jars were used in Ancient..."
entries.text: "Canopic jars were used in Ancient Egyptian burials to hold the significant major organs of the mummified person, typically decorated with images of gods."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The belief was that a person would..."
entries.text: "The belief was that a person would need the soul of their viscera in the afterlife, and the canopic jars were intended to store them until such a time."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""There would be four canopic jars p..."
entries.text: "There would be four canopic jars per mummified person; one to contain the stomach, one to contain the liver, one to contain the lungs, and one to contain the intestines."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In the later period, the once-plai..."
entries.text: "In the later period, the once-plain jars would be topped with the figure of a god, one of the four sons of Horus, each also associated with a companion goddess and a cardinal direction."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up Vase of Nectanebo."
entries.text: Look up Vase of Nectanebo.

title: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/9 - Spiritualism and Ghost Sightings

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A mix of guides on spiritual matter..."
entries.text: A mix of guides on spiritual matters, guides for making contact, and a record of, supposedly real, encounters with the afterlife.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Nothing right now..."
entries.text: Nothing right now...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Is there anything I want to look up..."
entries.text: Is there anything I want to look up?

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Second Sight."
entries.text: Look up the Second Sight.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Second Sight is a skill posses..."
entries.text: "The Second Sight is a skill possessed by some that allows them to know of the future, or events far from them they should rightly have no knowledge of."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up tarot cards."
entries.text: Look up tarot cards.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Originally a type of card deck use..."
entries.text: "Originally a type of card deck used for various Italian games, the tarot card was later adopted by the French for use in divination, or "cartomancy"."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This being a publication unconcern..."
entries.text: "This being a publication unconcerned with such mundane issues as simple card games, we will disregard the traditional use for its magical cousin."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A tarot deck consists of seventy-e..."
entries.text: "A tarot deck consists of seventy-eight cards and two Arcana, the twenty-one Major Arcana being "face cards", and the Minor Arcana being suits."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The Minor Arcana is divided into f..."
entries.text: "The Minor Arcana is divided into four suits (Wands, Swords, Cups, and Coins) and consists of cards of numbers one to ten, and four court cards."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Each Major Arcana has specific mea..."
entries.text: "Each Major Arcana has specific meaning, as does every suit and its cards therein; and every card has another meaning again if drawn in the reversed position."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Tarot cards are to be drawn one by..."
entries.text: "Tarot cards are to be drawn one by one in formation, and read with consideration of their individual meaning and their position in the draw."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""They are typically consulted in ma..."
entries.text: "They are typically consulted in matters of love and fortune, but can be asked a great many things - and, in general, are favoured for their versatility."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up séances."
entries.text: Look up séances.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A séance is a ritual used to speak..."
entries.text: "A séance is a ritual used to speak with the dead, typically hosted by a spirit medium, but attended and aided by a number of guests."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A spirit is called upon by the med..."
entries.text: "A spirit is called upon by the medium, and asked questions. It will answer them through physical means, such as moving a glass on a board..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...through audible means, such as..."
entries.text: "...through audible means, such as knocking, or, if one is so lucky, by the possession of one of those at the table."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In this case, the spirit is freque..."
entries.text: "In this case, the spirit is frequently able to articulate itself better, although some may find it to be a distressing sight."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Séances are typically used by stil..."
entries.text: "Séances are typically used by still-living loved ones to speak to those they have lost, or to divine secrets known only to the dead."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In Scotland, it is thought to run..."
entries.text: "In Scotland, it is thought to run in families, especially those in the highlands, and while the information gleaned through this mystic sense can be useful, it can also be harrowing."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It can also refer to the ability t..."
entries.text: "It can also refer to the ability to see the dead."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Sight alone does not mean understa..."
entries.text: "Sight alone does not mean understanding, nor can dark visions of the future necessarily be averted, though those with the Sight are often compelled to try."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up ghosts."
entries.text: Look up ghosts.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""There is much debate over the true..."
entries.text: "There is much debate over the true nature of ghosts - even their existence in the first place! - but there are two major prevailing theories."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""The first is that a ghost is a rem..."
entries.text: "The first is that a ghost is a remnant of a person - a soul that, for whatever reason, has not passed on."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This sort of ghost is typically at..."
entries.text: "This sort of ghost is typically attributed to the need for some desire of the soul - or the person it was - to be sated, be it revenge, ambition, or love."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In a similar vein, they frequently..."
entries.text: "In a similar vein, they frequently cling to some object or place of importance, unable to complete whatever business holds them there in their new state."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A secondary, less discussed - but..."
entries.text: "A secondary, less discussed - but widely credited - theory of the cause of apparitions is the manifestation of emotion or trauma."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In this theory, it is thought that..."
entries.text: "In this theory, it is thought that human beings are capable of imparting such emotion that it forever affects the location that witnesses it."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In these cases, it is not the spir..."
entries.text: "In these cases, it is not the spirit itself that haunts a place, but the event - typically a harrowing death - imprinting itself upon a space."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""These theories are not exclusive,..."
entries.text: "These theories are not exclusive, and could very well exist alongside each other. Such is the prevalence of spirits that it seems unlikely both are not true."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Society for Psychical R..."
entries.text: Look up the Society for Psychical Research.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Established in London, 1882, the So..."
entries.text: Established in London, 1882, the Society for Psychical Research endeavours to investigate psychical matters and occurrences...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Without prejudice or prepossession..."
entries.text: "Without prejudice or prepossession of any kind, and in the same spirit of exact and unimpassioned enquiry."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It publishes a regular journal and..."
entries.text: It publishes a regular journal and intermittent studies as to the society's findings, and its membership includes both "believers" and sceptics.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up the Hermetic Order of the G..."
entries.text: Look up the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""To the layperson, not much is know..."
entries.text: "To the layperson, not much is known about the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (henceforth "the Golden Dawn")."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""It is a secret magical society, fo..."
entries.text: "It is a secret magical society, founded in England, although it is rumoured to have further branches."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Reportedly, the Golden Dawn's focu..."
entries.text: "Reportedly, the Golden Dawn's focus is on divine magic and spiritual development, though the specifics of this are unknown."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Despite the Golden Dawn's enigmati..."
entries.text: "Despite the Golden Dawn's enigmatic nature, its members may be recognised by its symbol..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""A Latin cross with a rose in its c..."
entries.text: "A Latin cross with a rose in its centre, and a pentagram and several alchemical symbols on each arm."

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up mystics."
entries.text: Look up mystics.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""There exist among us certain peopl..."
entries.text: "There exist among us certain people predisposed to sensing and invoking the ebb and flow of the spiritual world and its denizens."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""These people, often called mystics..."
entries.text: "These people, often called mystics – as indeed I will refer to them here! – possess a unique capability."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""They are able to sense the superna..."
entries.text: "They are able to sense the supernatural and Otherworldly and in doing so provide means of communication with it, often using themselves as the go-between."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""This is most commonly achieved by..."
entries.text: "This is most commonly achieved by invoking a trance or otherwise altered state through spell, prayer, or ritual..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""...and inviting either a spirit, a..."
entries.text: "...and inviting either a spirit, a higher power, or a denizen from another world to speak through them."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "… though uncommonly encountered, an..."
entries.text: … though uncommonly encountered, an ancient binding ritual forged the creation of a particular rune used for the purpose of that binding and that alone.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A spiral with four intersecting lin..."
entries.text: A spiral with four intersecting lines (one at the top, three at the bottom) is thought to represent a gateway to the Otherworld...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...the bound gods’ blood, and the t..."
entries.text: ...the bound gods’ blood, and the three human clans who bound them, this symbol being used by the Milesians to seal off the Otherworld.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up occult orders."
entries.text: Look up occult orders.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "There are any number of occult orde..."
entries.text: There are any number of occult orders, some better known than others.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "It is truly impossible to know quit..."
entries.text: It is truly impossible to know quite how many there are, as many hold a tradition of secrecy.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Those at least deigning to let thei..."
entries.text: Those at least deigning to let their existence be known include the Freemasons and the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn…

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "But truth be told there may be many..."
entries.text: But truth be told there may be many more than are known, either through secrecy or relative informality.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Certainly, initially informal group..."
entries.text: Certainly, initially informal groups that may gather for rites or rituals such as séances have a tendency to take such form, once the anteed are sufficiently fervent.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up ritual markings."
entries.text: Look up ritual markings.

entries.speaker: Detective Ward
entries.label: Decision: "Look up fetters."
entries.text: Look up fetters.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""‘Soul trapping’, or the unwillful..."
entries.text: "‘Soul trapping’, or the unwillful binding of souls to inanimate objects, is a phenomenon that has been recorded throughout history and across the known world. One such instance occurred during an expedition to Egypt conducted by Lord Thomas Blake of Doon. A number of what locals termed ‘soul jars’ were unearthed near a tomb and were brought to Dublin by Lord Blake for further examination."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""In a drunken stupor, Lord Blake’s..."
entries.text: "In a drunken stupor, Lord Blake’s young apprentice Harry Arnold cracked his skull on an ancient tablet in Blake’s office and died almost immediately."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Lord Blake, upon hearing the lad’s..."
entries.text: "Lord Blake, upon hearing the lad’s anguished screams, ran to the office to find his apprentice’s lifeless corpse bleeding out on the bench. The screams, he soon realised, were coming from one of the soul jars and, to quell the wailing, Blake ordered that the jars be destroyed."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Elsewhere in the world, there are..."
entries.text: "Elsewhere in the world, there are stories of the souls of the recently departed being tied to objects of strong emotional significance. These objects, known as ‘fetters’, can take any form; fetters as small as a needle and as large as a carriage have been documented across the world."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: ""Some spiritualists theorise that e..."
entries.text: "Some spiritualists theorise that even entire buildings or areas of land can, under specific circumstances, become fetters, though no evidence of such a phenomenon has been found thus far. Others disagree with this assertion; they argue that the force of emotion needed to tie souls to something as large as a building or as intangible as an area of land would be, frankly, inhuman."

title: Ground floor/Bar/Eavesdrop Cathal and D'Arcy

entries.text: What are you thinking about?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Hm? Thinking - do you - sorry, did..."
entries.text: Hm? Thinking - do you - sorry, did you mean me?

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy

entries.text: Who else would I be talking to?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Oh, I don't know. I just thought......"
entries.text: Oh, I don't know. I just thought... I wasn't thinking of much.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Nonsense. I'm no mind reader, but I..."
entries.text: Nonsense. I'm no mind reader, but I know when a man has something on his mind. Now, what could it be...?

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Angels - that's your thing, isn't i..."
entries.text: Angels - that's your thing, isn't it? That's what I've heard. Go on and tell me about these angels, then.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Don't let me bore you with that. We..."
entries.text: Don't let me bore you with that. We could talk about something else.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Not at all! This way, I get to go h..."
entries.text: Not at all! This way, I get to go home and tell my friends about how I spoke to a boy who speaks with angels, which is just excellent! Do go ahead.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "How did you find out you could do i..."
entries.text: How did you find out you could do it in the first place?

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Oh, I nearly died."
entries.text: Oh, I nearly died.

entries.speaker: Missus D'Arcy
entries.label: DArcy: "Go on..."
entries.text: Go on...

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "Hah. A horse riding accident, just..."
entries.text: Hah. A horse riding accident, just over a year ago. You know how it is, the horse spooks, and there's only so much you can do.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "I don't remember much of what happe..."
entries.text: I don't remember much of what happened after I fell. Not what was around me, anyway. Just the most... revolting pain in my side and my leg.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "And the idea that I was going to di..."
entries.text: And the idea that I was going to die. I can't say it seemed clear, because nothing was, but it did seem very certain.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "And then I saw... I still don't kno..."
entries.text: And then I saw... I still don't know how to describe what it looked like. But behind all that was happening around me, I saw it - a thing that I instinctively knew was an angel.

entries.speaker: Mister O'Meara
entries.label: Cathal: "My companions got me to a doctor -..."

entries.text: If I don’t go to the séance now, I’ll miss it... and I have a feeling that somehow that would be a very bad idea.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/door beside Doyle, ch1

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "You almost have it, Sir. Room 4."
entries.text: You almost have it, Sir. Room 4.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/room plan examine

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A map of the upper floor. This shou..."
entries.text: A map of the upper floor. This should be useful for placing which guest is located where.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/portrait of Lady W Blake

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A portrait of a woman with dark hai..."
entries.text: A portrait of a woman with dark hair. She is holding an ornate vase that looks to be... Egyptian? That's curious.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The plaque reads "Lady Wilhelmina B..."
entries.text: The plaque reads "Lady Wilhelmina Blake".

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "This must be the same vase Miss His..."
entries.text: This must be the same vase Miss Hisham is so interested in. I doubt there is more than one of this sort among the Blake household...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "So she did indeed have the vase in..."
entries.text: So she did indeed have the vase in her possession. But where is it now?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "This was the vase Miss Hisham sough..."
entries.text: This was the vase Miss Hisham sought. We destroyed it, breaking its curse.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Walter blake portrait

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The plaque tells me this is Walter..."
entries.text: The plaque tells me this is Walter Blake, the Marquess' only child.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/look at device

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "A strange contraption."
entries.text: A strange contraption.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I wonder what its function is? What..."
entries.text: I wonder what its function is? What is it measuring?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "This does seem to be reacting to th..."
entries.text: This does seem to be reacting to the guests' choices in relation to the séance. I still have no idea why, though.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The second light is now off."
entries.text: The second light is now off.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The gauge is almost empty and the t..."
entries.text: The gauge is almost empty and the third light has gone off.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The gauge is empty and all lights a..."
entries.text: The gauge is empty and all lights are off.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The gauge is no longer full and the..."
entries.text: The gauge is no longer full and the first light has gone out.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I saw this happen when Mister Touss..."
entries.text: I saw this happen when Mister Toussaint decided not to go to the séance.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I wonder, can I get it to decrease..."
entries.text: I wonder, can I get it to decrease again by convincing another guest to avoid the event?

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/first device drop

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That gauge decreased and a light we..."
entries.text: That gauge decreased and a light went out as soon as Mister Toussaint decided he was no longer attending the séance...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "What exactly is that device monitor..."
entries.text: What exactly is that device monitoring and why?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Maybe I should convince another gue..."
entries.text: Maybe I should convince another guest to avoid the event and see if this occurs again...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I was right - the gauge decreases a..."
entries.text: I was right - the gauge decreases as people's plans for the séance change.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "I am still unsure of the device's p..."
entries.text: I am still unsure of the device's purpose but my gut says I want this as decreased as possible by the séance...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The second light has gone out. I wo..."
entries.text: The second light has gone out. I wonder what effect that will have on the séance...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "The third light is gone now, too. W..."
entries.text: The third light is gone now, too. What thresholds do the lights measure?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That's all the lights out. What doe..."
entries.text: That's all the lights out. What does that mean for the séance, I wonder?

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/ward after carmela flyer cutscene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...Her? Who could she be talking ab..."
entries.text: ...Her? Who could she be talking about? And what does that bible verse mean?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Clearly, someone in this hotel has..."
entries.text: Clearly, someone in this hotel has bad blood with Miss Mantovani. She thinks it's a woman - could it even be Miss Deane?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And that knife... Something tells m..."
entries.text: And that knife... Something tells me they're not likely to stop at threats.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti Catches You

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "...Wandering into people's rooms li..."
entries.text: ...Wandering into people's rooms like a wayward child is going to get you into trouble, Monsieur Ward.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That is rich, all things considered..."
entries.text: That is rich, all things considered.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Ah, but I do not care whose room yo..."
entries.text: Ah, but I do not care whose room you break into, Monsieur - as long as it is not mine.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti kicks you out

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Monsieur Ward... I warned you. You..."
entries.text: Monsieur Ward... I warned you. You know what must come next, Oui?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "...You're serious, aren't you? Isn'..."
entries.text: ...You're serious, aren't you? Isn't this just a bit hypocritical?

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Come now. Let us go inform the mana..."
entries.text: Come now. Let us go inform the manager of your good work among his guests...

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Perhaps. But, more importantly, it..."
entries.text: Perhaps. But, more importantly, it is sensible.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "Does all this not bore you?"
entries.text: Does all this not bore you?

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "Should it? It's fascinating, in a w..."
entries.text: Should it? It's fascinating, in a way. Lots of case studies, certainly.

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "It's nothing like your usual sort o..."
entries.text: It's nothing like your usual sort of thing...

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "Oh, it's not at all scientific, but..."
entries.text: Oh, it's not at all scientific, but... Look, you're talking to a woman with a shrine in her room. I'm not entirely clinical.

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "Besides - look at you! Ivy, I said..."
entries.text: Besides - look at you! Ivy, I said I would come with you! Do you expect me to regret it?

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "I suppose... I just thought, what w..."
entries.text: I suppose... I just thought, what with how things are...

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "You're always the first one to know..."
entries.text: You're always the first one to know when my temper's run short. Do you suppose I've managed to hide it from you, of all people?

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "Besides - you know I would take any..."
entries.text: Besides - you know I would take any excuse to spend my time with you.

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "Oh - good grief, but I... you are a..."
entries.text: Oh - good grief, but I... you are always so sweet.

entries.speaker: Missus Lau
entries.label: Lan Fen: "...Don't look away like that. Every..."
entries.text: ...Don't look away like that. Everything will be alright.

entries.speaker: Miss McLeod
entries.label: Ivy: "No, no, I just... Maybe it will. I..."
entries.text: No, no, I just... Maybe it will. I don't know. Maybe.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Ah. Mister Ward. Our final attendee..."
entries.text: Ah. Mister Ward. Our final attendee.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "My apologies. I was delayed in gett..."
entries.text: My apologies. I was delayed in getting ready.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Of course, Sir. There is no need to..."
entries.text: Of course, Sir. There is no need to excuse your time to us.

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "You've no idea, Sir!"
entries.text: You've no idea, Sir!

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "This is, however, a masked ball, Si..."
entries.text: This is, however, a masked ball, Sir. If you have not brought your own, we can provide one.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Please. I seem to be underdressed."
entries.text: Please. I seem to be underdressed.

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Sorry, Mister Varley, Sir. Not my p..."
entries.text: Sorry, Mister Varley, Sir. Not my place.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Hhhmmm..."
entries.text: Hhhmmm...

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Anyways. Here's your mask, Sir, and..."
entries.text: Anyways. Here's your mask, Sir, and some champagne for the toast.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "You may go on through, Sir. I'm sur..."
entries.text: You may go on through, Sir. I'm sure the others are eager for your arrival...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "My thanks..."
entries.text: My thanks...

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "I understand it might not be of aca..."
entries.text: I understand it might not be of academic concern to you, but you must see what allowing her attendance does to the event's credibility.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I'm not about to turn out a guest b..."
entries.text: I'm not about to turn out a guest based on hearsay, Mister Toussaint.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I'm afraid whatever issue you have..."
entries.text: I'm afraid whatever issue you have with Missus Erickson, it's between yourself and her. I'm not going to intervene.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "You misunderstand; I am not asking..."
entries.text: You misunderstand; I am not asking you to intervene. I am telling you that she is not what she seems.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "And consequently that so long as sh..."
entries.text: And consequently that so long as she is in attendance, the entire event is in question. That can't be acceptable, surely?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "The specifics of the event are not..."
entries.text: The specifics of the event are not up to me, Mister Toussaint. I just manage the hotel.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "If a guest has paid their way and i..."
entries.text: If a guest has paid their way and is not causing trouble, then I have no more to say on the matter.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Oh, for... Fine, fine. I understand..."
entries.text: Oh, for... Fine, fine. I understand.

entries.speaker: Mister Toussaint
entries.label: Ettiene: "Good day, Monsieur."
entries.text: Good day, Monsieur.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I suspect there is something to be..."
entries.text: I suspect there is something to be learned about our fortunes here. If only I could have gotten to it before it was cleaned up...

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "Why?"
entries.text: Why?

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "Aye, well, I suppose some folks her..."
entries.text: Aye, well, I suppose some folks here have never gutted a bird to read its entrails before.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "Is that... some kind of Irish sayin..."
entries.text: Is that... some kind of Irish saying?

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "No?"
entries.text: No?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "Oh. Well.  You'll excuse me then..."
entries.text:
Oh. Well. 
You'll excuse me then.

entries.speaker: Mister Ó Finn
entries.label: OFinn: "No. No use for one. Druidry is an o..."
entries.text: No. No use for one. Druidry is an oral tradition, so I never got much into the writing. Ogham has served me grand for my purposes - do you want my chisel?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "Eh... No... I was planning on takin..."
entries.text: Eh... No... I was planning on taking some notes.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I'm sorry Sir, but do you have a pe..."
entries.text: I'm sorry Sir, but do you have a pen I can borrow?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I want to go downstairs and examine..."
entries.text: I want to go downstairs and examine the energy left by that poor bird before breakfast.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Mister Ó Finn doesn't write and I d..."
entries.text: Mister Ó Finn doesn't write and I didn't see his name on the sign-in book - he must be the person who marked his name with an X. I'll make a note of that.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Missus Erickson, we need to talk."
entries.text: Missus Erickson, we need to talk.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "This had best not be about my perso..."
entries.text: This had best not be about my personal affairs again. Why don't you do us both a favour, Mister Ward, and stop interfering?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "What could you, of all people, poss..."
entries.text: What could you, of all people, possibly have to say to me?

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "That's not a bad point. Perhaps you..."
entries.text: That's not a bad point. Perhaps you'll be more interested in what Mister Toussaint has to say.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Shall we go to your room, then? Or..."
entries.text: Shall we go to your room, then? Or would you rather discuss this in the open?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "...Yes. My room, Sir."
entries.text: ...Yes. My room, Sir.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "So, you've read the notes and under..."
entries.text: So, you've read the notes and understand your situation?

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "He is right... I'm a damned fool..."
entries.text: He is right... I'm a damned fool...

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "But he wins. I forsake this ritual...."
entries.text: But he wins. I forsake this ritual. And I forsake this séance. I have no want to see others enjoying what I will never have.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Whether you face eternal damnation,..."
entries.text: Whether you face eternal damnation, now, is a point of debate - you have assumed that is linked to this magical nullness you have. You may well be wrong...

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "But if you do this, then you are lo..."
entries.text: But if you do this, then you are locking yourself onto that path.

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "And Mister Toussaint will ensure yo..."
entries.text: And Mister Toussaint will ensure your remaining days will not be easy - magic or no.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I wanted so much to be special, to..."
entries.text: I wanted so much to be special, to have what the others have.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "But now you have taken that hope fr..."
entries.text: But now you have taken that hope from me. Maybe you will have saved my soul, but even now I think I'd pay that price for a taste of that.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "If he wasn't going to rob my chance..."
entries.text: If he wasn't going to rob my chance to use and appreciate it.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I would curse you both if I didn't..."
entries.text: I would curse you both if I didn't know there would be no venom in my bite.

entries.speaker: Missus Erickson
entries.label: Hazel: "I hope they see their ghost and mor..."
entries.text: I hope they see their ghost and more. So much more.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Please, Missus Joyce, you must list..."
entries.text: Please, Missus Joyce, you must listen! You are clearly in pain today.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "...No. No, get away from me, witch!..."
entries.text: ...No. No, get away from me, witch! I'll not hear it, not from you.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "I said I'll not hear it! Rather my..."
entries.text: I said I'll not hear it! Rather my joints suffer the cold than your... your... corruption!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "What is this corruption of yours?..."
entries.text: What is this corruption of yours?  I simply see you need rest.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Now, my room is big and grand - and..."
entries.text: Now, my room is big and grand - and a horror to clean, I am sure. You were there an hour on Friday!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "That is an hour best spent at rest...."
entries.text: That is an hour best spent at rest. It is needed, and I am more than capable.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "I... You... you mean to say that-"
entries.text: I... You... you mean to say that-

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Why would you... No one's ever..."
entries.text: Why would you... No one's ever...

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "N-No. No! Idle hands make the devil..."
entries.text: N-No. No! Idle hands make the devil's work. Now please, please, leave me be!

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh no, Miss. I'm fine. Thank you."
entries.text: Oh no, Miss. I'm fine. Thank you.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Please, Missus Joyce, I beg of you..."
entries.text: Please, Missus Joyce, I beg of you to listen.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Please now, Miss Mantovani. I said..."
entries.text: Please now, Miss Mantovani. I said I am fine.

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "But I do not need the cards to see..."
entries.text: But I do not need the cards to see how much you carry. You need rest.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "I said I'll not hear it! I'd rather..."
entries.text: I said I'll not hear it! I'd rather my joints suffer the cold than your... your... corruption, witch!

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "You're... very kind. But no. This o..."
entries.text: You're... very kind. But no. This old place won't keep itself and I want everything ready for the séance.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "You all deserve that."
entries.text: You all deserve that.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Have you seen Darragh? He's meant t..."
entries.text: Have you seen Darragh? He's meant to have been helping me move some supplies into the basement all morning.

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "But once the delivery arrived he's..."
entries.text: But once the delivery arrived he's buggered off somewhere.

entries.speaker: Miss Murphy
entries.label: Saoirse: "Maybe? This event is bringing out a..."
entries.text: Maybe? This event is bringing out all sorts of strange behaviour in people.

entries.speaker: Miss Murphy
entries.label: Saoirse: "I don't... Maybe, the service in th..."
entries.text: I don't... Maybe, the service in the church?

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Oh he's holy all of a sudden, is he..."
entries.text: Oh he's holy all of a sudden, is he?

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "..."

entries.speaker: Miss Murphy
entries.label: Saoirse: "Thanks for the concern, Seamus."
entries.text: Thanks for the concern, Seamus.

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Ah whatever. I better get back to t..."
entries.text: Ah whatever. I better get back to the stables. Can't leave the basement door just sitting open like that.

entries.speaker: Mister Doyle
entries.label: Doyle: "Look. Whatever she got you into, ju..."
entries.text: Look. Whatever she got you into, just... be careful.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Do you have the master key for the..."
entries.text: Do you have the master key for the south east corridor?

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh no, Mister Varley. I only had th..."
entries.text: Oh no, Mister Varley. I only had the atrium master key with me today.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Might Mister Hunter have it?"
entries.text: Might Mister Hunter have it?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Thank you, no. One of the guests ha..."
entries.text: Thank you, no. One of the guests has lost her key and I was hoping I could use this to get her back in.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "No, I was just out in the stables...."
entries.text: No, I was just out in the stables. He has the north west corridor locked away in his safe there.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Mister Doyle's key privileges have..."
entries.text: Mister Doyle's key privileges have been revoked.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh, I forgot he locked the southwes..."
entries.text: Oh, I forgot he locked the southwest key in the basement storage. Has he not gotten that out yet?

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "I don't suppose Mister Doyle had it..."
entries.text: I don't suppose Mister Doyle had it?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Thank you, no. I'm just doing my we..."
entries.text: Thank you, no. I'm just doing my weekly audit.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "I can fetch it for you? It's only o..."
entries.text: I can fetch it for you? It's only on the room cart in the supply closet.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "What? What in the heavens was he do..."
entries.text: What? What in the heavens was he doing in there?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "No. He claims he can't find a way t..."
entries.text: No. He claims he can't find a way through. But I am telling you what I told Mister Hunter - do not do it for him.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "And that is not all - the fool also..."
entries.text: And that is not all - the fool also lost the north east corridor master in... one of the unassigned rooms...

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I do not know, but I doubt it was c..."
entries.text: I do not know, but I doubt it was cleaning. When you have time, perhaps you would see if you can find it. And clean up anything he's done.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "Oh, Mister Varley. I've had it up t..."
entries.text: Oh, Mister Varley. I've had it up to here with that boy. I'll get to it as soon as I'm done with my morning chores.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Missus Joyce?"
entries.text: Missus Joyce?

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I appreciate that."
entries.text: I appreciate that.

entries.speaker: Missus Joyce
entries.label: Caitlin: "..."

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "I would also appreciate some decoru..."
entries.text: I would also appreciate some decorum with Miss Mantovani. She is the Marquess' guest and the host of this séance, which you know is important to the future of this manor.

entries.speaker: Mister Varley
entries.label: Varley: "Once this whole business is done, s..."
entries.text: Once this whole business is done, she and the rest of the guests will be moving on. It is only a few days decency, Missus Joyce.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/after key note

entries.speaker: Mister Ward
entries.label: Ward: "Useful information to have. I've ma..."
entries.text: Useful information to have. I've made a note of it.

title: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Please..."
entries.text: Please...

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "You think this is the first time I..."
entries.text: You think this is the first time I have had scripture nailed to my door?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "And Leviticus 20:27?"
entries.text: And Leviticus 20:27?

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "This is not even original!"
entries.text: This is not even original!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "Hah!"
entries.text: Hah!

entries.speaker: Miss Mantovani
entries.label: Carmela: "It's her isn't it? Oh, she must be..."
